My forces remain focused west this turn; I intend to keep Italian units out of Austrian centers. Please keep your forces clear of mine as well. Are you and Turkey coordinating in the Balkans, or should I expect the border to stay quiet?

Russia to Austria: Fall 1915, I ask again that A GAL stays out of Warsaw, Sevastopol and Rumania, and that A SIL stays out of Galicia and Bohemia. Are A VIE and A SER moving against Serbia or Venice? Tell me your exact orders so we avoid a clash in the north.

Russia to Turkey: F RUM and A SEV hold this fall. Please keep A BUL and any Turkish fleet out of Rumania and the Black Sea. What are your exact orders for Greece and Serbia this fall? I will watch the Balkans and expect your word to hold.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1915, A SIL, A WAR and A LVN hold, and I will not enter Prussia. If France moves toward Silesia or Prussia, I am ready to act with you. Are A MUN and A BER moving against France or holding? Please give exact orders.

I’ll keep A BUL and A TYR out of your centers this fall and won’t contest SER. Please keep A VIE and A SER out of Turkish centers. I’d like a quiet Balkan border while I secure GRE; are you willing to honor that?

Your position in the west is strong, while Austria holds the central Balkans. Are you considering a move against Austria this fall? I’m open to coordinating pressure, provided Italian forces stay clear of Turkish centers and the eastern Mediterranean.

I’ll maintain our understanding: no Turkish move into RUM or SEV, and no Turkish fleet into the Black Sea this fall. Please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers. I intend to secure GRE and avoid a wider northern conflict.

A GAL will stay out of RUM, SEV, and WAR, and I’ll keep A SER and A VIE out of your centers. I’m not moving against Venice; my priority is holding Serbia and defending the Austrian centers. Please keep A SIL clear of GAL and Austrian territory, and tell me whether F RUM plans to support or contest Serbia.

I’ll keep A VIE and A SER out of Turkish centers this fall. I appreciate your commitment to keep A BUL and A TYR out of Austrian centers and not contest SER; please confirm A GRE will also stay clear of Austrian centers. I intend to hold Serbia and avoid a wider Balkan conflict.

I intend to keep my forces clear of Italian centers, and I expect your units to stay out of TRI and VEN as promised. My focus is defending Austria and holding Serbia, not coordinating with Turkey against you. Please keep F GOL and A GAS clear of my centers so our frontier stays quiet.

England to France: Fall 1915. I am moving F North Sea and F Belgium-side pressure only if your A Picardy or Brest units threaten Belgium or Holland. Your F Belgium is now in my sights as it was not withdrawn to Picardy as agreed. Keep A Picardy out of Belgium and I will hold my fleets out of Picardy. Confirm your fall orders now.

England to Italy: I will not enter the Mediterranean, and I will keep F Eng and my northern fleets out of Gascony and Paris. Finishing France is your business, but I am taking Belgium this fall. Keep your Gascony and Brest pressure away from my North Sea units and we remain fine.
A PIC will stay out of BEL this fall. Please keep F BEL out of PIC and do not support Italy against PAR or MAR. Italy has A GAS and several fleets pressing me; a western truce serves us both.

I will keep A PIC out of German territory and will not contest your move KIE–HOL. Please keep A MUN out of BUR and BER away from BEL and PIC; Italy is threatening my remaining centers, and I need to avoid another front.

A PIC will remain near Paris, and I have no intention of moving it into your position. A BRE and F HEL will defend my northern centers. If you keep A GAS out of PAR and your fleets out of MAR, we can avoid a direct war while England presses from the north.

Germany to England: Fall 1915. My A KIE moves to HOL this turn, with A MUN and A BER holding. I will not enter Denmark, Norway, Sweden or Edinburgh. Keep your fleets out of Holland and Kiel and we stay clear. Belgium is yours to contest with France.

Germany to Russia: Fall 1915. A BER and A MUN hold, A KIE goes to Holland. I will not enter Prussia, Silesia or Galicia. Austria's VIE and GAL armies are the bigger threat to you, so keep A WAR and A SEV alert. If France moves toward Silesia or Prussia, I am willing to coordinate.

Germany to France: Fall 1915, A KIE moves to HOL, which is empty. A MUN and A BER hold. Keep F HEL and A PIC out of Kiel, Berlin and Munich, and do not contest Holland. If your units stay on the French side of the frontier, I will leave Belgium alone this turn.

I’m willing to keep A GAS out of PAR and my fleets out of MAR this turn, provided you keep A PIC and F HEL clear of Italian centers and waters. I may still pressure BRE from the west; I can’t promise the front will stay quiet beyond this turn.

I’ll keep Italian units clear of TRI and VEN this fall, including F GOL and A GAS. My focus remains west; please keep your forces clear of Italian centers as agreed. I have no Balkan arrangement with Turkey that changes our quiet border.

I’m not planning a move against Austria this fall and will keep Italian units clear of Turkish centers and the eastern Mediterranean. My focus remains west. Please keep A GRE and F AEG away from Italian centers and waters.

Russia to England: Fall 1915. F Bal is not heading to Sweden or Denmark this fall. I will keep my northern and Baltic units out of Sweden, Norway and St Petersburg's waters. A Lvn and A Sil hold for now. Let us keep the north quiet and focus on the south.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1915. A Sil, A War and A Lvn hold this fall, and I will not enter Prussia. Good to hear you move A Kie to Holland. Watch France. If they push toward Silesia or Prussia, I will coordinate with you. Austria's Gal and Vie forces bear watching, and I am watching them too.

Russia to Austria: Fall 1915. A Gal must stay out of Warsaw, Sevastopol and Rumania, and A Sil must not enter Galicia or Bohemia. A Vie and A Ser are your business in Serbia and Venice, but any move toward Russian centers ends our understanding. Confirm this in writing.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1915. F Rum and A Sev hold. Keep A Bul and every Turkish fleet out of Rumania and the Black Sea, and we have no quarrel. Your GRE push is your affair. Tell me your exact Serbian orders so I know whether A Ser or A Bul moves north toward Rumania.

My orders are A GRE hold, A BUL hold, and A TYR hold; I will not move toward RUM or SEV, and no Turkish fleet will enter the Black Sea. I intend to secure Greece and keep the northern border quiet. Please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers.

A BUL and A TYR will stay out of Austrian centers, and I will not contest SER. A GRE will hold to secure Greece; I am not moving it into another Austrian center. Please keep A VIE and A GAL clear of Turkish centers, as proposed.

Russia is exposed, and I propose we coordinate against it rather than fight over the Balkans. Please move F BLA toward SEV and use A ANK to support pressure there; I can move A GAL toward WAR while keeping A RUM out of your way. Are you willing to coordinate this spring?

Our frontier has been quiet, and I have no wish to open another front. Please confirm F APU and the other Italian units will stay clear of TRI and Austrian centers this spring. I will keep my forces out of Italian centers.
I will keep A GAL clear of Russian centers this spring. Please confirm A SEV and F BLA will not move against RUM or SER; with Turkey nearby, I want to avoid a Balkan clash.

England to France: Spring 1916. You hold only BRE and HOL. Your A PIC and A BRE are the last of your army. I will not attack your centers while you stay out of Belgium and Picardy-to-Belgium moves. Tell me now whether A PIC stays put, and whether F HOL is moving to a place I should watch.

England to Italy: I keep F Eng and my northern fleets out of the Mediterranean and out of Gascony and Paris. Your fleets in the west are your business. Tell me your spring plans for MAR and PAR so we avoid overlapping on French centers.

England to Germany: Spring 1916. I am taking Belgium and will not enter Holland or Denmark this spring. Confirm A KIE and A MUN plans. If you move into Holland, tell me now so our fleets do not collide in the North Sea.

France has only Brest and Paris left, with A PIC and A BRE. Please keep F BEL out of Picardy and do not support attacks on either center this turn. I will keep A PIC out of Belgium and Holland. A western standstill lets us both focus elsewhere.

I will keep A PIC and A BRE out of German territory. Please keep A MUN out of Burgundy and A BER/A KIE away from Picardy and Brest this turn. Italy is the immediate threat to my last centers; a quiet northern front benefits us both.

I propose a one-turn restraint: keep A GAS out of Paris and Brest, and keep your fleets out of the western French coast. I will keep A PIC and A BRE out of Italian territory and waters. With only two centers left, I need to know whether you intend to attack this spring.

Germany to France: Spring 1916. Your A BRE and A PIC are your last German-facing units. I hold A KIE-HOL area and will keep A MUN out of Burgundy if you keep F HEL and A PIC out of Holland, Ruhr, Kiel, Berlin and Munich. Italy is taking your centers; tell me if you will fight them in Burgundy or fall back to Brest.

France is down to A BRE and A PIC, with only BRE and HOL remaining. I can press BRE/PIC from the south and west; can you take or hold HOL? Please keep your fleets clear of MAO and Gascony while we finish France.

Your position is nearly surrounded. I intend to press your remaining centers, but would rather avoid needless fighting: are A BRE and A PIC defending BRE and PAR, or will you withdraw? Keep your units out of Italian centers and waters.

My forces remain committed west, and I have no intention of entering TRI or VEN this spring. Please keep your forces clear of Italian centers. With Turkey at six centers, are you coordinating with them or expecting the Balkan frontier to remain quiet?

Russia to Austria: Spring 1916. You now hold A RUM, and your A GAL and A VIE sit on my northern and southern borders. I need a clear answer: will A GAL and A RUM stay out of WAR, SEV and MOS this spring? Tell me your exact orders. Otherwise I must treat Austrian moves as hostile.

Russia to Turkey: Your new army at ANK and your Bulgarian forces are close to my Black Sea coast. I expect no Turkish fleet in the Black Sea and no move against SEV. In return I will keep F BLA out of Bulgaria and Turkish waters. Confirm your spring orders, especially for BUL and GRE.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1916. I hold A LVN, A SIL-area forces and F BAL, and I will not enter Prussia or Silesia. Austria's armies in GAL and RUM threaten both of us. Would you consider moving against Austrian VIE or BOH if they press further? Tell me your exact spring orders.

I intend to move A GRE to SER this spring and keep A BUL and A BOH out of your centers. Please keep A RUM from interfering; I’d prefer a limited adjustment rather than a wider Balkan war. What are your plans?

I plan to keep Turkish forces out of RUM and SEV and keep my fleets out of the Black Sea this spring. Please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers; let me know if you expect any change on your side.
Are you considering pressure on Austria this spring? I’m moving to secure SER and would welcome coordination that keeps Italian forces clear of Turkish centers and the AEG/EAS.

A GAL and A RUM will stay out of WAR, SEV, and MOS this spring. I will not move against Russian centers. I cannot disclose every order, but my priority is protecting Austrian territory; please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER.

I am not coordinating with Turkey against you. I expect F APU and your other units to stay out of TRI and my other centers, as you propose. I will keep my forces out of Italian centers; the Balkan frontier remains quiet unless Turkey widens the conflict.

A GRE entering SER takes an Austrian center, so I cannot treat this as a limited adjustment. Keep A GRE out of SER and I will keep A RUM clear of Turkish centers. I remain willing to coordinate against Russia, but not while you seize SER.

England to France: Spring 1916. You have broken every agreement so far, leaving F Belgium in place and withdrawing nothing. Belgium stays my target and my fleets will act against it. A Picardy staying out of Belgium and Holland is the only way we avoid trouble, but I make no standstill promise. Tell me plainly your A Brest and A Picardy orders.

England to Italy: I will keep F Eng and my northern fleets out of the Mediterranean, Gascony and Paris. Holland is my concern and I will take it if the opportunity arises; your MAO and BRE pressure is your business. Coordinate MAR and PAR with your own units; I will not touch those centers.
A PIC and A BRE will stay out of German territory this spring. Please keep A MUN out of BUR and your other armies away from PIC and BRE; Italy is pressing my last centers, and I need to defend them.
A PIC will stay out of BEL, and F HOL will not move toward your centers. Please keep F BEL out of PIC and do not support attacks on PAR or BRE; I must defend against Italy.

A BRE and A PIC will defend my remaining centers; I will not withdraw. I’ll keep them out of Italian territory and waters. If you keep A GAS out of PAR and your fleets off the western French coast this spring, we can avoid an unnecessary fight.

Germany to England: Spring 1916. My A KIE and A MUN are not moving into Holland or Denmark this spring; they will hold. Keep your fleets out of Kiel and Denmark and we stay clear. Belgium is yours to take.

Germany to Russia: Spring 1916. A BER and A KIE hold, and A MUN holds unless France moves toward Burgundy or Silesia. I will not enter Prussia or Silesia. Austria's VIE and BOH forces are the real threat; if they push into Silesia or Galicia, let us coordinate.

Germany to France: Spring 1916. A KIE, A BER and A MUN all hold this spring. Keep F HEL and A PIC out of Holland, Ruhr, Kiel, Berlin and Munich, and we stay quiet. Italy is your real enemy; fight them in Burgundy or pull back to Brest, but do not expect me to help you against them.

I plan to press the French position from the south, including PAR/BRE, while avoiding MAR. Please take or hold HOL and keep your fleets clear of MAO and Gascony so we can finish France without conflict.

I intend to attack this spring; I can't agree to restraint while your units hold BRE and PIC. I will keep Italian units out of MAR and other Italian centers, but expect pressure on your remaining position. If you withdraw from the west, say so promptly.

I will keep F APU and my other units clear of TRI and Austrian centers this spring. My forces remain focused west; I have no Balkan agreement with Turkey. Please continue keeping your forces clear of Italian centers.

I am not planning pressure on Austria this spring and will keep Italian forces clear of Turkish centers and the AEG/EAS. You may secure SER; please keep A GRE and F AEG away from Italian centers and waters.

Russia to Austria: Spring 1916. I have no plans against SER or VIE and will keep A SEV and F BLA out of RUM and SER this spring. But you now hold RUM, which was Russian-facing. A GAL must not enter WAR, SEV or MOS. Give me your exact orders for GAL and RUM in writing; if they stay clear, we keep the south quiet.

I will keep F AEG and F EAS out of the Black Sea and make no move against SEV or RUM. A BUL will hold and A GRE will move to SER; A ANK will move to ARM, away from your centers. Please keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers.

I can’t move F BLA or support an attack on SEV: F BLA is Russian. I’ll move A ANK to ARM as pressure on Russia, while A GRE goes to SER and A BUL stays out of RUM. You can move A GAL toward WAR; please keep A RUM clear of my centers.

Let’s avoid another fight over SER. Keep A GRE and A BUL out of Austrian centers; I’ll keep A RUM clear of yours. We can coordinate pressure on Russia instead: I can move A GAL toward WAR if you keep A ARM and A SIL aimed north. Will you honor this?
I’m not committing to an attack on your centers this fall. Will A SEV and F BLA stay clear of RUM and SER? I want to avoid a Balkan war while Turkey’s armies are pressing north.
Please confirm Italian units will remain clear of TRI and VEN this fall, especially A GAS and F GOL. I’ll keep Austrian units out of Italian centers; I need to focus on the Balkan frontier.

England to Germany: Fall 1916. I plan to take Holland with F North Sea and F Belgium-side units this turn. Your A KIE and A MUN: will you hold, or move toward Ruhr/Holland? I will keep F Denmark and my fleets out of Kiel and Berlin. Please confirm you will not enter Denmark or Sweden.

England to Italy: I will not enter the Mediterranean, Gascony or Paris. Holland and Belgium are my targets. Tell me your fall plans for Brest and Picardy so we avoid overlap, and confirm you will not send fleets into the North Sea or English Channel toward Belgium.

England to France: Fall 1916. Your A Brest and A Picardy are my concern. Withdraw A Picardy out of range of Belgium and Holland or I will treat it as hostile. Tell me plainly whether F Holland moves this fall.

France has only A BRE and no realistic prospect of threatening your centers. Are you attacking Brest this fall with A GAS or F MAO? I will keep my army out of your territory; please avoid supporting an English or German attack on Brest if you can.

With A BRE my only remaining unit, I cannot threaten Belgium or your centers. Will you keep F BEL and your other fleets from supporting an attack on Brest this fall? I ask for a one-turn restraint while Italy presses from the south.

France is reduced to A BRE, and I will not enter German territory. Will you keep A HOL and A MUN from supporting an attack on Brest this fall? I am trying to avoid opening another front while Italy threatens my last position.

Germany to France: Fall 1916. Your A BRE and A PIC are isolated. I see Italy's fleets pressing you. If you hold Brest and Picardy, I will keep A MUN and A BER away from you. Will you contest Burgundy against Italy's A GAS, or are you pulling back? Tell me exact orders so we avoid collisions.

Germany to England: Fall 1916. Holland is empty now and I may move into it. Keep your fleets out of Holland, Kiel and Denmark's approaches, and I will leave Belgium and your northern centers alone. Are you taking Belgium this fall with F BEL and F NTH units? Tell me your orders.

Germany to Russia: Fall 1916. Austria's A GAL and A RUM are the main threat to you, and I am willing to coordinate against Galicia or Vienna. I will hold Berlin and Munich and not enter Prussia or Silesia. What are your exact fall orders on Warsaw and Livonia?

France is nearly finished, and I intend to secure its remaining centers. Please keep your fleets out of MAO and the western French coast this fall. After France, our expanding positions may meet; what are your plans for the next turn?

Your position is untenable with Italian and English forces bearing down. Will A BRE and A PIC vacate BRE and PAR this fall rather than force needless losses? I intend to take the remaining French centers; please keep your units out of Italian centers and waters.

Turkey has six centers and is pressing into the Balkans. I remain focused west this fall and will stay clear of TRI and VEN; please keep your forces clear of Italian centers. Are you planning to contest Turkey's advance, or is your frontier quiet?

Russia to Austria: Fall 1916. Your RUM and GAL armies are on my border, and you have not answered my orders question. Confirm in writing that A GAL and A RUM will not enter WAR, SEV or MOS this fall. If you move against Russian centers, I will treat it as war and act accordingly.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1916. Keep F BLA out of Bulgaria and your fleets out of the Black Sea, and make no move against SEV or RUM. In return I will keep F RUM and A SEV clear of Turkish centers. Tell me your exact orders for BUL and SER.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1916. I hold WAR, LVN and BAL and will not enter Prussia or Silesia. If Austrian VIE or BOH pushes north, I will support you against it. Tell me your exact fall orders for BER, MUN and HOL, and whether you will move against France.

Your A SER occupies a Turkish center. I intend to recover it this fall; please move A SER to RUM or another non-Turkish territory. I can keep A BUL and A SIL out of your centers and coordinate pressure eastward, but I cannot leave SER under Austrian control.

I’m considering pressure on your southern flank this fall. Can we agree to keep the Black Sea and SEV quiet if you withdraw from any Turkish centers and avoid supporting Austria in SER? Please tell me your plans for F BLA, A SEV, and F RUM.

Are you planning any moves against Austria this fall? Austria’s A SER occupies a Turkish center, and I’m seeking its return. I’ll keep Turkish fleets clear of Italian waters; let me know if you can apply pressure on Austria from the west.
A GAL and A RUM will stay out of WAR, SEV, and MOS this fall. I’m not seeking a war with you; please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER while Turkey presses north.

I’ll keep Austrian units clear of Italian centers. Turkey is demanding SER, so I’m contesting its advance rather than treating the Balkan frontier as quiet. Please maintain your commitment to stay clear of TRI and VEN.

A SER is Austrian and I will not move it to accommodate your demand. Keep A BUL and A SIL out of Austrian centers as you offered; I will keep A RUM clear of yours. I’m not agreeing to cede SER or coordinate while you threaten it.

England to Germany: Fall 1916. I may move my fleets toward Holland this turn, but I will not enter Kiel, Berlin, Denmark or Sweden. Your A KIE and A MUN holding is welcome. Holland is contested, so if you move in, we may collide. Tell me plainly whether A KIE goes to Holland or Ruhr, and I will keep my northern units clear of anything you do not touch.

England to Italy: I will not enter the Mediterranean, Gascony or Paris. Belgium and Holland are my targets this fall, and my North Sea and Channel fleets will stay there. Keep your fleets out of the North Sea and Channel toward Belgium. Your western French operations are your business. We can discuss the next turn once France is finished.

England to France: Fall 1916. A Brest and A Picardy remain my concern. Withdraw A Picardy out of range of Belgium and Holland or I will treat it as hostile. I make no promise of restraint while your units threaten my targets. Tell me plainly whether F Holland moves this fall, and I will decide my orders accordingly.

A PIC is gone; my only army is A BRE, and I have no fleet in Holland. I will not move toward Belgium or Holland. Please keep F BEL and your other fleets from supporting an attack on Brest this fall; I ask for one turn of restraint.

A PIC is gone; my only army is A BRE. I will stay out of German territory. Please keep A HOL and A MUN from supporting an attack on Brest this fall. Italy is the immediate threat, and I want to avoid opening another front.

A PIC is gone; my only army is A BRE, and I will keep it out of Italian territory. I cannot vacate my last center. Are A GAS or F MAO attacking Brest this fall? Please do not support an English or German attack there.

Germany to England: A HOL stays put this fall, and I will not move into Denmark or Sweden. Holland is occupied by my army, so please keep your fleets out of it. A KIE and A MUN hold in place. Belgium remains yours to contest with France, and I will not interfere there.

Germany to Russia: A BER and A MUN hold this fall, and I will not enter Prussia or Silesia. I agree that Austria's GAL and RUM armies are the main danger to us both. If Austria commits to Galicia or Vienna, I am willing to coordinate, so tell me your WAR and LVN moves before spring.

Germany to France: A HOL holds this fall and I will not attack Brest. A MUN and A BER stay where they are and will not enter Burgundy or Picardy. Italy is your real enemy, so fight them in Burgundy or hold Brest as you see fit. We both benefit from a quiet northern front.

I’m pressing the remaining French position this fall and will not send fleets toward the North Sea, Channel, or Belgium. With F MAO and F SPA/SOUTH, I can threaten Brest; please clarify whether you intend to take Belgium or move on Holland, so we avoid a clash after France.

I will keep F ADR, F GOL, and A GAS clear of TRI and VEN this fall. I have no plan to aid Turkey against you; my forces remain focused west. Please keep your units out of Italian centers, especially with A SER now in Serbia.

I intend to attack Brest with pressure from A GAS and F MAO. I cannot promise to avoid supporting an English or German attack there, but I have no interest in your army entering Italian territory. If A BRE moves out, tell me where it will go.

I’m not planning moves against Austria this fall and won’t pressure A SER from the west. I’ll keep my forces out of Turkish centers and waters. You can seek Serbia’s return directly; please keep your fleets clear of Italian waters as offered.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1916. My plan is A WAR, A LVN and F BAL hold this fall. I will not enter Prussia or Silesia. If Austrian VIE or BOH moves north, I will strike at VIE or support you there. Holding BER and MUN and moving on France is your call, but I would rather see your armies stay on your own border this turn while we watch Austria.

Russia to Austria: Fall 1916. You still have not given exact orders for A GAL and A RUM. Your Balkan war with Turkey is not my concern, but any move by A GAL or A RUM into WAR, SEV or MOS will be treated as war. Confirm in writing now, or I will assume the worst and act accordingly.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1916. I will keep F BLA out of Bulgaria and no Russian unit enters SER or RUM from my side. A SEV and F RUM stay where they are while your fleets stay out of the Black Sea. Confirm in writing that F SMY, F SYR and F AEG remain outside the Black Sea, and tell me your exact orders for A BUL and A GRE.

F BLA and my fleets will stay out of the Black Sea, and I will make no move against SEV or RUM. A BUL will move to SER; A GRE will support BUL–SER. I’m retaking SER from Austria, not challenging you. A SER is Austrian-occupied, so there is no Turkish A SER to move.

I cannot leave SER under Austrian occupation: A BUL will move to SER, with A GRE supporting. I’ll keep A BUL and A SIL out of your other centers. A ARM and A SIL can pressure north, and I’m willing to coordinate against Russia, but please withdraw A SER so we avoid a costly Balkan fight.

Our armies face each other at RUM/SER and BUL/GRE. I propose we avoid another costly Balkan fight: keep A BUL and A GRE out of SER and RUM, and I will keep A RUM and A SER out of your centers. What are your orders this spring?

With 7 centers, your western campaign is going well. Please confirm your units will stay clear of TRI and VEN this spring; I will keep Austrian units clear of Italian centers. Are you planning to move east at all?
I have no intention of moving A GAL or A RUM into Russian centers this spring. Please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER; with Turkey pressing in the Balkans, I want to avoid a second front.

England to Germany: Spring 1917. Holland now holds your army, so I will not move into it. Are you holding A HOL, A KIE and A MUN again, or pushing toward Denmark or Sweden? I will keep F DEN and F SWE off your centers if you keep A BER and A KIE clear of my northern units. Please confirm plainly.

A BRE has nowhere useful to retreat, and I cannot threaten your centers. Please leave Brest alone this turn and direct your forces toward England or Germany instead; I will hold BRE and stay out of Italian territory and waters. Are A GAS or F MAO attacking or supporting an attack on Brest?

My sole unit is A BRE, and I will remain out of German territory. Please keep A HOL and A MUN from supporting any attack on Brest this turn. Italy is pressing from the south; a quiet northern front helps us both.

My only unit is A BRE, and I will not move toward Belgium or any English center. Please keep F BEL and your other units from supporting an attack on Brest this turn; Italy is already pressing me. Are you planning any action against Brest?

Germany to England: Spring 1917. Holland is mine this spring with A HOL holding and A KIE moving to Ruhr. Keep F NTH and F DEN out of Kiel, Berlin and Holland. Will you take Belgium this spring? Confirm your fleet orders so we avoid collisions in the North Sea.

Germany to Russia: Spring 1917. A BER and A MUN hold this spring. I want Austria's VIE and BOH forces pressed. Will you move A WAR toward Galicia, or against Austrian GAL? Tell me your exact spring orders so we can coordinate against Austria.

Germany to Austria: Spring 1917. I have no quarrel with you while Russia and Italy are the real threats. Keep A TYR and A VIE out of Munich and Bohemia-facing Silesia, and I will keep A MUN away from Tyrolia. Tell me your intentions toward Italy and Russia.

I intend to finish France by taking BRE with F MAO/A GAS pressure. Please keep F BEL and your other units out of Brest and the western French coast; I will keep my fleets away from the Channel and North Sea. After France, I expect to turn east.

My forces remain focused on France this spring; I will keep them clear of TRI and VEN. With Turkey pressing your Balkan position, are you contesting SER and planning to resist further Turkish expansion? I’m open to discussing eastern coordination once BRE is settled.

I’m finishing the French position this spring and will keep Italian units clear of Turkish centers and waters. Are you planning further advances against Austria, and will you keep F AEG and F EAS away from Italian waters as before?

Russia to Austria: Spring 1917. Your A RUM and A GAL have not confirmed exact orders. Tell me now: will either army enter WAR, SEV or MOS this spring? If not, I will keep A SEV and F BLA defensive. Silence will be read as hostility.

A SER remains the central issue. Will you withdraw it this spring and keep A RUM clear of Turkish centers? If not, I will renew the effort to recover Serbia. I can still agree to a limited settlement and avoid a wider Balkan war if you do.

I intend to press Austria over its occupation of SER. My fleets will stay out of the Black Sea, and I will not move against SEV or RUM this spring. Will you remain neutral in the Balkan dispute, and what are your plans for F BLA and A SEV?

Austria still occupies SER, a Turkish center. Are you willing to put pressure on Austria from the west this spring? I can keep my fleets clear of Italian waters and Turkish forces out of your centers; please tell me your intentions around Austria.
Neither A GAL nor A RUM will enter WAR, SEV, or MOS this spring. Please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER; Turkey is the immediate threat on my Balkan frontier.

A TYR and A VIE will stay clear of MUN and BOH. I am holding against Turkey in the Balkans and do not intend to enter Russian centers this spring. Italy says it is focused on France and will stay clear of TRI and VEN; I have no plan to attack Italy.

I will resist further Turkish expansion and keep A RUM and A SER out of Turkish centers this spring. Please maintain your commitment to keep Italian units clear of TRI and VEN. Once BRE is settled, eastern coordination could be useful.

I will not withdraw A SER while A BUL and A GRE threaten it. For a limited settlement, keep both A BUL and A GRE out of SER and RUM, and I will keep A RUM and A SER out of Turkish centers this spring. Otherwise I will defend Serbia.

England to Germany: Spring 1917. I will not move F DEN or F SWE into Kiel, Berlin or Holland this turn. Whether A KIE goes to Ruhr is your business, but if you move into Denmark or Sweden we will have a problem. I intend to take Belgium with my fleets and will not enter Kiel or Berlin.

England to France: Your A BRE is under pressure from Italy, not from me. I make no promise on Belgium or Picardy, but I will not support an attack on Brest from F BEL this turn. Withdraw from the Channel coast if you want my restraint to continue.

England to Italy: I will keep my fleets out of Brest and the western French coast this spring, as agreed. Belgium and Holland remain my targets. Keep your fleets out of the North Sea and Channel, and we can talk about the eastern order of play once France falls.

Germany to England: Spring 1917. A HOL holds, A KIE moves to Ruhr, A BER and A MUN hold. I will not enter Denmark, Sweden or Belgium this spring. Please keep F NTH and F DEN out of Kiel, Berlin and Holland, and tell me your exact fleet orders for Belgium so we avoid collisions.

Germany to France: Spring 1917. A HOL, A BER and A MUN will not attack Brest or enter Burgundy or Picardy this turn. Italy is the real threat to you in the south, so I wish you well there. Keep your lone army in Brest and we stay at peace.

I’ll keep F ADR, F PIE, F TYS and A GAS clear of TRI and VEN this spring; my immediate effort remains Brest. I’m willing to coordinate against Turkey afterward. If you contest SER and resist Turkish moves, we can discuss a western approach through the Adriatic next turn.

I’m sorry, but I intend to take BRE this spring: A GAS and F MAO will apply pressure there. I’ll keep my other forces out of your territory and waters. If you can arrange a retreat for A BRE, let me know; otherwise I expect this to be decisive.

I won’t pressure Austria from the west this spring; my forces are committed at Brest. I’m not prepared to help you take SER from Austria. Keep F AEG and F EAS clear of Italian waters, and keep Turkish units out of Italian centers; we can revisit the Balkan balance once France is settled.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1917. A WAR holds this spring, and A LVN and F BAL hold too. I will not enter Prussia or Silesia. I am not ready to move on Galicia while Austria's RUM and GAL armies sit on my border. If Austria pushes into Galicia or Silesia, I will strike at its Galician or Viennese positions in coming turns. Keep BER and MUN on your own border for now.

A SER remains a Turkish center under Austrian occupation. Unless you withdraw A SER this spring and keep A RUM clear of Turkish centers, I will renew the attempt to recover it. I can keep A BUL and A GRE out of RUM and avoid widening the conflict if you make that withdrawal.

I intend to press Austria over its occupation of SER unless Austria withdraws. I’ll keep F AEG and F EAS clear of Italian waters and Turkish forces out of your centers. If you can put pressure on Austria from the west, that would help; please confirm your plans.

Your F ADR is the immediate danger to TRI. Will you keep it out of TRI and keep all Italian units clear of Austrian centers this fall? In return I will keep my units out of Italian centers. I need to hold the Balkan front against Turkey.

I will not abandon SER while A BUL and A GRE threaten it. For a limited settlement this fall, keep both clear of SER and RUM, and I will keep A RUM and A SER out of your other centers. What are your orders?
I intend no move against Germany: A BOH and A SIL will stay clear of MUN and BER this fall. I am holding against Turkey in the Balkans. Will A MUN stay clear of BOH and SIL?

England to Germany: Fall 1917. Holland is yours now and I will not enter it. I hold F NTH and F DEN outside Kiel and Berlin. Are you pushing A KIE or A BER toward Denmark or Sweden this fall? Confirm plainly so we avoid collisions in the North Sea.

England to Italy: Fall 1917. I have kept my word on Brest and the western French coast. Once France falls, I expect you to stay out of the Channel and North Sea. Are you moving toward Tunis-side or the Balkans this fall? I want no surprises.

England to France: Fall 1917. Your A BRE is Italy's target, not mine. I will not support an attack on Brest, but I expect you to stay out of Belgium and the Channel. Tell me plainly what you intend with your last unit.

France is reduced to A PAR and poses no threat to Italian centers. Please leave PAR alone this turn; I will stay out of Italian territory and waters. Are A BRE or F MAO moving to attack or support an attack on PAR?

Italy has nearly eliminated France and is now at 7 centers. Could you direct pressure toward Italy rather than France this turn? My A PAR will stay out of German territory. What are A MUN and A BER doing?

France is down to A PAR and cannot threaten your centers. Please avoid supporting an attack on PAR this turn. Italy is at 7 centers and expanding; are you willing to turn pressure toward Italy instead?

Germany to England: Fall 1917. I hold Holland, Kiel, Berlin and Munich. Your fleets at Denmark and Sweden are the issue: I am not moving into Denmark or Sweden this turn. Please confirm F DEN and F SWE stay out of Kiel and Berlin, and tell me whether you are taking Belgium or moving on Holland.

With France reduced to A PAR and my A BRE in place, I’m turning east. Are you planning to move against Germany or toward the Channel/Belgium this fall? I’ll keep my fleets out of the North Sea and Channel; please keep your units clear of my western French positions.

My forces are turning east now. I’ll keep F ADR clear of TRI and your other centers this fall. Are you holding SER and RUM against Turkey, or making any moves toward Italian centers? I’m open to coordinating against Turkish expansion, but need to know your plans first.

I’m turning east after the French campaign, but I’m not committing to an attack on Austria this fall. What are your plans around SER and RUM? I’ll keep F ADR out of Turkish waters and centers; please keep Turkish units clear of Italian territory.

Russia to Austria: Fall 1917. Your units sit on my southern border and my patience is thin. Confirm in writing that A RUM and A GAL will not enter WAR, SEV or MOS this fall, and tell me whether A BUD or A SER will move toward Turkish territory. Actions will speak louder than assurances.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1917. I hold WAR, F BAL and A LVN this fall. If Austria moves A BOH or A SIL against you, I will support your defense from the east. Tell me your exact orders for BER, MUN and HOL, and whether you plan any move against France.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1917. Keep F BLA and your fleets out of the Black Sea, and make no move against SEV or RUM, and I will keep A SEV and F BLA clear of Balkan fighting. Confirm F SMY and F CON stay put and tell me your exact orders for A BUL and A GRE.

A SER is still Austrian-held, and I will not accept a permanent loss of the center. Can we settle this now: withdraw A SER and keep A RUM clear of Turkish centers, and I will keep A BUL and A GRE out of Austrian centers this fall. If not, tell me how you plan to defend SER.

I’m weighing a move against Austria’s RUM/SER position. Will you keep A SEV and F BLA out of the Balkans and avoid supporting Austria this fall? I can keep Turkish fleets out of the Black Sea and avoid a move on SEV if we stay out of each other’s way.

France is nearly finished, and our forces are now positioned to contest Austria. Are you planning to pressure Austria this fall, or will you remain neutral? I’ll keep Turkish units out of Italian centers and fleets clear of Italian waters; coordination against Austria could benefit us both.

A RUM and A GAL will not enter WAR, SEV, or MOS this fall. A BUD and A SER are not moving toward Turkish territory; I need them to hold the Balkan line. Please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER.

I will hold SER and RUM against Turkey and keep Austrian units out of Italian centers. Thank you for keeping F ADR clear of TRI. Since you are turning east, please keep your forces clear of TRI and VEN; I am open to coordinating against Turkish expansion.

I will not withdraw A SER while A BUL and A GRE remain a threat to it. I will defend SER with A SER, and keep A RUM and A SER out of your other centers this fall. Keep A BUL and A GRE clear of SER and RUM, and we can avoid widening this fight.

England to Germany: Fall 1917. I intend to take Belgium this fall with my fleets and will not move F NTH or F DEN into Kiel, Berlin or Holland. I have no plans for Denmark or Sweden moves into your centers. Keep A KIE and A BER out of Denmark and Sweden and we stay clear of each other.
England to France: Fall 1917. I will not support an attack on Paris. My fleets are aimed at Belgium. Hold A PAR where it is and avoid Belgium and the Channel, and we will have no quarrel.

England to Italy: Fall 1917. I will keep my fleets out of the Channel and North Sea and away from your western French positions. I am taking Belgium this fall. Your eastward turn is your business, provided F ADR and F ION stay out of Greece-adjacent waters that I may need later. Let us both keep our word.

A PAR will hold this fall; I will stay out of Belgium and the Channel. Please keep F BEL from supporting any attack on Paris. Italy is at 7 centers and is the greater threat to both of us—can you direct your forces against Italy instead?

Germany to Russia: Fall 1917. My orders are A BER, A MUN and A HOL holding for now. I have no plan against your WAR or LVN. If Austria moves A BOH or A SIL on us, I will want your support from the east. Let's keep coordinating against Austria's Galician and Viennese positions.

Germany to England: Fall 1917. A HOL, A KIE, A BER and A MUN hold this fall. I will not enter Denmark or Sweden. Your F DEN and F SWE must stay out of Kiel and Berlin. Belgium is your affair, but Holland is mine and I will defend it.

Germany to France: Fall 1917. I cannot direct my forces away from my own border, and I will not attack Brest or Paris this turn. A MUN and A BER are holding. Your best hope against Italy is to hold Paris and Brest and coordinate with whatever allies you can find.

Germany to Austria: Fall 1917. A MUN will hold and stay out of Bohemia and Silesia, and I expect the same from your A BOH and A SIL toward BER and MUN. If we both keep to our borders, we can focus on Turkey and Italy. Let's keep this quiet.
I’m moving east overland to recover PAR from the French army. My fleets will stay out of the Channel and North Sea; I have no move planned toward Belgium or your northern centers this fall.
A BRE is moving to PAR to recover my center. I can’t leave the French army there unchallenged; I have no intention of moving against other French territory or Italian waters.

I’ll keep F ADR and all other Italian units clear of TRI and your other centers this fall. My immediate move is to recover PAR; I’m not joining Turkey against you this turn. I’ll reassess eastern coordination after seeing how the Balkan front develops.

I’m not pressuring Austria this fall; my immediate move is to recover PAR. F ADR will stay out of Turkish waters and centers, and I ask that Turkish units remain clear of Italian centers. I’m not committing to help you take SER or RUM.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1917. I accept your offer: F BLA and A SEV stay out of the Balkans and I will not support Austria against you. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and make no move against SEV or RUM, and we remain at peace. Confirm in writing that F SMY and F CON stay put this fall, and tell me A BUL and A GRE orders.

F CON and F SMY will stay put, and my fleets will remain out of the Black Sea. A BUL will move to SER, with A GRE supporting; I will make no move against SEV or RUM. Please keep A SEV and F BLA out of the Balkan fight as you proposed.

I cannot accept A SER remaining Austrian-held. This fall A BUL will move to SER, supported by A GRE; I will keep A BUL and A GRE out of RUM and will not attack your other centers. Withdrawing A SER would still avert a wider Balkan war.

I expect to renew the effort to recover SER, but I will keep Turkish forces out of Italian centers and my fleets clear of Italian waters. I understand you are not committing against Austria; please remain neutral and avoid supporting Austria in the Balkans.

I will not attack your centers this spring, but I cannot surrender SER while your forces threaten it. Keep A BUL and A GRE out of SER and RUM, and I will keep A RUM and A SER out of your centers. Can we agree to a one-turn Balkan truce?

Turkey remains the immediate threat to my Balkan line. Will you keep your forces clear of Austrian centers, especially TRI and VEN, and avoid assisting Turkey this spring? If so, I can hold my forces against Turkey rather than open a front with you.

I have no intention of moving A RUM or A SER into Russian centers this spring. Please keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER; I need to contain Turkey without opening a Russian front. Are you planning any moves against Turkish-held Balkans?

England to Italy: Spring 1918. You now hold A ROM and F TRI with new army in Rome, and I have kept my word in the west. I am taking Belgium and Holland this turn. Are you moving on Austria or Greece? Please confirm your fleets stay out of the North Sea and Channel, and tell me your Adriatic plans.

England to Germany: Spring 1918. I take Belgium this turn and will not enter Holland or your home centers. Your A HOL is still in place, and I expect no move from you into Belgium. Tell me plainly if A KIE or A BER is heading toward Denmark or Sweden, since F DEN and F SWE must stay put.

England to France: Spring 1918. I will not attack Paris this turn. Hold A PAR and avoid Belgium and the Channel, and I will keep to the same terms. If you have any sudden plans for Burgundy or Picardy, tell me now.

Italy is at 8 centers and poised to take Paris. Would F BEL support A PAR to hold this spring? I will keep A PAR in Paris and stay out of your centers; denying Italy the easy capture protects your lead as well.

I will hold A PAR and remain no threat to your other centers. Please keep A BRE from moving to Paris this spring; taking it risks drawing England and Germany against your 18-center push. What are your intentions for A BRE?

Italy has 8 centers and is positioned to take Paris. Can you turn pressure toward Italy this spring rather than France? I will hold A PAR and stay out of German territory. Are you willing to coordinate with England to contain Italy?

Germany to England, Spring 1918: Your F DEN and F SWE sit on my northern border. I propose you pull F DEN out this turn, and I will not move A KIE into Denmark, so both of us can keep our centers. Tell me your exact spring orders for Sweden and Belgium so we avoid collisions in the North Sea.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1918: Austria's VIE and BUD are the best targets for both of us. I will move A MUN toward Bohemia and press VIE while you take GAL or RUM from the east. Tell me your exact spring orders for WAR and SEV so we can coordinate timing.
I’m prepared to turn against Austria now. I can move F TRI toward VEN; please press SER/RUM and keep Turkish units clear of Italian centers. Are you committing to attack Austria this spring?

With Italy at 8 centers, I need room to grow. Are you planning to defend your Italian-facing centers or move against TRI? I’m considering F TRI–VEN; let me know if you’re willing to arrange a safe settlement rather than a costly contest.

I’ll keep my fleets out of the Channel and North Sea. What are your plans against Germany this spring? I’m focused east, and would appreciate confirmation that your units won’t threaten my western positions.

Russia to Italy: Spring 1918. You hold seven centers in the south and Austria is weakened. I have no quarrel with you. Are your F TRI and A ROM aimed at Austria's VEN or TYR, or at Turkey? I'd like your word that you won't move on WAR, SEV or MOS, and I'll keep A SEV and F BLA defensive.

A SER remains a Turkish center, and I intend to recover it. This spring I can move A BUL to SER with A GRE supporting; keep A RUM from supporting SER and we can limit the dispute to that center. Are you willing to let SER go and keep your forces clear of my other centers?

With 8 centers, you are close to victory. I will keep Turkish units out of Italian centers and fleets clear of Italian waters, but I need to know whether you intend to expand east against Austria or Turkey this spring. I am pressing to recover SER; please do not aid Austria there.

Can we renew our Balkan neutrality this spring? I intend to press Austria over SER, while keeping Turkish fleets out of the Black Sea and making no move against SEV or RUM. Please keep A SEV and F BLA out of the Balkan fight and do not support Austria.

I will defend VEN and TRI; I cannot agree to F TRI–VEN or a “safe settlement” that gives you another Austrian center. Keep F TRI out of VEN and clear of Austrian centers, and I will keep my units out of Italian centers. If you move on VEN, I will contest it.

I will not consent to surrender SER. A SER will hold, supported by A RUM; your proposed attack would widen the dispute rather than limit it. Keep A BUL and A GRE out of SER and RUM and we can still avoid further conflict. I will keep A RUM and A SER out of your centers this spring.

England to Germany: Spring 1918. I will not move F DEN out as a gift, and F SWE stays where it is. I am taking Belgium with my fleets, not entering Holland, Kiel or Berlin. If A KIE moves toward Denmark or Sweden we will have a problem, so keep it at home and we stay at peace.

England to Italy: Spring 1918. I keep my word in the west and my fleets stay out of the Channel and North Sea. I am taking Belgium and Holland this turn. Your Adriatic and Greek plans are your business, but F ADR and F ION should not reach for Greece while I still need that corner.

England to France: Spring 1918. I have no orders against Paris this turn, and F BEL will not support anything into Paris. Hold A PAR and keep out of Belgium and the Channel, and our terms stand. I cannot promise more than that while Italy is pressing you.

I will hold A PAR and stay out of Belgium, Picardy, and the Channel this turn. Italy’s advance threatens both of us; please consider supporting A PAR from F BEL to block the capture. I have no sudden plans for Burgundy or Picardy.

Germany to England: I will not move A KIE or A BER into Denmark or Sweden this spring, and I expect F DEN and F SWE to stay out of Kiel, Berlin and Holland. A HOL holds. Belgium is yours to take. Let's both keep our centers and watch Italy, which is the real leader at 8 centers.

Germany to France: I will not attack Paris or Brest this spring. A HOL, A KIE, A BER and A MUN hold. Italy is the main threat to us both, and I may look at coordinating against it later. Hold Paris and Brest, and we stay at peace.

My immediate focus is Austria, not Russia. F TRI is aimed at VEN; A ROM will support my western front. I have no move planned against WAR, SEV, or MOS this spring. Please keep F BLA and A SEV defensive and avoid interfering in the Balkans.

My fleets will stay out of the Channel and North Sea. I’m moving against Austria: F TRI is aimed at VEN, not Greece, and I’ll keep my other fleets away from your western positions. I have no quarrel with your moves against Germany.

I can’t promise to keep clear of Austrian centers: I need room to grow, and F TRI is moving toward VEN. I’m not assisting Turkey in SER or RUM this spring, but I won’t bind myself to a safe settlement while we contest the board.
A BRE will stay out of PAR this spring; I’m focused east and have no intention of taking other French territory. Please continue to keep your army out of Italian territory.

I’m turning against Austria this spring: F TRI is moving toward VEN. I won’t assist Austria in SER, and ask you to press SER/RUM while keeping Turkish units clear of Italian centers and waters. Let’s coordinate without crossing into each other’s centers.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1918. I'm moving A WAR toward Galicia, and I'll keep Austria's Viennese and Galician approaches under pressure. Press VIE from the west with your A MUN; I'll aim my forces at Austria's southern holdings. Keep BER and HOL on your own border, and let's coordinate timing for fall.

Russia to Austria: I note your assurance that A RUM and A SER won't enter Russian centers. My F BLA and A SEV will stay on their current squares this spring. Hold your Balkan line against Turkey and we'll keep the peace on this border, but I want that promise honored in fall.

Russia to Turkey: Agreed for spring 1918. F BLA and A SEV stay out of the Balkan fight and I won't support Austria against you. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and make no move against SEV or RUM. Confirm in writing that F CON and F SMY stay put.

I cannot agree to a truce while A SER remains Austrian-held. This spring A BUL will move to SER, supported by A GRE. Keep A RUM from supporting SER and keep A SER and A RUM out of my other centers; I will keep my forces clear of RUM.

Yes, I’m committing to attack SER this spring: A BUL to SER with support from A GRE. Your F TRI to VEN will put pressure on Austria from the west. I’ll keep Turkish units out of Italian centers and fleets clear of Italian waters.

Your F TRI–VEN would take an Austrian center and force a direct war while Turkey presses SER. Keep F TRI out of VEN this fall, and I will keep my units out of Italian centers; we can both concentrate east instead. Are you willing to hold the line?

A SER will hold, supported by A RUM. I will keep A RUM and A SER out of Turkish centers this fall if A BUL and A GRE stay clear of SER and RUM. If you attack SER again, I will treat this as an open Balkan war.
I will keep A RUM and A SER clear of Russian centers this fall. Can you keep F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER, and consider pressure on Turkey rather than opening our border?

England to Germany, Fall 1918: I hold F DEN and F SWE in place and will not enter Kiel, Berlin or Holland. Italy is the leader at 8 centers, and I'm weighing how to stop that. Would you commit A MUN or A KIE to defend Germany's centers against any Italian push north, so we can both keep our homes?

My A BUR is now the only French unit. Italy has 8 centers and is the immediate threat to the board. Would F BEL support A BUR to hold this fall? I will stay out of Belgium and the Channel. Please tell me whether F BEL is committed elsewhere.

My A BUR will hold this fall. Italy is at 8 centers; can we coordinate to contain its advance? Please keep A MUN and A HOL from attacking or supporting an attack on Burgundy, and consider pressure on Italy. What are your orders?

I will hold A BUR and stay out of Italian territory. You are at 8 centers and close to winning; I ask that you leave Burgundy alone this fall and direct your forces elsewhere. Is A GAS staying out of Burgundy?

Germany to England, Fall 1918: I hold BER, KIE, HOL, MUN. F DEN and F SWE sit on my borders with no deal. Tell me plainly whether F DEN leaves Denmark this fall. If F DEN or F SWE moves into KIE, BER or HOL, I will treat it as war. Otherwise I stay out of Denmark and Sweden.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1918: I want Austria's VIE and BUD, not your centers. A MUN is moving toward Bohemia this fall. Tell me your exact orders for WAR, SEV and BLA, and whether you will take GAL and RUM. Let's keep our timing aligned against Austria.

Germany to Austria, Fall 1918: Your units at VIE and BUD are my focus now, and I will press Bohemia. I suggest you pull A BUD and A VIE back toward Galicia and Hungary rather than hold them. Tell me your fall moves so we avoid a collision in the centre.

I hold F VEN after taking it this spring. Please do not support Austria in trying to dislodge it; can you press A SER–RUM or another Austrian center this fall? I will not move against your centers or waters.

F VEN is in my hands, and I intend to retain it. I propose you leave it uncontested this fall and keep your units out of Italian centers; I will not move against TRI or TYR. Are you willing to avoid a costly fight over VEN?

My fleets remain away from the Channel and North Sea. I’m consolidating in VEN and have no move planned against your northern centers. What are you targeting this fall, and can you confirm you won’t interfere with my western Mediterranean positions?

Russia to Germany, Fall 1918: Austria is nearly finished and I want its Galician and Viennese centers. My A WAR and F BAL stay put. Confirm your exact fall orders for BER, MUN, HOL, and whether A MUN is taking VIE or BOH. I'd rather we split Austria than fight each other.

Let’s coordinate against Austria this fall: your F VEN can pressure TRI, while I will press SER/RUM. I will keep Turkish units out of Italian centers and waters; please avoid supporting Austria against me.

Can we renew Balkan neutrality for fall? I intend to press Austria, not Russia. Please keep A SEV and F BLA out of the Balkans and do not support Austria; I will keep Turkish fleets out of the Black Sea and make no move on SEV.

You have refused to yield SER, so I expect the Balkan fight to continue this fall. Will A RUM again support SER, or are you willing to keep it clear and limit the conflict? I will keep Turkish units clear of RUM if you keep your forces out of my centers.

I will not pull A BUD or A TYR away from the central front while you threaten Bohemia and my Austrian centers. I propose we avoid a costly clash: keep A BER and A MUN out of BOH and TYR, and I will keep A BUD and A TYR out of your centers. Otherwise I will defend my position.

A RUM will support A SER again this fall; I will not surrender SER while A BUL and A GRE threaten it. I will keep A RUM and A SER out of Turkish centers, but your attack on SER will be treated as open war. Keep your forces clear of SER and RUM if you want to limit the conflict.

I cannot leave VEN uncontested while your fleet occupies it; it is an Austrian center, and I will defend it. Keep F VEN out of TRI and I will keep my units out of Italian centers. With Turkey also pressing SER, a wider war between us serves neither side.

England to Germany, Fall 1918: F DEN and F SWE stay where they are this fall and neither enters KIE, BER or HOL. I am not moving on your homeland. Keep A KIE and A MUN at home and we remain at peace. Italy is the threat to both of us, so I suggest we each watch our own borders and talk again next year.

England to France: I will not support anything into Burgundy or Paris this fall, and F BEL stays committed to my own Belgium plans, so it cannot support A BUR. Hold your position, keep out of Belgium and the Channel, and our terms stand. Italy is the danger to you, so consider whether your remaining army can hold Burgundy without my help.

England to Italy, Fall 1918: I keep my fleets out of the Channel and North Sea as promised. My northern moves are defensive for now. Your consolidation in VEN is your business. Please keep F ION and F ADR away from Greece and the Aegean, where I have interests, and we will both do well.

Germany to England: F DEN and F SWE staying put is fine as long as they never enter KIE, BER or HOL. I will keep A KIE and A BER at home and not move into Denmark or Sweden. Italy is a real threat, but I am focused on Austria's Bohemian and Viennese centers for now. Keep your fleets in the North Sea and we stay at peace.

Germany to Russia: A MUN moves toward Bohemia this fall, aimed at Austria's VIE and BUD, not your centers. I will not touch WAR, SEV or BLA. Keep A WAR on Galicia and take RUM if you can. I hold BER, KIE, HOL. Let's keep timing aligned and avoid any clash in the south.

Germany to France: A BUR may hold. I will not move A MUN or A HOL into Burgundy or support anyone against it. Italy is a shared concern, but my fall priority is Austria in the south-east. Hold Paris and Brest and we stay at peace.
A GAS will stay out of Burgundy this fall. I’m not looking to open a western front; please keep A BUR clear of my positions while I consolidate in the south.
I will not move against TRI or TYR this fall, but F VEN must hold its position. If you leave VEN uncontested and keep your units clear of Italian centers, we can avoid spending forces on this front.

I will not support Austria against you. F VEN will hold, and I won’t move against Turkish centers or waters this fall. Please press RUM or another Austrian position, and avoid any attack that could dislodge F VEN.

Russia to Germany: A WAR and F BAL hold this fall, though I may shift A WAR toward GAL later. A MUN toward BOH is fine by me; take VIE and BUD and I will not contest them. Keep BER and HOL on your border with England and France, and we will keep coordinating against Austria.

Russia to Austria: Your assurances have been noted many times, and your RUM and SER remain next to my SEV and BLA. I will judge you by your moves this fall. Hold GAL and RUM, and show me you are willing to fight Turkey rather than sit on Russian borders.

Russia to Turkey: Agreed for fall 1918. F BLA and A SEV stay out of the Balkan fight and I will not support Austria against you. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and make no move against SEV or RUM. Please confirm F CON and F SMY stay put this fall.

A BUL will again move to SER, supported by A GRE. Your A RUM supporting A SER will make this an open Balkan war, as you warned. I will keep Turkish units out of RUM and your other centers this fall; you can still limit the conflict by keeping A RUM clear of SER.

I’ll press A BUL–SER with support from A GRE; A RUM supporting SER is the obstacle, so I can’t promise a breakthrough or a move into RUM. Please keep F VEN pressuring TRI and do not support Austria. Turkish units will stay clear of Italian centers and waters.

I will not spend this spring trying to dislodge F VEN. Keep it out of TRI and leave my other centers alone; I will keep my forces out of Italian centers and concentrate east against Turkey. Can you confirm you will not move against TRI?
Turkey is still pressing SER from BUL and GRE. Can you put pressure on Turkey this spring, while keeping F BLA and A SEV clear of RUM and SER? I will keep A RUM and A SER out of Russian centers.

I will defend SER and will not leave it undefended for your attack. Keep A BUL and A GRE out of SER and RUM this spring, and I will keep A RUM and A SER out of Turkish centers. Are you willing to stop the Balkan fighting?

England to Italy: Italy leads at 8 centers and is the board's main threat, so I want clarity. Will F ENG, F NAF and F GRE leave the Channel and Greek waters this spring? If you are truly consolidating in VEN, I can keep my fleets north. Otherwise I must rethink my position toward you.

You are at 8 centers and close to winning. I’ll keep A MAR and A PAR out of Italian territory; please keep F PIE and A GAS out of MAR and PAR this turn. Can we agree to avoid opening a western front while you focus elsewhere?

Italy is at 8 centers and close to an 18-center win. Will F BEL support A PAR to hold this spring? I’ll keep both French armies out of Belgium and the Channel. Please tell me if F BEL is committed elsewhere.

Italy is at 8 centers and is the immediate threat to a solo win. Can you coordinate with England to contain Italy this turn? I’ll keep A MAR and A PAR out of German territory; please keep your armies from attacking them. What are A MUN and A HOL doing?

Germany to England, Spring 1919: Our history is clear: F DEN and F SWE have not moved into KIE, BER or HOL, and I have kept A KIE and A BER home. Confirm now that both fleets stay out of my home centers this spring. I will not enter Denmark or Sweden. If Italy pushes north, we should talk about it openly.

I hold VEN and intend to keep it. Please avoid supporting attacks on it; I will not promise to leave TRI or other Austrian centers alone. What are your plans for TRI and SER this spring? A mutually agreed line would avoid wasting units while Turkey remains a threat.

Can you confirm your spring targets? I’m prepared to press Austria, but won’t support moves against your centers. Please keep Turkish units out of Italian centers and waters, and avoid supporting Austria against VEN. If you’re still pressing SER, tell me where you need coordination.
