Russia to Germany: Fall 1932. Italy is still the leader and must be stopped. Confirm your A VIE and A MUN actions and whether A BUD holds. I will send A SER against Trieste and keep A WAR out of Silesia and Prussia. Send exact orders first so we avoid bounces.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1932. Italy at 10 is the shared threat. Tell me your exact moves for F SMY, A ANK and A SYR. I will not enter Constantinople, and I will keep A SEV and A BUL off your centers if you keep your fleets out of Sevastopol and Bulgaria. Let us coordinate against Italian Rumania.

Italy now has 10 centers and remains the immediate danger. This fall I can renew pressure on GRE from BUL/SOUTH, with EAS supporting. Will you use A SER to pressure TRI and A RUM to defend against or attack Italy? Please keep A RUM out of Turkish centers and tell me your exact orders.

Italy’s lead is now decisive: it has 10 centers. Can you move A MUN toward TYR or A SIL toward TRI this fall? I’ll keep pressure on the Italian Balkan position from the south. Please tell me which route you can commit to.

Italy is at 10 centers and needs only eight more to win. Are you willing to coordinate against its expansion this fall? Your northern fleets can threaten Italian holdings such as BRE or support pressure elsewhere; I can contest GRE from the south. What are your plans?

England to Germany: My fall orders are still open. Italy's western fleets are the threat, so I may move F BEL and F LON toward PIC and BRE if Italy does not withdraw. Tell me your exact A MUN, A BUD, A SIL moves first, and I will coordinate with you before committing my northern fleets.

England to France: I will not move F BEL into PIC to help you unless Italy's A BUR and F WES leave the western coast in writing. Hold A PAR and A BRE for now. If Italy attacks Brest or Paris, I will reconsider support, but I make no firm promise this fall.

England to Turkey: I agree Italy must be checked before it reaches 18. I will press Italy's western fleets rather than promise more. Please contest GRE and the Balkans from the south, and tell me your exact fall orders so we can avoid blundering into each other.

Germany to England: I am holding A MUN, A BUD and A SIL this fall, so no northern move from me. Italy's western fleets are your problem to press. I will not commit to striking VIE or TYR yet. Keep F LON and F BEL pressuring Brest and Picardy and we can both gain.

Germany to Russia: Italy must be checked, but I need your exact orders first. Show me A SER, A BUL, A RUM and A WAR. If you clearly attack Trieste or Rumania, I will hit Italian units in the north. Until then A BUD and A MUN hold.

Germany to Turkey: A MUN goes nowhere this fall; I am holding it and A BUD for defense. Italy's northern armies are the danger to me, so I need to see Italy move first. Keep your pressure on the Balkans from the south and tell me your orders.

Germany to Italy: Your A VIE and A TYR are close to MUN and BUD. Hold them out of Tyrolia and Bohemia and I will keep my armies home. If A VIE or A TYR moves toward MUN or BUD, I will respond with force. Confirm your orders now.
A VIE and A TYR will stay out of MUN and BUD this fall. I need to keep the eastern front contained, so please keep A MUN and A BUD out of VIE and TRI. I’m not seeking a northern war.

I can’t promise to withdraw F GOL or A BUR while Turkey and Russia threaten my centers. I will keep A BUR out of PAR and PIC this fall, but Italy will defend its position. Please don’t move F LON or F BEL against my western forces.

A RUM will stay out of SEV, and A VIE will stay out of Russian centers this fall. I can’t withdraw from Rumania while your A SER line threatens my Balkans. Please keep A WAR and A SER out of TRI and VEN; I will not attack Russian centers.
A BUR will stay out of PAR this fall, and I will keep my western units out of French centers. Please keep A BRE out of Italian centers; I need to focus on the eastern front.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1932. My plan: A SER to Trieste, A GAL and A SEV press Rumania, A WAR holds in Warsaw and stays out of Silesia. Please keep A BUD off Serbia and hit Italian units in Tyrol or Vienna, not Munich-adjacent lines. Confirm your orders first so we avoid bounces.

Russia to England: Agreed Italy must be slowed. This fall A GAL, A SEV and A SER go for Rumania, and A SER may hit Trieste. Vienna is out of reach for me this turn. Press Italy's western fleets, and keep your fleets out of the Baltic and Russian Norway waters.

Russia to France: I will contest Rumania this fall with A SER, A GAL and A SEV. Trieste is pressured too. Italy's eastern centers are my focus, so I cannot promise anything in the west. Hit Italian units around Burgundy and Marseille if you can.

Russia to Turkey: I will not enter Constantinople or Greece. A SEV stays out of Bulgaria unless Italy moves into Rumania against me. Keep F SMY and A ANK off Sevastopol and Moscow. Italy is the target, so tell me whether your Greek strike is coordinated with my Rumania push.

Russia to Italy: No standstill. A RUM must leave Rumania and your Serbia-adjacent units must stop pressing Russian positions. Until then A SER and A SEV stay hostile to Trieste and Rumania. You lead at 10, so I will not hand you any more centers.

I’ll keep A ANK, A SYR, F EAS and F BUL/SOUTH off Russian centers. I intend to keep pressure on GRE from F BUL/SOUTH, with F EAS supporting if possible; I won’t move against RUM. Please use A SER to pressure TRI and keep A RUM out of Turkish centers.

I can’t agree to leave GRE unchallenged while you hold 10 centers and have A RUM and A VIE nearby. I’ll keep my forces clear of RUM and TRI this fall, but F BUL/SOUTH will contest GRE. Please keep A VIE and A RUM away from ANK and SMY.

England to Italy: Your fleets have shifted west while you promised quiet. Italy at 10 is too strong to ignore. State plainly whether A BUR and F WES will stay out of BRE, PIC, BEL and PAR this spring, and whether F SPA/SOUTH and F ION are heading toward Tunis or the Aegean. I will decide my northern moves based on your answer.
A BUR can still take PAR if you turn west. You have repeatedly said it will stay out; please confirm A BUR holds or moves east this spring. I will keep A PAR out of Italian territory.
Italy remains the solo threat, and A BUR is one move from my last center. Can A MUN move to BUR this spring to contest it? I will keep A PAR out of German territory.
Please keep pressure on Italy’s eastern centers this spring, especially RUM or TRI, and avoid any arrangement that lets Italy gain ground. My A PAR and A BRE will hold.

Germany to Italy: Spring 1933 I hold A MUN and A BUD, but Italy's A VIE and A TYR are right next to both. Italy is at 10 and must be stopped by someone. Confirm in writing that A VIE and A TYR will not enter Bohemia, Tyrolia or Munich-adjacent lines, and I will reciprocate.

Germany to Russia: Spring 1933. Italy is the leader and both our Balkan fronts are the key. I need your exact orders for A SER, A GAL, A RUM, A WAR, A MOS and A SEV before I commit A BUD or A MUN. If you hit Trieste or Venice, I will move against Italian units in Tyrol.

Germany to England: Italy's fleets on WES and ION threaten you both. Tell me your exact F LON, F BEL, F NTH orders this spring. I am holding A MUN, A BUD and A KIE for now and will not strike HOL or DEN while you press Channel and Brest.

Russia remains the immediate threat on the Balkan line. I propose we avoid attacking each other’s centers this spring: keep F BUL/SOUTH and F EAS out of GRE and my other centers, and I’ll keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish territory. Can you confirm your orders?

I can’t withdraw A SER or abandon my Balkan position, but I have no reason to open a new front against you this spring. Keep A WAR and A RUM out of TRI and my other centers, and I’ll keep A SER out of your centers. Are you willing to hold?

I’m concentrating on the Balkan front this spring. I will keep A BUR out of PAR and PIC; please keep F LON and F BEL away from my western forces and centers. Can we leave the western front quiet for this turn?

Russia to Italy: Spring 1933. You hold 10 centers and A RUM is still in Rumania. Tell me now whether A RUM leaves Rumania this spring and whether F BLA stays out of Sevastopol. Without a clear answer, I will press Rumania and treat your Balkan units as hostile.

I’ll keep pressure on Italy from the eastern Mediterranean. What are your exact plans against Italy this spring, especially for your fleets near the western centers? Please avoid moves that interfere with my fleets in EAS and BUL.

Italy remains the immediate threat. I will keep A ANK, A SYR, F EAS, and F BUL clear of Russian centers. What are your spring orders for A RUM, A SER, and A GAL? I’d like us to coordinate pressure on Italy without either of us entering the other’s centers.

I will not move against ANK or SMY this spring. Italy’s 10 centers remain an urgent threat; are A VIE and A RUM staying clear of Turkish centers, and what are your plans for F GRE? I cannot promise to leave the Balkans uncontested while you remain poised to expand.

England to Germany: My spring plan is to keep F LON and F BEL in place and move F NTH to hold the North Sea; I will not strike HOL or DEN. Italy's western fleets are the threat, so if you press TYR or VIE with your armies, I will keep pressing Brest and Picardy. Let's keep our orders visible to each other before fall.

England to Italy: Your fleets still sit on the western coast, and A BUR is next to PAR and PIC. I will hold my western fleets this spring only if A BUR and F WES leave BRE, PIC, BEL and PAR in writing. Answer plainly whether F SPA/SOUTH and F ION head to Tunis or the Aegean. Otherwise I will reconsider.

England to Turkey: My spring orders keep the northern fleets near home, and I am not moving into the Mediterranean. I will press Italy's western fleets if they stay on the Atlantic and Channel coasts. Keep contesting GRE and BUL from the south, and I will avoid interfering with your fleets in EAS and BUL.

Germany to France: A MUN to Burgundy is not something I can commit to this spring. Italy's A BUR is adjacent to your last centers, but my armies are needed on the eastern front against Italian moves into Tyrolia. If you hold A PAR and A BRE firmly, we may both survive. Tell me your exact orders and I will keep you in mind.

A RUM will hold this spring, and F BLA will stay out of Sevastopol. I’ll keep A SER out of Russian centers; please keep A WAR and A RUM out of TRI and my other centers. I’m not withdrawing from the Balkans while your forces remain poised there.

A BUR will stay out of BRE, PIC, and PAR this spring, and F WES will stay out of your centers. F SPA/SOUTH and F ION are focused on the Mediterranean, not your northern centers. Please keep F LON and F BEL away from my western units and centers.
A VIE and A TYR will not enter Bohemia or Munich this spring. I’m not seeking a northern front; please keep A MUN and A BUD out of VIE and TRI. My priority is containing the Balkan threats.
A BUR will hold this spring and will not enter PAR. I’ll keep my western forces out of French centers; please keep A PAR out of Italian territory while I focus east.

A VIE and A RUM will stay clear of Turkish centers this spring, and F GRE is not moving against you. I’ll keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish territory if F BUL/SOUTH and F EAS stay out of GRE and my other centers. Russia remains the immediate Balkan threat.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1933. My orders: A SER attacks Trieste, A GAL and A MOS hold the Rumania line with A SEV supporting, A WAR holds Warsaw. A RUM stays hostile to Italian units. Hold A BUD and A MUN if you like, but move on Tyrol or Venice with your A MUN and A BUD and I will press Italy hard in the Balkans with you.

Russia to France: I am pressing Rumania and Trieste this spring with A SER, A GAL and A SEV. Italy's western centers around Marseille and Spain are yours to contest. I cannot spare units for the west, but hold your Brest and Paris and keep your fleets active in the Mediterranean.

Russia to Italy: A RUM is still hostile and your Balkan units are treated as threats. I will not give you a standstill. If A RUM leaves Rumania and F BLA stays out of Sevastopol, I will keep A WAR out of Trieste and Venice this spring. Answer clearly before I commit.

Russia to Turkey: My spring plan is A RUM and A SEV pressing Rumania and A SER against Trieste. A GAL holds. I will not enter Bulgaria or Constantinople this spring. Keep your A ANK, A SYR and F EAS off Sevastopol and Moscow, and your Greek push from F BUL/SOUTH is your business against Italy.

I can confirm F EAS and F BUL/SOUTH will stay out of GRE and your other centers this spring. I will keep A ANK and A SYR clear of your territory as well. In return, keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and keep A VIE and A RUM away from ANK and SMY. I’m preserving the Balkan line while Russia remains the immediate threat.

England to Italy: Your fleets and A BUR sit on our western coast while you promise quiet. Italy at 10 is too strong. Write plainly that A BUR and F GOL leave the Channel and Brest approaches this fall, and I will keep F LON and F BEL home. Otherwise I will press your western units.

England to Germany: Italy is the leader and must be checked. If you move A TYR or A VIE against Italy this fall, I will press Italian western units with F BEL and F LON. Tell me your exact A MUN, A BUD, A SIL orders so we can coordinate before I commit.

England to Russia: Italy threatens us both. Are you striking Rumania or Vienna this fall with A GAL, A WAR, A RUM? I will pressure Italy's western fleets. Confirm your exact orders so we avoid blundering into each other.

Italy’s A BUR can take PAR, and F GOL threatens MAR. Can you move F BEL to PIC this fall and commit to supporting A PAR’s defense next spring? I’ll keep A BRE clear of your centers. Please also use your northern forces to keep Italy from gaining ground.

Italy’s A BUR threatens my last center, PAR. Please move A MUN to BUR this fall to contest it; I’ll keep A PAR out of German territory. Italy is the common threat—can you spare that move rather than let it consolidate in the west?

A BUR can eliminate France by taking PAR, while F GOL threatens MAR. Please keep A BUR out of PAR and F GOL out of MAR this fall as you have promised before. I’ll keep A BRE clear of Italian centers; otherwise I have little choice but to seek help against your western advance.

Germany to Italy: Fall 1933. Italy at 10 centers is too far ahead for me to accept. Your A BOH and A TYR sit next to my A MUN and A BUD. Withdraw A BOH from Bohemia now and I will keep my armies home. Otherwise I will treat Bohemia as hostile and act accordingly.

Germany to Russia: Fall 1933. Italy holds A BOH and A BUL, next to my Bohemia and your Rumania line. Let us both strike together: I will move A MUN to Bohemia against A BOH if you hit A BUL or A SER with A RUM and A GAL. Confirm your exact orders now so we avoid bounces.

Germany to England: Italy's F GOL and F ADR threaten both of us. Tell me your exact fall orders for F LON, F BEL and F NOR. I will keep A HOL and A KIE off Denmark and Belgium if you press Brest or Picardy against France's last centers and the Italian western fleets.

Russia remains the obstacle in the Balkans. This fall I propose we coordinate against Russian centers: I can press RUM from BUL and SEV from BLA; please avoid GRE and my other centers, and tell me whether F TYS will move east or west. I’ll keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers.

I intend to focus west against France, with F GOL toward MAR and A BUR staying out of PAR and PIC this fall. Please keep F BEL and F LON away from my western units and centers; are you planning to move against France or Italy?

I’m not seeking a new attack on your centers this fall, but I cannot abandon the Balkans while your forces remain there. I’ll keep A SER out of Russian centers; will A WAR stay out of TRI and VEN, and will you avoid attacking RUM?

Russia to Italy: Fall 1933. Your F BLA and A BUL sit on my southern border, and you still hold A RUM-free Rumania but I see no withdrawal. Tell me now: will A BUL leave Bulgaria and F BLA stay out of Sevastopol? Without a clear yes, I will treat your Balkan units as hostile and press Rumania and Warsaw-adjacent lines.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1933. Italy holds Bohemia and Tyrol-adjacent units, so the Italian A BOH and A TRI are your natural targets. I will hit A TRI or A BUL from the east with A GAL, A RUM and A SEV. Please move A MUN toward Bohemia or Tyrol and tell me your exact orders so we avoid bounces.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1933. I will keep A SEV and A MOS off Bulgaria and Constantinople. Your F CON and A ANK must stay off Sevastopol and Moscow. Italy's A BUL is the shared threat; tell me whether you will strike it from F CON or A SMY so we coordinate without bounces.

Italy is still at 10 and the immediate threat. I plan A BUL-GRE with F EAS supporting. Please keep A SER and A RUM out of Turkish centers; can you use A SER to pressure TRI and tell me your orders for RUM and GAL?

Italy remains close to winning. I plan to contest GRE from A BUL, supported by F EAS. Please continue pressure on Italy’s western holdings and let me know which Italian center your fleets can threaten this fall.

I’m keeping A ANK, A SYR, and F CON clear of your territory, but I cannot leave your 10-center position unchallenged. I intend to contest GRE from A BUL with F EAS support. Keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and keep A VIE away from ANK and SMY.

England to Germany: My fall orders are F LON to ENG hold, F BEL hold, F NOR hold, with no move into HOL or DEN. If you hold A HOL and A KIE and keep A BUD, A MUN, A SIL off Italian-held ground, I will consider pressing Italy's western units. Tell me your exact A SIL and A MUN orders first.

England to Italy: Your F GOL and A BUR sit on our coast and Italy at 10 is too strong. I will not take your word again. Answer plainly: will A BUR and F GOL leave the Channel and Brest approaches this fall? Without a written yes, I will press your western units with F BEL and F LON.

England to Turkey: Thanks for the Balkan pressure. My fall fleets stay home in the North Sea and Channel, so F EAS and your A BUL attack on GRE will not be interfered with by me. Keep pushing GRE and TUN from the east, and tell me which Italian centre you target so we do not overlap.

England to France: I will not move F BEL into PIC this fall; that would expose my northern centres to Germany. I can make no promise to support A PAR next spring either. Hold A PAR and A BRE, and if Italy's A BUR attacks Paris I will reconsider in spring.

Germany to England: I will not move A HOL or A KIE against Denmark or Belgium this fall. Italy's F GOL and F ADR are the real threat to both of us. I am still weighing a push on Bohemia, so give me your exact F LON, F BEL and F NOR orders first. Press Brest or Picardy and I will keep my word.

Germany to Russia: Your plan to hit A TRI or A BUL is sound. I will decide on A MUN after I see your exact orders for A GAL, A RUM and A SEV. Confirm them and I will consider moving against A BOH. Do not hit Silesia or Munich-adjacent lines, or we will both lose the bet.

Germany to France: A MUN to Burgundy is not possible for me this fall. Italy's A BOH and A BUL need all my attention on the east. Hold A PAR and A BRE firmly and press Italy's western fleets with England if you can. I cannot promise more.

A BUR will leave the French border this fall and will not enter PAR or PIC. F GOL is in the Mediterranean, not the Channel approaches; I will not promise to leave it out of MAR. Keep F LON and F BEL home as you proposed.
A BOH will leave Bohemia this fall; I’m not seeking a northern front. Please keep A MUN and A BUD out of my centers, especially TRI and VIE, while I focus west and south.

I won’t promise to remove A BUL while Turkish and Russian forces threaten the Balkans. F BLA is not moving to SEV this fall, and I’ll keep A SER out of Russian centers. Keep A WAR away from TRI and VEN and do not attack RUM.

I will keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and A VIE away from ANK and SMY. I can’t accept an attack on GRE. My priority is the Russian line; please keep F EAS and F TYS away from my centers while we deal with Russia.

A BUR will stay out of PAR, and I’ll keep it clear of PIC as well. I cannot promise F GOL will stay out of MAR; your best course is to keep A BRE clear of my centers and avoid joining a coalition against me.

Russia to England: I am not striking Vienna this fall. A RUM moves against Bulgaria, with A GAL supporting, and A WAR and A MOS hold. Italy's western fleets are your problem to pressure, and I'll keep my units away from Norway, Sweden and St Petersburg.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1933 orders: A RUM to BUL, A GAL supports A RUM into Bulgaria, A WAR holds, A MOS holds. Move A MUN to Bohemia against A BOH and we should both gain. I won't touch Silesia or Galicia-to-Vienna lines this turn.

Russia to Italy: I have no standstill to offer. Your A BUL is under threat from A RUM this fall. Withdraw it and I will reconsider Balkan moves. Keep F BLA away from Sevastopol and I won't press further in the south.

Russia to Turkey: Fall orders: A RUM attacks Bulgaria, supported by A GAL. A SEV and A MOS stay off Bulgaria and Constantinople. Strike A BUL from F CON or A SMY as you planned; if that succeeds, we both gain. Keep your units off Sevastopol and Moscow.

I cannot strike A BUL this fall: it is my unit, and F CON cannot attack Bulgaria. I intend A BUL-GRE with F EAS supporting; please keep A SER and A RUM out of Turkish centers. Use A SER against TRI if possible, and let me know your RUM and GAL plans.

I will not coordinate an attack on Russian centers while you hold 10 and are positioned to win. F TYS will not move west in support of your expansion; I intend to contest GRE from A BUL with F EAS support. Keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and A VIE away from ANK and SMY.

England to Italy: Your fleets sit in the west while you promise quiet. Italy at 10 is too strong. Tell me plainly whether A BUR and F MAR stay out of BRE, PAR, PIC and BEL this spring, and whether F AEG and F ION are heading east, not Tunis. Without a clear written answer I will reconsider my northern orders.

Italy’s A BUR can take PAR if it attacks. Please move F BEL to PIC and support A PAR to hold; I will keep A BRE and A PAR clear of English centers. If Italy leaves PAR alone, your fleet can return next turn.

Your A BUR still threatens my last center. Please keep A BUR out of PAR this spring, as you have promised before, and keep F MAR out of Brest. I will keep A BRE and A PAR out of Italian centers. Can you confirm your orders?

Italy remains the power closest to winning. Can you move A MUN to BUR and support my A PAR holding from Italy’s A BUR? I will keep A PAR out of German territory. If you cannot contest Burgundy, please tell me what you can do to check Italy.

Germany to Italy: Italy at 10 is too strong for either of us to ignore. Your A BOH has not left Bohemia, and A TYR threatens my Munich line. Withdraw A BOH and A TYR from my border now or I will strike Tyrolia this spring. Reply with exact orders.

Germany to England: Italy's fleets are the real threat to us both. I want to strike Italian Bohemia and Tyrolia this spring. Tell me your exact orders for F LON, F BEL, F NOR, F DEN and A EDI. I will keep HOL and KIE from attacking you if you press Brest and the Italian western fleets.

Germany to Russia: Confirm exact orders for A MOS, A WAR, A SEV, A RUM and A MOS. Italy's A RUM and A SER are the target. If you hit Rumania with A SEV and A WAR, I will move A BUD and A MUN against A BOH this spring. Do not move into Silesia.

I propose a Balkan standstill: keep F ION and F CON away from GRE and my centers, and I’ll keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers. I need room to deal with Russia; are you willing to hold that line this spring?

I’m focused south and east this spring, not on German centers. Please keep A MUN and A BUD out of TRI and VIE, and I’ll keep my northern units clear of your centers. Can we avoid opening a front between us?

I’m not seeking English centers this spring. Please keep F LON and F BEL away from my western units and centers, and I’ll avoid moving against your centers. Are you prepared to keep the western front quiet?

Russia to Italy: Italy has 10 centers and is the runaway leader, so Russia cannot stand by. I will not promise a standstill. Tell me plainly whether A BUR, A TYR and F BLA will stay out of Russian centers, and I will decide my Balkan moves from your answer.

Russia to Turkey: Italy must be stopped before it reaches 18. Let us both hit Italian units in the Balkans this spring. I will press Rumania and Bulgaria with A RUM and A GAL. Confirm your F CON and A SMY moves against A BUL so we avoid bounces, and keep your fleets off Sevastopol and Moscow.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1934 I will hit Italian units in the Balkans and keep Warsaw and Moscow secure. Strike A TYR or A BOH from your side with A MUN and A BUD, and I will not touch Silesia or Galicia-to-Vienna. Confirm your exact orders so we avoid bounces.

Italy remains the leading threat at 10 centers. Please press its western centers this turn—especially MAR or SPA—and tell me your exact target. I will pressure Italy from the east; avoid NAP and the eastern Mediterranean so our attacks do not overlap.

Italy at 10 centers is too close to victory for me to leave uncontested. I propose you keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and I will keep my units out of your centers this turn. I intend to strengthen my Balkan position; what are your exact orders for A ALB, F AEG, and F BLA?

Italy is still the urgent threat, but I need to secure my own line. Keep A SEV and A MOS out of Turkish centers, and please tell me your plans for A RUM and A WAR. I will not commit to an attack on your centers; can you pressure Italy rather than contesting the Balkans with me?

England to Germany: F LON, F BEL, F NOR, F DEN and A EDI hold this spring. I am not attacking your Holland or Kiel. Italy is the target; strike Bohemia and Tyrolia and I will look at pressing Italian western units in fall. Keep A HOL and A KIE off Denmark and Belgium.
England to France: F BEL will not move to Picardy this spring. My northern centres need guarding against Germany. Hold A PAR and A BRE. If Italy attacks Paris, we can talk again in fall.

England to Italy: Words are not enough. Write plainly that A BUR and F MAR leave BRE, PAR, PIC and BEL this spring, and that F AEG and F ION head east, not Tunis. Without that, I keep my northern fleets ready to press your western units.

England to Turkey: Agreed on Italy as the main threat. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Channel this spring, so Italy's western units will feel pressure from me later. Keep attacking GRE and Italian Adriatic and Aegean holdings; I will not interfere with your eastern Mediterranean plans.

Germany to Russia: My Spring 1934 plan is to strike Italian Bohemia and Tyrolia, but I will only move A MUN and A BUD once you have actually hit A RUM with A SEV and A WAR. Send me your exact orders first. I will not move into Silesia, and I expect the same from you toward Warsaw and Galicia.
A BUR will stay out of PAR, PIC and BEL; F MAR will not move to BRE. F AEG and F ION are moving east, not to Tunis. Please keep F LON and F BEL away from Italian units and centers this spring.

A BUR and A TYR will stay out of Russian centers, and F BLA will not move to SEV. I cannot promise wider Balkan restraint while Russian units threaten my position. Keep A WAR away from TRI and VEN, and avoid RUM.
A BOH will move out of Bohemia this spring; A TYR will not move against Munich or any German center. Please keep A MUN and A BUD out of TRI and VIE, and we can avoid opening a front.
Confirmed: A BUR will not move to PAR, and F MAR will stay out of Brest. I will not move against your centers this spring if A BRE and A PAR remain clear of Italian centers.

A ALB will hold, F AEG will move east, and F BLA will not attack a Turkish center. I will keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers if your units stay out of mine; please keep F ION and F CON clear of GRE and Italian centers.

Russia to Germany: My Spring 1934 plan is A WAR holds, A MOS holds, A SEV holds, and A RUM attacks Bulgaria-side Balkan targets with A GAL. I will not move into Silesia or against Galicia-to-Vienna. Strike Italy's A BOH or A TYR with A MUN and A BUD as you proposed, and we both gain. Do not touch Warsaw or Moscow.

Russia to Turkey: I will keep A SEV and A MOS off Turkish centers, and A WAR stays home. A RUM will press Bulgaria and Rumania against Italy, not your units. Italy at 10 is the danger, so strike A BUL with F CON and A SMY as you planned and keep your fleets away from Sevastopol and Moscow.

I will not commit F CON or A SMY against A BUL; F CON cannot enter Bulgaria, and I will keep it away from your centers. I’m not agreeing to a joint attack on Italy’s units while Italian forces are adjacent to my centers. Keep A SEV and A MOS clear of Turkish centers, and tell me whether A RUM will threaten BUL or my line.

I cannot accept a standstill that leaves Italy’s 10 centers unchallenged. I will keep my units out of your centers this spring, but I reserve the right to contest them later. Please keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers; what are A ALB, F AEG, and F BLA doing?

England to Italy: Italy is at 10 and your western fleets still sit on our coast. Plainly: will F GOL and A RUH stay out of BRE, PIC and BEL this fall, and will you commit to not attacking French or English centres? A written yes helps us both avoid a costly war while Turkey and Russia press you.

Italy is now at 10 and has A RUH near my last centers. Please support my A PIC hold with F BEL this fall, and keep your other units clear of BRE and PAR. I will keep A GAS and A PIC out of English centers.

Italy’s A RUH threatens my last centers and Italy is only eight centers from victory. Can A HOL move to RUH or otherwise contest Italy’s western army? I can keep my units clear of German centers; please tell me what pressure you can bring against Italy.

Your A RUH is close to my remaining centers. Please keep it out of Burgundy and my French centers this fall, and keep your western fleets away from French territory. I will keep A GAS and A PIC clear of Italian centers while you do.

Germany to Italy: Fall 1934. You lead at 10 centers and I will not help you grow further. Tell me exactly what A TYR, A VIE and A RUH do this fall. If A VIE or A TYR moves toward Munich or Bohemia, Germany will respond in force. Withdraw from my border and we can talk about a truce.

Your F ROM is occupying my center, and your F GRE/F CON threaten my southern line. Will you withdraw F ROM to NAP and keep your fleets out of Italian centers this fall? I need a clear answer before orders; I will not leave ROM undefended.
I’m not seeking German centers this fall. Please keep A BUD and A TYR out of TRI and VIE; I’ll keep my units clear of your centers. Can we avoid opening a front while I address the Turkish threat?

I propose keeping the western front quiet this fall: I will keep A RUH and F GOL out of PAR, PIC and BRE. Please keep A GAS and A PIC out of MAR and my other centers while I deal with the threat in the south.

Russia to Italy: You are at 10 and the board is turning against you. I want a real answer: will F BLA and A BUL leave Russian reach this fall? If you pull A BUL out of Bulgaria and keep F BLA off Sevastopol, I will hold A SEV and A MOS and stay out of Rumania. Otherwise expect A RUM and A WAR to hit your Balkan units.

Italy is at 10 and must be stopped. Your A GAS and A PIC are positioned to threaten its western centers: please move GAS-SPA and PIC-MAR this fall, or coordinate whichever attack is feasible. I will keep my eastern fleets clear of your operations.

Italy is close to winning. Please use A TYR to pressure VEN and A SIL/KIE to secure your line rather than leaving Italy free to expand. I will press Italy from the east; let me know if you can commit to VEN.

Italy is at 10 and has A RUM; we need to contain it now. Can A SEV attack RUM while A MOS supports, and can A WAR stay clear of Bulgaria? I will pressure Italy from the Balkans. Please avoid Turkish centers.

England to France: I will not move F BEL to support A PIC this fall; my northern centres face German units on HOL and KIE and I need F BEL where it is. Hold A PIC and A GAS, and keep your units off English centres. If Italy's A RUH moves on Paris or Brest, tell me plainly and we can discuss spring.

I’ll keep A PIC and A GAS out of your centers this fall, provided you keep A RUH and F GOL out of Burgundy and my French centers as proposed. Please confirm you will maintain that restraint next spring as well.

GAS-SPA is feasible; PIC-MAR is not a legal move. I can send A GAS to Spain while A PIC holds Paris. Please keep pressure on Italy in the east, especially Rumania or Trieste, so Italy cannot concentrate against us in the west.

Germany to Italy: Your fall moves so far have not satisfied me. A TYR and A VIE are on my border and I will not accept promises alone. Withdraw A TYR from Tyrolia to a non-border area and keep A VIE away from Bohemia and Munich, and we can discuss a truce. Otherwise Germany will respond against Tyrolia this fall.

Germany to France: A HOL cannot reach RUH this fall, and I will not expose my home centers to an Italian counterattack. I will keep A MUN and A BUD on defense. Press Italy's western army with England and your own units. I cannot promise more than that.

Germany to Turkey: I understand the threat Italy poses. A TYR to VEN is not something I will commit to this fall, since Italy's A VIE and A TYR sit on my border. Keep pressing Italy from the east and tell me your exact orders; I may reconsider once Italian units leave Bohemia and Tyrolia.
A BUL will leave Bulgaria toward CON, and F BLA will stay off Sevastopol. Please keep A WAR away from TRI and VEN and stay out of RUM; I want no Russian-Italian clash this fall.

A TYR will not move toward Munich or Bohemia, A VIE will stay clear of German centers, and A RUH will not move toward your centers. Please keep A BUD and A TYR out of TRI and VIE so we can avoid a front.

Yes: F GOL and A RUH will stay out of BRE, PIC and BEL, and I will not attack English or French centers this fall. Please keep F LON and F BEL away from my units and centers while I address the southern threat.

Confirmed: A RUH will stay out of Burgundy and all French centers, and my western fleets will stay away from French territory. Please keep A GAS and A PIC clear of MAR and my other centers while I deal with the threat in the south.

Russia to Turkey: I am weighing A SEV attacking RUM with A MOS support, but I need you to commit first. Show me F CON or A SMY moving against Italian units in Bulgaria or Greece this fall, and I will decide. A WAR will stay out of Bulgaria. Do not move toward Sevastopol or Moscow.

I will not withdraw F ROM to NAP; it is holding your center as pressure against your expansion. F GRE and F CON will remain out of your centers this fall, but I will not promise a broader standstill. Keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers, and keep A VIE away from ANK and SMY.

England to Italy: Your fall word stands on record. Spring 1935: will F ION and F TYS stay out of Spain, Marseille and the Channel? If you move F TYS toward Spain or BRE, I will treat it as a declaration. Tell me plainly by reply.

England to Germany: You now have A MUN and A RUH near Belgium and Holland. Confirm A RUH and A MUN will not enter BEL or HOL this spring. I hold F BEL and F LON, and I will keep F NOR and F DEN defensive if you strike Bohemia and Tyrolia as agreed.

England to France: I still hold F BEL in place. Your new A BRE is a welcome defence. If Italy's A BUR or A SPA moves on Paris, tell me and we can discuss support. Keep A PAR and A SPA off English centres.

Our western front is still the easiest place for either of us to lose ground. I propose a clear spring stand-down: keep A TUS and F TYS out of MAR and my other French centers, and I’ll keep A BUR and A BRE out of Italian centers. Can you confirm your intentions?

With ENGLAND and TURKEY both at 8 centers, we should avoid weakening each other while they race ahead. Will A RUH stay out of BUR and the French centers this spring? I’ll keep A BUR clear of German territory; please tell me where you intend to move it.

You are tied for the lead at 8, so your next moves matter greatly to France. Are you pressing ENGLAND or ITALY this spring? Please keep your units clear of my French centers; I’ll avoid Turkish centers while we both check the leaders.

Germany to England: I hold six centers and need your fleets to stay off HOL and KIE. In return I will move A MUN and A RUH away from your Low Countries. Which of F BEL, F LON and F NOR are you using to pressure France this fall? Tell me exact orders.

Germany to France: Italy's A RUH and A BUR are the threat to both of us. I can move A MUN to BUR this spring only if you support it with A PAR. Tell me exactly what A PAR and A SPA do, and whether you will hit Italy's western army.

Germany to Italy: Your A TYR and A VIE still sit on my border, and you have not withdrawn them. Tell me exact spring orders for A TYR, A VIE, A TRI and A SER. If Italian units stay in Bohemia or Tyrolia, Germany will move against them.

F ROM is occupying an Italian center. I intend to contest it with F TYS; keep F GRE and F CON out of Italian centers, and do not move F ROM to NAP or support it against me. I will keep A SER and A TRI out of Turkish centers this spring. Can we agree to avoid widening the war?

I want to avoid a Balkan front while I recover Rome. Keep A WAR out of TRI and VEN and stay out of RUM; I will keep F BLA off SEV and A SER out of Russian centers. Are you holding your Balkan units this spring?

I am not seeking German centers this spring. A TRI will stay clear of VIE and A SER clear of BUD; please keep A MUN and A VIE away from TRI and VEN. Can we keep the central front quiet while I address the Turkish threat?

Russia to Turkey: Italy's forces are the shared threat, but your F CON and A SMY have not moved against A BUL. Show me a real commitment this spring: F CON or A SMY into Bulgaria or Greece. Until then my A SEV and A MOS stay off your centers, and I will keep A RUM out of your line if you keep F ANK and A CON off Sevastopol and Moscow.

You are at 8 centers and the closest immediate rival to my 8. What are your orders this spring? I can keep my fleets out of your centers; please keep your units clear of my centers and the eastern Mediterranean while we contain Italy.

Italy is contained at 6 centers, but its units still threaten the Balkans. Can A TYR move to VEN this spring? I will keep pressure on Italy from the east. Please tell me your exact intentions around VEN and TRI.

Your forces remain close to my line. Will A SER and A TRI stay out of Turkish centers, and will F BLA avoid ANK and CON this spring? I intend to defend my centers and continue contesting Italian expansion; tell me your orders.

England to Germany: My spring orders are F BEL and F LON holding, F NOR and F DEN defensive. I will not move into HOL or KIE. Your A MUN and A RUH must stay out of BEL and HOL this spring, as you offered. Strike Bohemia and Tyrolia, and we can discuss Italian western units in fall. Confirm in writing.

England to Turkey: My spring is defensive: F BEL, F LON, F NOR, F DEN hold, A EDI stays home. I have no plans against your centres. Italy remains the shared threat in the west and south. Keep your fleets off my Scandinavian and Channel holdings and we stay at peace. Let me know if you press Italy's MAR or SPA, so I can time pressure on the west.

I’ll keep A BRE, A BUR, and A SPA clear of English centers. Italy’s western armies remain a serious threat; please consider pressuring them rather than leaving France isolated. Are you willing to move F BEL toward PIC or support France if Italy attacks Paris?

I cannot support A MUN-BUR from Paris: France has no unit in PAR, and A BUR currently occupies BUR. I can move A BUR-PAR, but that would leave you free to enter BUR and put Paris under pressure. I propose we both hold against Italy instead; tell me whether A RUH will stay clear of French centers.

Germany to England: My spring plan keeps A RUH and A MUN out of BEL and HOL this year if your F BEL, F LON and F NOR stay off HOL and KIE. I am not moving toward Denmark. Confirm F NOR and F DEN will not move into HOL or KIE, and tell me your exact fall orders.

Germany to Italy: Your A TYR and A VIE still sit on my border. Withdraw them from Tyrolia and Bohemia this spring and I will keep A MUN and A VIE-side units off TRI and VEN. Stay put and Germany will act against Tyrolia. Give exact orders for A TYR, A VIE, A TRI and A SER.

Germany to Turkey: A TYR to VEN is not something I can commit to this spring while Italian units hold Bohemia and Tyrolia. Strike Italy's southern units yourself, and tell me your exact orders for A SMY, A CON and F ROM so I can judge the Balkan picture.

Germany to France: I will move A MUN to BUR only if your A PAR supports it, and I need your exact orders for A PAR and A SPA. A RUH stays out of BUR this spring if you hit Italy's A BUR-side units and keep your fleets off Germany. Otherwise I cannot promise more.
F ION and F TYS will stay out of Spain, Marseille, and the Channel this spring. I’m focused on recovering Rome, not opening a western front; please keep F LON and F BEL away from Italian centers.
A TYR will move to BOH, A VIE will move to GAL, A TRI will stay out of VIE, and A SER will stay out of BUD. I’m not seeking German centers; please keep A MUN and A VIE away from TRI and VEN.
A SER and A TRI will stay out of Turkish centers, and F BLA will avoid ANK and CON. I intend to contest F ROM with F TYS; please keep F GRE and F CON out of Italian centers and do not support F ROM.
Agreed: A TUS and F TYS will stay out of MAR and all French centers this spring. Please keep A BUR and A BRE out of Italian centers; I want to avoid widening the western front while I recover Rome.

Russia to Italy: I will keep A WAR out of Trieste and Venice and stay out of Rumania this spring, as long as F BLA stays off Sevastopol and A SER stays out of Russian centers. Your A BUL is a different matter; if it moves toward Rumania or Sevastopol, I will respond. Holding my Balkan units for now, but I want your fleets and armies kept clear of Moscow and Warsaw too.

I’ll make a real commitment against Italy: F CON will move to Bulgaria this spring. Keep A RUM out of Bulgaria and my line, and keep A SEV and A MOS clear of Turkish centers. Please say whether A SEV is moving against Rumania.

I won’t agree to a wider standstill while F ROM occupies one of your centers. I’ll keep F GRE and F CON out of Italian centers this spring, but F ROM will not withdraw or support your defense. Keep A SER and A TRI clear of Turkish centers, and F BLA away from ANK and CON.

I’m pressing Italy in the east, not England this spring. I’ll keep my units clear of French centers; please keep your units clear of Turkish centers and continue pressuring Italy’s western flank. Is A GAS moving to SPA again?

England to Germany: Fall 1935 I hold F BEL, F LON, F NOR, F DEN and A EDI. I will not move into HOL or KIE. Please confirm A MUN and A RUH stay out of BEL and HOL this fall, and tell me your exact orders against Italian units in Tyrolia or Bohemia.

England to Italy: Your spring word stands on record. Fall 1935: confirm in writing that F ROM, F AEG and A VEN will not enter Spain, Marseille, Brest, Picardy or Belgium, and that your western units will not move toward English or French centres. Without a clear answer, I will keep my Channel fleets ready.

England to France: I keep F BEL in place this fall for now. If Italy's A SER or A TUS moves toward MAR or SPA, tell me your exact plan and I will weigh supporting you in spring. Keep A POR and A PAR off English centres.

France has only A MAR, A PAR and A POR, so another western clash could finish me without helping you. Please keep A TUS and A VEN out of MAR and keep your fleets away from SPA this fall. I will keep my units out of Italian centers; confirm your intended moves.

Please keep A TYR and your other armies clear of MAR, PAR and SPA this fall. France is too weak to threaten you, and I will keep my units out of German centers. Are you directing your strength against Italy rather than the French centers?

With ENGLAND and TURKEY both at eight centers, please use your eastern pressure against Italy rather than France. Keep F GRE and A BUL clear of my centers, and tell me whether you can threaten Italy’s RUM, SER or TRI this fall.

Germany to Italy: Your A TYR and A VIE are still on my border. Withdraw A TYR from Tyrolia and A VIE from Bohemia this fall, and I will keep my units off TRI and VEN. Otherwise Germany will act against Tyrolia. Confirm your exact fall orders in writing.

Germany to France: Italy's western army is the shared threat. If you move A PAR and A SPA to pressure Italy's units in BUR and MAR, I will consider A RUH to BUR. Tell me your exact fall orders first, and confirm France will not enter Germany.

Germany to Turkey: Italy's A VEN, A SER and fleets at ROM and RUM are your main target. I still cannot commit A TYR to VEN while Italian units hold Tyrolia. Send me your exact fall orders for A SMY, A CON, F NAP and A BUL so I can judge the Balkan picture.

I intend to recover Rome and avoid widening the war. F ROM will hold Rome; I propose F NAP move out and no Turkish support against Rome. I’ll keep A SER and A TRI clear of Turkish centers. Can you confirm F NAP will not attack Rome this fall?

I have no intention of attacking German centers this fall. Please keep A MUN, A VIE and A TYR away from TRI and VEN; I will keep A SER clear of BUD and A TRI clear of VIE. Let’s avoid opening a central front.
I want no Balkan clash while I recover Rome. I’ll keep A SER out of Russian centers and F BLA off SEV; please keep A WAR away from TRI and VEN and stay out of RUM this fall.

Russia to Turkey: Your F CON was to move to Bulgaria in spring, yet A BUL is still Turkish-held and you took ROM only to lose it. Show me the move this fall. If F CON and A SMY hit A BUL, A SEV stays put and I keep A RUM off your line. Tell me exactly which units go where.
I intend to press Italy this fall. What are A SEV and A MOS doing? Please keep A RUM out of Bulgaria and my centers; if you can pressure Rumania, tell me your exact orders so we can avoid a clash.
I will continue contesting your expansion this fall. Keep A SER and A TRI clear of Turkish centers, and keep your fleets away from ANK and CON. What are your plans for F ROM, F RUM, and A SER?

I have no plans against English centers this fall. Please keep your fleets clear of Turkish centers and the eastern Mediterranean. Are you continuing pressure on Italy, or are your forces turning toward another front?

England to Turkey: Thanks for the clarity. I have no plans against your centres in the eastern Mediterranean this fall. My fleets stay in the North Sea and Channel while I watch Italy's western units. I will keep F LON and F BEL off Italian centres for now. If Italy turns on you in the Adriatic or Aegean, tell me and we can discuss pressure on Italy's MAR and SPA holdings in spring.

I will order A PAR to support A RUH-BUR, A MAR to hold, and A POR to hold. France will not enter German territory. Please move A RUH-BUR as proposed and keep your other armies clear of MAR, PAR, and SPA.

My fall plan is A PAR supporting Germany’s A RUH-BUR, A MAR holding, and A POR holding. I will keep all units off English centres. Italy’s A TUS is the immediate danger to MAR; please consider pressure on Italy’s western flank next spring.

Germany to England: I will keep A MUN and A RUH out of BEL and HOL this fall as long as your F BEL, F LON, F NOR and F DEN stay out of HOL and KIE. My focus this fall is Italy's Tyrolia and Bohemia units, not your centers. Let us both keep our fleets in the North Sea and avoid a costly clash.

Germany to Italy: Your A TYR and A VIE are still on my border and I have seen no withdrawal. Give me exact fall orders for A TYR and A VIE. If they leave Tyrolia and Bohemia, I will keep my units off TRI and VEN. If not, Germany will act against Tyrolia this fall.

Germany to France: I can consider A RUH to BUR only if you commit A PAR and A SPA against Italy's western units, with A PAR moving to BUR or MAR. Send your exact fall orders first. I will not enter France, and I will not move toward your centers while you are pressuring Italy.
I will move A TYR to BOH and A VIE to GAL, keeping A TRI out of VIE and A SER out of BUD. I have no intention of attacking German centers; please keep A MUN, A VIE and A TYR away from TRI and VEN.

Confirmed: F ROM, F AEG and A VEN will not enter Spain, Marseille, Brest, Picardy or Belgium, and my western units will not move toward English or French centers. I am focused on recovering Rome. Please keep F LON and F BEL away from Italian centers.

F ROM will hold Rome; F RUM and A SER will not enter Turkish centers. I intend no attack on your centers, but I will defend Rome. Please keep your units out of Italian centers and do not support an attack on Rome.

Confirmed: A TUS and A VEN will stay out of MAR, and my fleets will stay out of SPA. I will keep my units out of French centers and have no western offensive planned. Please keep your units out of Italian centers as proposed.

Russia to Turkey: I hear your intent to press Italy, but words are cheap. Show me the move: F CON and A SMY into Bulgaria this fall, with the order shown to me before I commit. A SEV and A MOS stay put for now, and A RUM stays out of your line only while your fleets stay off Sevastopol and Moscow.

Russia to Italy: Noted. A WAR stays out of Trieste and Venice and out of Rumania this fall, provided F BLA stays off Sevastopol and A SER stays out of Russian centers. Your A BUL is the open question; if it moves toward Rumania or Sevastopol, I will respond. Keep Moscow and Warsaw clear too.

I have no unit in CON or SMY: my army is in BUL and my fleet in ANK. This fall A BUL will move to RUM; please keep A SEV and A MOS clear of my centers and avoid a clash there. What are your exact orders for A SEV and A RUM?

My fall orders are A BUL-RUM and F NAP-ROM. F ANK and F GRE will hold; I have no A SMY or A CON. I’m pressing Italy from the south and east. Please keep A TYR and A VIE from supporting Italian positions, and tell me if you’ll threaten VEN or TRI.

I can’t promise F NAP won’t attack ROM; I intend to contest your recovery. I’ll keep A SER and A TRI clear of Turkish centers, and ask that F RUM stay away from BUL and F ROM avoid NAP. We can still avoid widening the war beyond the contested fronts.

I’m pressing Italy: A BUL can threaten RUM, and F NAP can contest ROM. I have no immediate move on SER or TRI this fall. F GRE and A BUL will stay clear of French centers; please continue keeping your units clear of Turkish centers.

England to Germany: Spring 1936, I hold my Low Countries and North Sea units. Germany has been building toward Russia and Italy. Will A MUN and A KIE stay off BEL and DEN this spring? If you want English help against Italy's Tyrolia, tell me your exact spring orders in writing so we avoid a clash.

A BUR is the key to our border. Will it stay out of PAR and MAR this spring? I’ll keep my armies out of German centers if you do. Italy’s A TUS also threatens MAR; are you willing to keep pressure on Italy rather than France?

Will A TUS stay out of MAR and my other French centers this spring? France will stay out of Italian centers. With Turkey pressing in the east, let’s avoid opening a western front—please tell me your intended moves around MAR and BUR.
Please keep F BEL out of PIC and my French centers this spring. I’ll keep my armies off English centers. Italy’s A TUS threatens MAR; are you willing to help contain Italy rather than press France?

Germany to Italy: Your A TYR and A VIE still sit on my border. Withdraw from Tyrolia and Bohemia this spring and Germany keeps off TRI and VEN. Otherwise I will act against Tyrolia. Give me your exact spring orders for A TYR, A VIE, A TRI and A SER in writing.

Germany to France: Send me your exact spring orders for A PAR, A MAR and A SPA first. If France is pressing Italy's western units, I may consider A MUN to BUR with support. I will not enter France or move toward your centers.

Germany to England: I will keep A MUN and A RUH out of BEL and HOL this spring provided your F BEL, F LON, F NOR and F DEN stay out of HOL and KIE. Confirm in writing and state your spring orders for A EDI and F STP.

I want to avoid another fight over Rome while keeping my Balkan centers secure. I will keep A BUD and F RUM out of Turkish centers; will you keep F TYS and F GRE out of Italian centers and avoid supporting any attack on ROM? What are your plans for F TYS and A BUL?

I propose we avoid a Balkan clash this spring: I’ll keep A BUD and F RUM out of Russian centers, and ask that A WAR stay clear of TRI and VEN. What are your plans for A WAR and A SEV? A coordinated understanding would leave us both freer to deal with Turkey.
I have no plans against German centers. I’ll keep A TRI out of VIE and A BUD out of your centers; please keep A MUN and A VIE away from TRI and VEN. Can we maintain a quiet central front this spring?

Russia to Turkey: Your A BUL is headed for RUM, which is my space. Stop claiming intent and show me orders. Keep F ANK and A CON off Sevastopol and Moscow, and I will keep A SEV and A MOS off your centers. Tell me exactly what A ARM and F TYS do this spring.

Russia to Italy: Your A BUL and F BLA are the real problem. If A BUL moves toward Rumania or Sevastopol this spring, I will strike it. Pull A BUL out of Bulgaria and keep F BLA off Sevastopol, and A WAR stays out of Trieste and Venice. Answer now.

Russia to Germany: I will keep A WAR out of Silesia and A GAL in Galicia-facing posture, and I am not attacking Vienna. If you press Italy in Tyrolia or Bohemia, I want no German move into Warsaw or Galicia against me. Confirm your spring orders for A GAL and A VIE.

I intend to contest Italy’s F RUM from A BUL this spring. Please keep A SEV out of RUM and Bulgaria so we avoid a clash. What are A SEV, A MOS and A WAR doing? I’ll keep my forces clear of your centers.

I’m pressing Italy from the south and east. Can you threaten VEN or TRI with your northern units, or support pressure on Italy elsewhere? Please keep A VIE and A TRI from supporting Italian units; tell me your intended moves around GAL, VIE and TRI.

I intend to keep contesting your eastern positions this spring. Please keep A SER and A TRI clear of Turkish centers, and tell me whether F RUM and F AEG will defend or move. I’m willing to keep this conflict contained to the contested front if you do the same.

England to Germany: Confirmed for spring 1936. My F BEL, F LON, F NOR and F DEN hold and will not enter HOL or KIE. A EDI and F STP stay put defensively. I expect A MUN and A KIE to stay off BEL and DEN. Let us both focus on Italy's Tyrolia and Bohemia units this year.

England to France: F BEL will hold this spring and will not move to PIC. I will keep my fleets off French centres. I cannot commit to containing Italy's southern front yet, but if Italy's A TUS moves on MAR or SPA, let us discuss coordinated action in fall.

I’ll keep A PAR out of German centers and use it against Italy’s western threat. Please keep A BUR out of PAR and MAR this spring; I won’t enter BUR or other German centers. Are you moving A MUN to BUR, and will you keep your other armies clear of France?

Germany to England: Spring 1936, A KIE holds and A MUN holds. Neither moves into BEL, HOL, or DEN this spring, provided your F BEL, F DEN, and F LON stay out of HOL and KIE. A EDI and F STP are your call; I have no interest in them this turn.

Germany to Russia: A GAL holds and A VIE holds this spring. I am not moving toward Warsaw or Silesia, and I am not attacking Vienna or Galicia. Keep A WAR and A MOS clear of GAL and BOH and we stay quiet.

Germany to Italy: A TRI holds, A VIE holds, and A MUN moves to TYR this spring. I will not enter VEN or TRI. Keep your units out of Bohemia and Tyrolia and we avoid a clash. Send me your exact fall orders.
Germany to France: A BUR holds this spring. I will not move into PAR or MAR, and I have no plans against your centers. If Italy's A TUS moves on MAR, press it, and we can talk about the border later.

Germany to Turkey: A TRI holds and A VIE holds this spring. I will not threaten VEN this turn, but A MUN moves to TYR, so Italy's northern flank is under pressure. Keep your southern attack on Italy going and tell me your fall orders.

The current position has no Italian A TYR, A VIE, A TRI, or A SER, so I cannot give orders for those units. A BUD will stay out of German centers, and I have no move planned against TRI or VEN. Please keep your units away from Italian centers as well.

There is no Italian A BUL or F BLA in the current position. I have no plans for A BUD or F RUM to enter Russian centers; please keep A WAR out of TRI and VEN and A SEV away from my units. Let’s avoid a Balkan clash while Turkey remains the common problem.

A TUS will stay out of MAR and all French centers this spring. I have no western offensive planned; my attention is east. France’s A MAR and other units can likewise stay out of Italian centers, and we can keep the western front quiet.

A SER and A TRI are not in the current position. F RUM will defend rather than enter Turkish centers, and F AEG will not move against ANK or CON this spring. I want to contain the conflict, but need F TYS and F GRE to stay out of Italian centers and no support against ROM.

Russia to Italy: Your A BUL is still in Bulgaria and F RUM sits on my border. My A WAR stays out of Trieste and Venice this spring. I will hold A SEV and A MOS, but if A BUL or F RUM moves toward Rumania or Sevastopol, I will answer. Pull A BUL out of Bulgaria and keep F BLA off Sevastopol, and we can talk.

Russia to Turkey: You say you will contest F RUM from A BUL, yet you have not shown a single order against Italy. Show me F CON or A SMY moving into Bulgaria or Greece before I say anything about A SEV or A MOS. A WAR stays out of the Balkans. Keep F ANK and A CON away from Sevastopol and Moscow.

A ARM will move to SYR, and F TYS will move to ROM to pressure Italy. A BUL will attack F RUM. I’ll keep F ANK and A ARM clear of your centers. What are A SEV, A MOS and A WAR doing this spring? Please keep A SEV out of RUM and Bulgaria so our moves don’t clash.

I can’t agree to leave ROM unchallenged: F TYS will move to ROM, and A BUL will attack F RUM. F GRE will stay out of Italian centers. A ARM moves to SYR. I’ll keep A BUL out of your Balkan centers beyond the attack on RUM; please keep A BUD clear of Turkish centers.

England to Germany: Fall 1936. I hold F BEL, F LON, F NOR, F DEN, A EDI. I will not enter HOL or KIE. Please confirm A MUN and A KIE stay off BEL and DEN this fall, and tell me whether your Russian front is taking your armies east, leaving Scandinavia and the Low Countries untouched.

England to France: Italy's A TUS and A SER threaten MAR and SPA. I can move F BEL toward ENG/PIC-free support only if you confirm your A MAR and A POR hold and you will not strike my centres. Tell me your exact fall orders so we can coordinate a western push.

England to Russia: Your three centres are under pressure from Germany and Turkey. I hold the North with F STP and F NOR. Propose: you keep A WAR and A MOS off my STP and SWE approaches, and I will keep F STP out of your Gulf of Bothnia and Baltic routes. Tell me your fall orders.

A BUR is still the immediate threat to Paris. Will it hold and stay out of PAR and MAR this fall? I will keep A GAS and A BRE out of German centers if you keep A BUR and your other armies out of France. Please tell me your plan.
Please keep F BEL out of PIC and my French centers this fall. I will keep my units out of English centers. Can you confirm F BEL will hold, rather than move against France?

Turkey is still at 9 and needs containing. I’m looking at F TYS–NAP and A VIE–BUD; can you direct any available forces toward Turkish centres this spring? I’ll keep A PIC and A BUR out of BEL, HOL and DEN, and F BRE will hold.
Your nine centres remain a serious threat. I’m considering F TYS–NAP and A VIE–BUD this spring. Are you planning to move against French centres, and what are A TYR and your nearby fleets doing?

Germany to Russia: Spring 1947. I have 3 centres and need your help. A WAR holds and A MUN moves to BOH against French units. Please keep A MOS, A SEV and A RUM off WAR and VIE, and tell me whether you will push into Galicia against Turkey this spring.

Germany to Italy: Spring 1947. Venice is contested between us. I will keep A VEN where it is this spring and will not move against Trieste or Tyrolia. If you leave VEN alone, I will not attack your Adriatic or Italian positions. Tell me your spring plans.

Germany to Turkey: Spring 1947. I am not targeting your Tyrolia or Trieste units this turn. My armies are busy with France in Bohemia. If you keep A TYR away from MUN and VEN, I am open to discussing Galicia and the Russian front with you.

Turkey and you are both at 9, so neither of us can afford to let the other run away with the game. I can help contain Turkish expansion, but please keep A MAR, A VIE, and A BUR clear of Italian centers. What concrete move are you making against Turkey this spring, and can you avoid attacking NAP or TRI?

With you at 9 centers, I need a clear commitment that F TUN, F ALB, and A TYR will not move against NAP, ROM, or TRI this spring. I am prepared to discuss joint pressure on France, but will oppose any Turkish move against Italy. What are your orders around the western Mediterranean?

Turkey and France are both on 9 centers and are the immediate threats. Can you commit to a concrete move that keeps France occupied while I help contain Turkey? Please keep your fleets out of Italian centers and the Mediterranean; let me know what you intend this spring.

Russia to Turkey: Spring 1947. Southern line holds from my side: A RUM stays out of BUL and off your centres. In return, tell me plainly what A ARM and F BLA do this spring, and confirm no move on SEV or UKR. I hold SEV and MOS, and will judge you by actions.
I intend to keep F ALB and A TYR clear of TRI this spring, as agreed. Are you planning to move A TUS or F TYS, and can we keep the Italian front quiet?
I’m focused on the eastern board this spring and have no plans against French centres. Please keep A VIE and your other eastern units clear of Turkish territory; what are your plans for A VIE?

England to Italy: I will not send fleets into the Mediterranean and F NTH, F ENG stay in the North Sea and Channel this spring. I cannot pressure France beyond defending my own centres, so keep your own forces on France's southern flank. Keep your fleets out of British centres and the North Sea as promised.

England to France: Confirmed only if you put it in orders: A PIC and A BUR must not enter BEL, HOL or DEN, F BRE holds, and F TYS and A TYR stay away from ENG and the North Sea. I will keep F NTH and F ENG defensive. I will not send forces toward Turkey, but I will not allow a move on my centres.

A PIC and A BUR will stay out of BEL, HOL, and DEN; F BRE will hold. F TYS and A TYR have no plans toward ENG or the North Sea. Please keep F NTH and F ENG clear of French centres while we contain Turkey.

I’ll keep A MAR, A VIE, and A BUR out of Italian centres. My concrete anti-Turkish moves are F TYS–NAP and A VIE–BUD. Can A TUS support F TYS into NAP? Please keep your other units clear of those moves; I’ll avoid VEN and TRI.

A VIE will move to BUD; I’m also considering F TYS–NAP. I have no plans against your other centres this spring, but I will contest Turkish expansion. Keep your forces out of French centres and tell me whether A TYR or your nearby fleets intend to move against France.

Germany to England: Spring 1947. I hold A WAR and A MUN and A VEN for now. A MUN is moving to BOH against France, not north. A VEN stays put this spring, and A WAR holds. I will keep A BER, A MUN and A WAR away from DEN, SWE and HOL. Keep F NTH, F SWE and F STP away from my centres, and we can talk about Kiel later.
I will leave A VEN alone this spring and keep my forces clear of German positions. Please maintain your commitment not to move against TRI or TYR; I will not support any attack on VEN.

I plan to keep A TUS and F NAP clear of Turkish centers this spring, but I cannot promise the entire Italian front quiet while Turkish forces can threaten my centers. Keep F ALB and A TYR clear of TRI, and keep F TUN clear of NAP and ROM; I will not support attacks on you.
I can support F TYS–NAP with A TUS, provided you confirm that F TYS is moving to NAP and A VIE is moving to BUD. I will keep A ROM and A APU clear of your moves, and will not move against VEN or TRI.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1947. Your Bohemia move is still only words until it succeeds. I keep A MOS, A SEV and A RUM off WAR and VIE this spring. I will not push into Galicia while you show nothing against France. Take BOH, then we will talk about Turkey.
The southern line holds: A ARM will hold and F BLA will move to CON. Neither will move toward SEV or UKR, and A RUM remains clear of BUL. I expect us both to keep the border quiet.

A TYR will not move against MUN or VEN this spring. I have no present plan to enter Galicia or attack Russia; my forces are focused on the eastern Mediterranean. Let me know if you need coordination against France.

F TUN, F ALB, and A TYR will not move against NAP, ROM, or TRI this spring. I’m willing to keep the Italian front quiet, but I need your assurance you won’t support French moves against Turkish centers. What are A TUS and F TYS doing?

I am not moving against French centres this spring. A TYR will stay clear of French and Italian centres, and my nearby fleets are focused east. I will oppose A VIE–BUD; please keep A VIE out of Turkish territory and tell me where it will move.

England to France: Fall 1947. You hold 9 centres with A BER, A MUN area and BEL adjacent to my units. Your A PIC and A BUR must not enter BEL, HOL or DEN. Do you still hold F BRE and F TYS, and where is A BER now? Put exact orders in writing.

England to Germany: Fall 1947. You have 3 centres and A KIE, A VEN, A WAR near my Baltic and northern centres. Tell me your exact fall moves. If A WAR or A KIE moves toward SWE, DEN or HOL, I will respond. Keep A BER away from DEN and HOL and I will keep F NTH and F STP off your centres.

England to Turkey: Fall 1947. You are at 9 centres. I have no fleets moving south. Keep F ADR, F AEG and F NAF away from TUN, NAP and the North Sea, and tell me whether you plan any move against Italy or England this fall.

Turkey remains the main threat, but I need centers to catch up. Will A TUS support F TYS–NAP this fall? I’ll keep A MAR, A VIE and A MUN clear of Italian centers; please keep A ROM and A APU clear of NAP and coordinate with me.

With both of us at nine, this turn decides who gets the lead. Are you moving against French centers or supporting an attack on my eastern units? I intend to contest your expansion; propose a concrete way to keep our units out of each other’s centers this fall.

I’ll keep A PIC and A MUN out of HOL and DEN, and F BRE clear of English centers this fall. In return, keep F NTH and your other fleets out of French centers. I’m focused east and will not move against your centers this turn.

Germany to Russia: Fall 1947. I have 3 centres and no more time for words. A MUN is taking BOH from France this fall, and A WAR holds. Your A MOS, A SEV and A RUM must stay off WAR and VIE. If you take Galicia from Turkey with me, I will support you there next spring. Confirm now.

Germany to England: Fall 1947. A WAR, A MUN and A VEN hold or move against France and Italy, not your centres. Keep F NTH, F SWE and F STP away from BER, WAR and KIE. I will not touch DEN or HOL. Tell me what F NTH and A LVP intend for the North Sea this fall.

Germany to France: Fall 1947. A MUN moves to BOH this fall and I will not enter your Silesia or Bohemia units' centres beyond that. Keep A BUD and A GAS away from VIE and MUN. If you want peace in the west, hold your Burgundy and Ruhr units and I will keep A BER off BEL and PAR.

F TYS–NAP threatens my center and would dislodge my fleet. I will not support it. Please keep F TYS out of NAP this fall; if you instead commit to a concrete move against Turkey, I can consider coordinating while keeping A TUS clear of your centers.

The balance is still tight at 9 centers each, and France’s F TYS threatens NAP. Are you actually keeping your forces clear of Italy this fall? I will not support attacks on your centers without a concrete reciprocal commitment, and I will defend NAP, ROM, and TRI against any move.

With France at 9 and Turkey at 9, we should prevent either from gaining the final centers. Are you keeping A VEN clear of TRI this fall? I will not attack VEN; please tell me whether you can hold against French pressure and avoid Italian positions.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1947. You have A ARM, F BLA and A VIE near my southern border. Tell me plainly which of them move this fall. I hold SEV, UKR and MOS. If your fleets stay out of the Black Sea and A VIE stays off Galicia, my A RUM stays out of BUL. Judge us by actions.

With both of us at nine centres, neither can afford a quiet stalemate. What are your plans for A BUD and A BER this fall? I’m prepared to keep my forces clear of French centres if you will keep A BUD out of Turkish territory and avoid supporting attacks on my centres.

You’re one centre from nine, and France is tied with me at nine. Can we coordinate to contain France this fall? Tell me your plans for F STP/NORTH and F SWE; I can discuss pressure on France from the east, but I won’t leave my own centres exposed.

France is the immediate threat to both of us. Can you coordinate pressure on its eastern holdings this fall? Please tell me your plans for A KIE and A WAR; I can apply pressure from the Balkans, but need to know whether you’ll contest French positions.

England to Germany: Fall 1947. I will keep F NTH, F SWE and F STP off your centres, including BER, WAR and KIE, as long as you make no move into DEN, SWE or HOL. A WAR, A KIE and A VEN should hold or head against France and Italy. Confirm your exact orders in writing and I will do the same.

England to Turkey: Fall 1947. I have no fleets moving south and will keep F NTH, F NWG and F STP out of the Mediterranean. Your F ADR, F AEG and F NAF should stay away from TUN, NAP and any British centre. I am not interested in coordinating against France this fall; I am focused on my own northern centres.

England to France: Fall 1947. Your word that A PIC and A BUR stay out of BEL, HOL and DEN is noted. I expect F BRE and F TYS to hold position and no French unit to enter the North Sea or English centres. Confirm your exact orders in writing; I will keep F NTH and F ENG defensive while you do.

F BRE and F TYS are still where they were, and A BER is in BER. This fall A PIC and A MUN will stay out of HOL and DEN, and F BRE will stay clear of English centres. I will not move against your centres; please keep F NTH and your other fleets out of French centres.

A BUD and A GAS will stay out of VIE and MUN. I have A MUN in MUN, so your proposed A MUN–BOH cannot be made from the position shown; please keep A KIE out of French centres. I’m willing to keep A BER out of BEL and PAR and avoid a western fight.

A BER remains in BER. I intend to move A BUD to SER and keep it out of VIE; I will not support attacks on your centres. I cannot promise a quiet stalemate while we are tied at nine, but I will keep my other units clear of French and Turkish centres this fall.

Understood: F TYS will stay out of NAP. I’ll keep A MAR, A VIE and A MUN clear of Italian centres. Please keep A ROM and A APU clear of NAP and my units, and consider coordinating against Turkey; F TYS can pressure TUN instead.

Germany to England: Fall 1947. A WAR holds, A VEN holds, A KIE holds this fall. I am not moving toward DEN, SWE or HOL. A MUN goes to BOH against France. Keep F NTH, F STP and F SWE off BER, WAR and KIE and we stay at peace in the north.

Germany to Turkey: Fall 1947. I agree France is the main danger. A MUN takes BOH this fall, and A KIE and A WAR hold. I can press French positions in the west later, but I cannot move this fall beyond Bohemia. Keep A TYR away from MUN and VEN and we can coordinate in spring.

Germany to Italy: Fall 1947. A VEN holds this fall and will not move to TRI. I will not attack your Adriatic or Italian positions. Keep A TUS and A APU away from VEN and we are fine. Against France we should coordinate in spring, not now.

I will not support F TYS–NAP, and A ROM and A APU will stay clear of NAP as requested. Please keep F TYS out of NAP and A MAR, A VIE, and A MUN out of Italian centers. If you are making a concrete move against Turkey, give me the target and orders; I can consider coordination, but I will not enable an attack on my own NAP.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1947. I hear you but see no result yet. Your A MUN to BOH is an attack on France, not on me. I will hold A MOS, A SEV and A UKR and keep A RUM out of WAR and VIE this fall. Show me BOH taken and I will consider Galicia with you next spring. Until then, no confirmation.

A ARM will hold and A VIE will not move to Galicia or any Russian centre. F BLA will remain out of the Black Sea. In return, keep A RUM out of BUL and do not support attacks on Turkish centres; we can keep this border quiet while dealing with the western threat.

I have no plans against England or its centres this fall. F ADR and F AEG will stay clear of TUN and NAP, and F NAF will not move toward England or the North Sea. France is the immediate threat; will you pressure its northern centres while I contain it from the east?

I propose a clean separation this fall: my forces will not enter French centres, and you keep A BUD out of Turkish territory and do not support attacks on Turkish centres. Tell me whether A BUD and A BER will stay clear of my holdings. I will oppose any move into them.

I will keep F ADR, F AEG, and F NAF clear of NAP, ROM, and TUN this fall, and A VIE clear of TRI. In return, do not support attacks on Turkish centres. France’s F TYS is the immediate threat to NAP; I will not assist France against you.

England to France: Spring 1948. Your A BER, A KIE and A PAR sit close to my northern centres. Put in writing that A KIE and A BER do not move into DEN, HOL or BEL, and that F BRE and F GOL do not enter ENG or NTH. I will keep F NTH, F SWE and F STP off your centres in return.

I’m focused on the east and Germany, not your centres. I’ll keep French units out of BEL, HOL, DEN, and English waters this spring. Please keep your fleets clear of French centres; where are F NTH and F ENG moving?

Please keep A VIE and A RUM out of BUD and keep your fleets clear of French centres. I intend to defend my eastern position and press Germany rather than enter Turkish centres. What are your exact plans for A VIE and the nearby fleets?
I’m not moving against VEN or TRI this spring. Please keep A TUS clear of VEN and coordinate against Turkish expansion if you can; what are your plans for APU and your fleets this turn?

Germany to Russia: Spring 1948. A RUH moves to MUN to retake it from France. A WAR and A VEN hold. Keep A MOS and A SEV off WAR. Let us coordinate: you take Rumania (RUM) with A SEV while I hold the centre. Confirm in writing whether you will stay off WAR this spring.

Germany to England: Spring 1948. A RUH moves to MUN against France, not north. A WAR holds. Keep F NTH, F STP and F SWE away from BER, WAR and KIE and I will do the same toward DEN, SWE and HOL. Tell me your North Sea moves.

Germany to Turkey: Spring 1948. A RUH to MUN targets France, not you. A VEN holds. Keep A VIE and A TYR off VEN and MUN and I will stay off Tyrolia and Trieste. Tell me your spring plans against Russia or France.

Your F ADR can move to VEN and F WES can pressure TYS, so please confirm both stay clear of Italian centers this spring. I will keep A APU, F NAP, and A TUS out of Turkish centers and will not support French attacks on Turkey if you maintain this nonaggression.

Please keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian territory and do not move F GOL to TYS. My A TUS, A APU, and F NAP will hold clear of your centers. What are your concrete plans for the southern units this spring?

Can you keep A VEN out of TRI and other Italian positions this spring? I will leave A VEN alone and keep my units clear of your centers. Please let me know if France is threatening VEN or your other southern positions.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1948. Your Bohemia attacks have not shown results, and France is still a threat to us both. I will hold MOS, SEV and UKR. If you want Galicia talk, show me WAR secure and BOH taken this spring, then we can discuss Turkey's VIE.

Russia to Turkey: Spring 1948. Tell me plainly what A VIE, A ARM and F BLA do this spring. I hold SEV, MOS and UKR and will not attack your centres. Any move into Galicia or Ukraine ends our line, and A RUM stays out of BUL as long as your fleets stay out of the Black Sea.

Russia to France: Spring 1948. Your fleets have been weakened by Portugal's loss and I see no reason for hostility between us. If you keep A BUD and A BUR away from Galicia and Ukraine, I will keep my forces out of Silesia and Prussia. Confirm your intentions for A KIE and A BER.

Your A BUD sits on the key line into VIE and SER. What are A BUD and A BER doing this spring? I am considering pressure on BUD; if you keep clear of Turkish centres and do not support attacks on them, tell me whether you will keep A BUD out of VIE and SER.

France is the strongest immediate obstacle to both our expansion. Can you pressure its eastern position with A WAR toward SIL or BER this spring while I threaten BUD from VIE/RUM? Please say plainly where A WAR and A RUH are going; I will keep A VIE clear of your centres.

I want the Italian front quiet while I deal with France. Will A APU, F NAP, and A TUS stay clear of Turkish centres, and will you avoid supporting attacks on them? I can keep F ADR away from TRI this spring if we agree to mutual restraint.

England to France: Spring 1948. I will not put my fleets on your centres, but I cannot accept vague promises. Put exact orders in writing: A KIE and A BER do not move into DEN, HOL or BEL, and F BRE and F GOL stay out of ENG and NTH. Until I see that, F NTH and F SWE stay where they are.

England to Germany: Spring 1948. F NTH holds in the North Sea this spring and F STP and F SWE stay away from BER, WAR and KIE, as long as you make no move into DEN, SWE or HOL. Confirm A WAR and A RUH stay out of those three northern centres in writing and I will do the same.
A BER and A KIE will stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL; F BRE and F GOL will stay out of ENG and NTH. I’m pressing east and Germany. Please keep F NTH, F SWE and F STP clear of French centres.
