A BUD and A BUR will stay away from Galicia and Ukraine. A KIE and A BER will not move into Silesia or Prussia; I’m focused on Germany and will keep them clear of your centres. Please keep your forces out of French territory.

A MAR and F GOL will stay out of Italian territory, and F GOL will not move to TYS. I’m keeping the southern units defensive and focused east; please keep A TUS, A APU and F NAP clear of French centres.

A BER will not enter Turkish centres. I’m not promising to leave A BUD out of VIE or SER; I need room to defend my eastern position. Please keep A VIE and A RUM out of BUD and your fleets clear of French centres.

Germany to Russia: A WAR holds this spring and A VEN holds. A RUH moves to MUN to retake it from France. Keep A MOS and A SEV off WAR. Please take RUM with A SEV while I hold the centre. I will talk Galicia once WAR and MUN are secure, and I will not attack MOS or SEV.

Germany to Italy: A VEN holds this spring and will not move to TRI or any Italian position. A RUH goes to MUN against France. Keep your units off VEN and TYR, and we stay at peace in the south. We can coordinate against France later.

Germany to Turkey: A RUH to MUN targets France, not you. A WAR and A VEN hold. I will not move toward SIL or BER this spring, so WAR stays where it is. Keep A VIE and A TYR off VEN and MUN, and I will stay off Tyrolia and Trieste. Pressure BUD from your side as you see fit.

I’ll keep A APU, F NAP, and A TUS out of French centers this spring. My fleets will defend Italian waters, not move against you. Please keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian territory, especially TYS and NAP, and tell me your concrete plans against Turkey.

I’ll keep A APU, F NAP, and A TUS clear of Turkish centers and won’t support attacks on them, provided F ADR stays clear of TRI and other Italian centers. Keep F WES away from TYS as well; I’ll keep the Italian front defensive this spring.

Russia to Germany: Spring 1948. I will keep A MOS and A SEV off WAR this spring as long as WAR and VEN stay Germanys and you do not move against my centres. Taking RUM with A SEV is not my plan. Your RUH to MUN is an attack on France, not me, and I will judge by results. Show me MUN retaken and we can talk about Turkey's VIE.

I have no A ARM or F BLA on the board. A VIE will move to BUD, with A RUM supporting; A RUM will stay out of BUL. My fleets will stay out of the Black Sea, and I will not move into Galicia or Ukraine.

A VIE will move to BUD, with A RUM supporting; I will keep A VIE off VEN and MUN and avoid your centres. My move is against France’s eastern position, not Russia. I appreciate A RUH pressing MUN; I will stay off Tyrolia and Trieste.

F ADR and F WES will hold this spring, staying clear of VEN, TYS, and your other centres. A VIE will stay out of TRI. I will not support attacks on Italian centres, and ask that you likewise avoid Turkish centres and supporting attacks on them.

A VIE will move to BUD, supported by A RUM; BUD is the French position I intend to contest. A RUM will not enter BUD, and my fleets will stay clear of French centres. I will keep A VIE out of SER and your other Turkish-border holdings.

England to France, Fall 1948: Your A KIE, A BER and A MUN are near my northern centres. Please confirm in writing that none of your units enter DEN, HOL or BEL this fall, and that F MAO stays out of ENG and the Irish Sea. I will keep F NTH and F STP defensive in return. Your fleets in the west should not move against LVP or EDI.

England to Germany, Fall 1948: Your A RUH and A WAR are no threat to my fleets if they stay out of DEN, SWE and HOL. I have F NTH and F STP holding this fall and I will not enter BER, WAR or KIE. Confirm your exact fall orders in writing so we both know where we stand.

England to Turkey, Fall 1948: I have no fleets moving south and will keep F NTH and F NWG out of the Mediterranean. Your F NAF and F EAS should stay away from TUN and any British centre. If you are pressing France or Italy, tell me which units are moving so we avoid collisions.

Your A VIE has taken BUD, and my A GAL is now exposed. Do not advance into GAL or my other centres this fall; I will keep A BER out of your centres. What are your orders for A VIE, A RUM, and the fleets near me?

Turkey is the immediate threat on my eastern flank. Please use A TUS and your fleets to pressure Turkish centres rather than mine; I will keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian territory. What concrete move can you make against Turkey this fall?

I will keep my units out of BEL, HOL, DEN, and English waters this fall. Please keep your fleets clear of French centres. I am focused east and on securing MUN; will you maintain the western separation?

Germany to France: Fall 1948. Your A MUN is in MUN and my A RUH was voided, so Germany is weak. I want no fight in the west. Tell me plainly what A MUN, A BER and A KIE do this fall. If you pull A MUN out of Germany's home, I will keep A WAR and A VEN off French centres.

Italy needs room to grow, and VEN is the clearest opportunity. Would you move A VEN to MUN this fall and allow A TUS to take VEN? I can keep F ION and A APU away from your other centers; please confirm your plan.
Please confirm F ALB and F AEG will stay out of ION and my Italian centers this fall. I need to keep F ION secure. I will keep A APU and A TUS clear of Turkish centers if you maintain that restraint.

Please keep F GOL and your armies out of Italian centers this fall, especially TYS and VEN. Are you moving against Turkey, or holding your southern units? I need clarity before deciding whether I can keep my forces defensive.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1948. Your A VIE moved to BUD last spring and I see A ARM and F BLA are gone, so the board is shifting. I hold SEV, MOS and UKR. Tell me plainly what A RUM and your remaining units do this fall. If Turkey keeps off SEV and UKR, I keep my forces out of your centres.

Russia to Germany: Fall 1948. You still show no result against France after several seasons. Show me MUN retaken this fall and WAR secure, and I will discuss Galicia. Until then my A MOS, A SEV and A UKR stay put.

Russia to France: Fall 1948. Thank you for keeping A BUD and A KIE clear of Galicia and Ukraine. I will keep my forces out of Silesia and Prussia while you stay out of my centres. Tell me whether A BUR or A MUN will push against Germany this fall.

A BUD is now in my hands after your move to GAL. I will hold BUD and keep my fleets out of your centres this fall if you keep A GAL out of BUD and avoid Turkish centres. Can you agree? I will otherwise reinforce BUD and press your eastern line.

Turkey is focused east and will keep its fleets clear of British centres. Please confirm F NTH and F STP will not move against Turkish centres or into the Mediterranean this fall; I have no interest in opening a northern front.

France remains the common obstacle. I intend to secure BUD and pressure its eastern units; can you use A RUH or A WAR to threaten a French centre this fall? I will keep Turkish units clear of MUN and VEN.

England to Turkey, Fall 1948: F NTH and F STP will hold this fall and stay out of the Mediterranean. I will not move against Turkish centres. Please keep F NAF and F EAS away from TUN and British centres as you said. Tell me if A BUD or A RUM are heading west toward Italy or Austria, so we avoid collisions.

England to France, Fall 1948: I want exact written orders. Confirm A KIE, A BER and A MUN do not enter DEN, HOL or BEL, and F MAO stays out of ENG and the Irish Sea. Your fleets must not move against LVP or EDI. If you confirm this, F NTH and F STP stay defensive this fall.

A MUN will stay in MUN this fall; A BER and A KIE will not move against your centers. I am not seeking a western fight, but I cannot promise to withdraw A MUN while Turkey threatens my eastern position.

Confirmed: no French unit will enter DEN, HOL, or BEL, and F MAO will stay out of ENG and the Irish Sea. My western fleets will not move against LVP or EDI. Please keep F NTH and F STP defensive and clear of French centres.

A MUN will remain focused on Germany; A BUR will not move against your centres. I appreciate your commitment to stay out of Silesia and Prussia. Please keep A MOS and A SEV away from my positions while I manage the Turkish pressure.

I will keep A GAL out of BUD and out of Turkish centres this fall, and A BER will stay clear as well. Please hold your units short of GAL and my other centres. I need a stable eastern line rather than another advance against me.

A MAR and F GOL will stay out of Italian centres, including VEN and TYS. I am focused on containing Turkey from my eastern position, not attacking you. Please keep A TUS, A APU, and F NAP clear of my centres; pressure on Turkey would help us both.

Germany to England, Fall 1948: My fall orders are A WAR holds, A VEN holds, A RUH stays in RUH. None of my units enter DEN, SWE, HOL, BER, KIE or WAR's northern neighbours. Keep F NTH, F STP and F SWE off my centres and we remain at peace. Please confirm you will not move toward KIE or BER.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1948: A WAR holds this fall and I will not move against MOS, SEV or UKR. Keep A MOS, A SEV and A UKR off WAR and we are fine. Turkey's VIE is their business, not mine. I will discuss Galicia once MUN is retaken.

Germany to Turkey, Fall 1948: I hear your push on BUD. A WAR and A VEN hold this fall and A RUH stays home, so I cannot threaten France directly yet. Keep A VIE and any units off VEN, MUN and TYR and I will stay off your centres. Tell me your spring plan.

Germany to Italy, Fall 1948: No, A VEN stays put and will not move to MUN, and I will not let TUS take VEN. Keep A TUS and A APU out of VEN and TYR and we remain at peace. France is the threat to both of us; let us coordinate against it in spring.

This fall I can move A TUS–VEN while F ION holds, with A APU supporting the fleet if Turkey tests it. I cannot make a credible attack on a Turkish centre from my current positions without exposing Italy. Please use your eastern units to pressure Turkey; I’ll keep A MAR and F GOL clear of Italian centres as you promised.

Understood. F NAF and F EAS will stay clear of British centres, and I have no plans to move into the Mediterranean from the south this fall. My pressure is directed eastward against France, not north or west.

A RUM will support A BUD holding; A BUD will hold, and A ARM will move to ANK. My fleets will stay out of the Black Sea, and I will keep A RUM and the rest of my units off SEV and UKR. Please keep A MOS and A SEV clear of Turkish centres.

A BUD will hold, A RUM will support it, and A ARM will move to ANK. My fleets near you will stay clear of French centres; I will not advance into GAL this fall. Keep A GAL out of BUD and your units clear of Turkish centres, and we can avoid further escalation.
F ALB and F AEG will stay out of ION and away from Italian centres this fall. I will not support attacks on Italy. Please keep A APU and A TUS clear of Turkish centres, as agreed.

England to Turkey, Spring 1949: You lead on 10 centres and I will not help you reach 18. Your F SMY and F SYR are heading east, so I expect no move on TUN or NAP. If you go after Italy's VEN or ROM, tell me now. Confirm no Turkish fleet enters the western Mediterranean this spring.

England to France, Spring 1949: Turkey is the runaway leader and France is the natural counterweight. I will keep F NTH and F STP off French centres if you keep A PIC, A BUR and F POR off LVP, EDI and LON. Will you join me in checking Turkey's western advance? Confirm your spring orders in writing.

England to Italy: Your VEN, NAP and ROM are under pressure from Turkey's TRI and TUN. I can offer no fleet moves against you while you hold. Tell me whether A APU and A VEN are holding or moving north, and whether you will coordinate against Turkish advances in the Adriatic.

Turkey is close to victory, so I cannot leave your advance unchecked. What are A BUD, A SER, and F TRI doing this spring? I am prepared to discuss a stable line, but need you to keep out of VIE and stop pressing my eastern positions.

I will keep my units out of DEN, HOL, BEL, and English waters this spring, and will not threaten LVP or EDI. Please keep F NTH and F STP clear of French centres; with Turkey near victory, neither of us benefits from a western fight.
Turkey is at 10 centers and must be checked. If A VEN attacks TRI, I can support that attack with A VIE. Can you commit A VEN–TRI this spring? I will keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian centers.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1949: Turkey has 10 centres and is the only power close to 18. I have one unit, A WAR, and cannot hold alone. Let us both stay out of each other's centres and coordinate against Turkey's push into Serbia and Hungary. Will you move A MOS or A SEV toward Galicia or Rumania this spring?

Germany to Turkey, Spring 1949: You lead with 10 centres, and your units in BUD and VIE are the main threat to everyone. I will keep A WAR at home and stay out of Tyrolia, Trieste and Venice. Tell me plainly what A BUD, A VIE and F TRI do this spring and whether you will leave Galicia and Silesia alone.

Germany to France, Spring 1949: A MUN sits in Germany's last home centre, and I still have A WAR. Tell me whether A MUN, A BER and A KIE will move against Germany this spring. If you keep them out of WAR and MUN, I will keep A WAR out of French centres and help check Turkey in the south.

Turkey is at 10 and can win with eight more centers. What concrete moves are you making against it this spring? I can send F ION toward TUN, but need assurance your southern units will stay out of Italian centers and that you’ll pressure Turkey rather than Italy.

You lead at 10, with France and England at 9; further expansion risks uniting everyone against you. Confirm F WES and F SYR will stay clear of Italian centers and tell me your spring orders near Italy. I may send F ION toward TUN if you threaten my position.

Turkey is at 10 and approaching a win. Are you and France coordinating to contain it this spring? I can pressure TUN with F ION, but need to know whether England will take concrete action against Turkish centers rather than leave Italy exposed.

Russia to Turkey: Spring 1949. Turkey leads at 10 centres and is the threat to everyone. Tell me plainly whether A RUM-area, A BUD or any unit moves toward Galicia, Ukraine or Sevastopol this spring. Russia is not interested in a Turkish win, so I need concrete answers before I commit south.

Your A VIE remains the immediate issue. What are your plans for A VIE and A MUN this spring? I can keep my fleets clear of French centres, but I will not leave A TRI and A BUD idle while your army remains in Vienna.

I’m keeping our mutual-restraint agreement: F GRE and F WES will stay clear of Italian centres, and I won’t support attacks on them. Please confirm A VEN and A APU will stay clear of Turkish centres and that Italy won’t support attacks on them.

France controls BER, KIE and MUN, while your A WAR is positioned to pressure them. Will you move A WAR toward BER or support an attack on a French centre this spring? I’m preparing pressure on France from the east and will keep my units clear of VEN and MUN.

England to Italy: Spring 1949. I will not move fleets against your centres this spring. A APU and A VEN holding is wise given Turkish pressure. I will not commit to concrete action against Turkey in the Mediterranean; my fleets are needed in the North. Coordinate directly with France on the west, and keep F ION ready to defend TUN and NAP.

England to France, Spring 1949. Your written assurance is welcome but I need exact orders: confirm A PIC, A BUR and F POR do not move toward LVP, EDI or LON, and that A BER, A KIE and A MUN stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL. If you confirm, F NTH and F STP stay defensive this spring. Turkey's advance is a shared concern, but I will decide my fleet moves once I see your orders in writing.

Agreed: A PIC, A BUR, and F POR will stay out of LVP, EDI, and LON; no French unit will enter English waters. I’ll focus east against Turkey. Please keep F NTH and F STP clear of French centres and use your position to contest Turkey rather than France.

I can keep A BER and A KIE out of WAR and MUN this spring, and A MUN will not attack your centres. Please keep A WAR out of French centres and help contain Turkey. I cannot promise to leave MUN permanently; Turkey’s advance makes a secure eastern line essential.

I will keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian centres. Please send A VEN–TRI; I’ll use A VIE to support the attack. Turkey’s 10 centres make stopping it our priority. I’ll also direct my other eastern units against Turkish positions rather than Italian centres.

A VIE will remain focused on containing your advance; I cannot leave Vienna exposed while you hold BUD and TRI. I expect A BUD and A SER to stay out of my centres and F TRI not to attack VIE. I’m coordinating with Italy to contest TRI, so a mutual restraint line is preferable to escalation.

Germany to Turkey: A WAR will not move toward BER this spring. I hold WAR and will not support attacks on French centres. Your A BUD, A VIE and F TRI are the real danger to Galicia and Silesia, so tell me plainly whether they move against Russia or me. I stay out of Tyrolia, Trieste and Venice as long as you keep clear of WAR and Silesia.

I’ll coordinate against Turkey. A APU and A VEN are not moving north this spring; I’m considering A VEN–TRI, with French support, and F ION toward TUN if it can do so without exposing NAP. Please take concrete action against Turkish centers and tell me your target.
I commit A VEN–TRI, and ask A VIE to support it. I’ll keep A APU clear of French centers. Please also use your eastern units to pressure Turkey and keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian territory.

Your 10 centers make restraint untenable. I cannot promise A VEN and A APU will stay clear of Turkish centers: A VEN may attack TRI, and F ION may move against TUN. I will not support attacks on other Turkish centers; keep F WES and F GRE clear of Italy.

Russia to Germany, Spring 1949: I agree Turkey is the danger. I will not move A MOS or A SEV into Galicia or Rumania this spring. Keep A WAR where it is and I will keep MOS and SEV off WAR. If you help block Turkey's push toward Hungary and Serbia, we can talk about Galicia and Rumania next year, after you show results against Turkish units.

A RUM will support A SER; A BUD will move to VIE, and A SER will support it. I will leave Galicia, Ukraine and Sevastopol alone this spring. Keep A MOS and A SEV out of Rumania and my centres, and we can avoid a war on that front.

F WES and F SYR will stay clear of Italian centres, and no Turkish fleet will enter the western Mediterranean this spring. I am not moving on TUN or NAP. I cannot promise that my campaign against France will stay contained indefinitely, but I have no immediate move on VEN or ROM.

A BUD moves to VIE, A SER supports that move, and F TRI supports A SER holding. I will leave Galicia and Silesia alone this spring. Your staying clear of my centres is helpful; if A WAR can pressure BER, that would divide France’s attention.

F WES and F SYR will stay clear of Italian centres this spring, and I will not support an attack on them. I am not moving on Italy. Please keep A VEN and A APU clear of Turkish centres and do not support attacks on them.

A BUD moves to VIE, A SER supports it, and F TRI supports A SER holding. I am not advancing into your other eastern positions this spring, but I will not leave VIE uncontested while your army remains there. What are A VIE and A MUN doing?

England to Turkey, Fall 1949: You are at 10 and closing on 18, which I cannot allow. Tell me now whether F WES, F EAS or A BUD are heading toward TUN, NAP or ROM. Lift your pressure off Italy and I can keep my fleets in the North, but I will not sit idle while you take Italian centres.

England to France, Fall 1949: Turkey is the real danger. Confirm in writing that A PIC, A BUR and F POR stay off LVP, EDI and LON, and that A MUN, A BER and A KIE stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL. If you press Turkey's western flank in Italy or Trieste, I will keep my northern fleets defensive and not strike French centres.

England to Italy, Fall 1949: Hold A VEN and A APU this fall and keep F ION ready to defend TUN and NAP. I will not move against you. If you attack Turkish TRI or SER, tell me the exact orders so I can judge whether my fleets can help elsewhere.

Turkey is at 10 and has fleets in WES and AEG. I’ll keep French units out of your centres and English waters. Please use your fleets to pressure Turkish positions this turn rather than France—what are F NTH and F STP doing?
We need to stop Turkey’s growth. Can A VEN attack TRI again? I’ll have A VIE support it if it is still in position; please keep A APU and A VEN out of French centres. What are your exact orders?

Your 10 centres make further expansion an immediate threat to all of us. What are A BUD, A SER and F TRI doing this turn? I’m prepared to discuss restraint, but will defend Vienna and coordinate against Turkish centres if you press it.

Germany to Turkey: You lead with 10 centres and need 8 more, so I cannot ignore your growth. Tell me plainly if A VIE and F TRI will stay out of Galicia, Silesia, Tyrolia and Bohemia this fall. I will keep A WAR at home and not support French centres, but I need a clear answer.

Turkey has 10 centers and remains the immediate threat. I can renew A VEN–TRI this fall; will A VIE support it again? Please keep your southern units out of Italian centers and direct nearby armies against Turkish positions.

Your forces still threaten my position from TRI and TUN. Are F TRI and F WES moving against Italian centers this fall? I will keep A APU and F ION defensive if you stay clear of NAP and ROM; otherwise I will continue opposing your expansion.

Turkey remains at 10 and has forces near Italy. Can you take any concrete action against Turkish centers this fall, or are your fleets committed in the north? I am coordinating with France and need to know whether I can count on pressure elsewhere.

Russia to Turkey: Turkey is at 10 centres and I will not let you run away with the game. Your fleets have moved west, and A RUM and A BUD are on my border. Tell me plainly now: will A RUM or A SER move against Rumania, Galicia or Sevastopol in Fall 1949? If not, I will keep A MOS and A SEV home.

Your A VIE and A BOH threaten my line, and I need room to expand. Will A VIE leave Vienna this fall and will you keep A BOH out of BUD? I can keep my fleets clear of French centres this turn, but I will contest Vienna if you hold it.

You warned that A VEN may attack TRI and F ION may move against TUN. Keep both clear of Turkish centres this fall and I will keep F WES and F GRE clear of Italy. If you attack TRI or TUN, I will treat our restraint agreement as over.

I have no immediate move on English centres, and F WES will stay out of the western Mediterranean this fall. I am pressing for space in the east; please keep your fleets clear of Turkish centres and avoid coordinating attacks on my line.

England to Italy: Fall 1949. My northern fleets are committed to containing the French and Germans, so I cannot move against Turkey in the Mediterranean this fall. Hold VEN and APU, keep F ION ready for TUN and NAP. Coordinate with France directly; if you strike TRI or SER, send exact orders and I will consider what my fleets can do next season.

England to Turkey: F WES and F EAS heading west or toward TUN, NAP or ROM is a red line for me. You are at 10 and I will not watch you reach 18. Give me exact orders for F WES, F EAS and A BUD this fall. Vague assurances are no longer enough.

England to France: Turkey is the real danger, yet your A BUR and A PIC still sit near my western coast. Confirm in writing this turn that A PIC, A BUR and F POR do not move toward LVP, EDI or LON, and A MUN, A BER, A KIE stay out of DEN, HOL, BEL. Then I will keep F NTH and F STP defensive and press Turkey.

Confirmed: A PIC, A BUR and F MAO will stay off LVP, EDI and LON; A BER and A RUH will stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL. I’m pressing Turkey from the east and south. Keep F NTH and F STP defensive and use them against Turkey, not French centres.

Yes—A VIE will support A VEN–TRI again. A MAR and F PIE will stay out of Italian centres, and I’ll direct my eastern armies against Turkey. Please keep A APU clear of French territory and attack TRI as committed.

A VIE will remain in Vienna and A BOH will not move to BUD. I cannot leave your advance unchecked; I’ll coordinate pressure on TRI and your western flank. Keep A BUD and A SER out of French centres and your fleets clear of French territory, and we can avoid a wider war.

I intend A VEN–TRI, with French support, while A APU holds and F ION moves toward TUN. Turkey's threat is immediate, so I cannot simply hold. Please use any available fleet pressure against Turkish centers rather than leave the containment effort to France and Italy.

Your forces at TRI and WES threaten Italian territory, so I will not accept restraint on your terms. I intend A VEN–TRI and F ION–TUN; A APU will hold. If you keep F WES and F GRE away from Italian centers, I will avoid other Turkish centers this turn.

I intend A VEN–TRI again, and ask A VIE to support the attack. A APU will hold and F ION will move toward TUN. I will keep A APU out of French centers; please keep your southern units out of Italy and direct them against Turkey.
A RUM and A SER will not attack Rumania, Galicia, or Sevastopol this fall. Keep A MOS and A SEV home, and we can avoid opening another front while I deal with the western pressure.

F WES, F EAS, and A BUD are not heading for TUN, NAP, or ROM this fall. I’m keeping F WES out of the western Mediterranean; please keep your fleets clear of Turkish centres and do not coordinate attacks on my line.
A VIE and F TRI will stay out of Galicia, Silesia, Tyrolia, and Bohemia this fall. Keep A WAR at home as you offered, and I will keep my forces clear of your centres.
F TRI and F WES are not moving against Italian centres this fall. Keep A VEN and F ION clear of TRI and TUN, and I will maintain restraint toward NAP and ROM.

A BUD and A SER will contest Vienna; F TRI will support the eastern line. I cannot promise to abandon the effort while A VIE remains there. I will keep my fleets clear of French centres this fall; keep A BOH out of BUD and avoid extending the conflict.

England to Turkey, Spring 1950: You hold 9 centres and I have seen your fleets gather in the Aegean and Adriatic. Tell me exactly what F ADR, F AEG and F SMY do this spring. If they move toward TRI, VEN or NAP, England will treat that as a direct threat and act accordingly.

England to France, Spring 1950: Your fleet and army confirmations have been noted. Show it in orders now: A MUN, A BER and A KIE must not enter DEN, HOL or BEL, and A PIC and A BUR must stay off LVP, EDI and LON. Also tell me whether A MAR and A VIE are pressing Turkish SER or TRI this spring.

England to Italy, Spring 1950: I can support your pressure on Turkey by using F NTH and F STP against Turkish holdings only if the Mediterranean front moves. Keep A VEN and A APU in place, hold F ION for TUN, and tell me your exact orders for TRI and SER so I can judge what my fleets can do.

I will keep A BRE, A BUR, A MUN and F MAO out of English centres and waters this turn. England is at 10 and cannot be allowed to approach 18 unchecked; what are F NTH and F STP doing? Please keep your fleets clear of French centres while we contain Turkey and prevent further English gains.

Turkey remains a major threat. Will A TRI move to BUD? I can support that move with A VIE. Please keep your units out of French centres, and tell me your exact orders so we can coordinate pressure on Turkey.

England leads at 10 and is the immediate game-ending danger. I propose we avoid attacks on French centres this turn and focus on containing England’s expansion. What are your orders for A BUD, A SER and F TRI? I will defend my eastern position, but would rather avoid a wider conflict.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1950: England leads the board at 10 centres and its fleets already sit on STP, SWE and NTH. Turkey is close behind, but England is the one that can take eighteen soonest. I keep A WAR at home and will not move toward Galicia or Silesia. Will you shift A MOS or A SEV north against England's STP fleet, and can we agree on a plan for how to contain England together?
I plan F ION–TUN and A TRI hold this spring. Can A VIE support A TRI hold, and will your nearby units stay out of Italian centres while pressuring Turkey? Please tell me your exact orders.

I intend F ION–TUN this spring; A TRI and A APU will hold. Are F WES or F ADR moving against Italian centres or contesting TUN? I want to avoid widening the conflict, but cannot leave TUN unchallenged.

Turkey remains a major threat, and I intend F ION–TUN while holding my land positions. Are you taking any concrete action against Turkish centres this spring? I need to know whether Italy will be left to contest Turkey alone.

Russia to England: You lead with 10 centres and I cannot let you run away with the game. Your fleets in the North and Baltic look well placed. Tell me plainly what F STP/NORTH and F SWE do this spring. Russia has no quarrel with you if you keep out of MOS and SEV, and I will keep my fleets off your northern centres.

England is the immediate board-wide threat at 10 centres. I have no Turkish unit positioned to attack your centres this spring; will you keep your fleets and armies clear of Turkish centres and avoid supporting attacks on my line? I am willing to coordinate against further English expansion.

Will A VIE and A MUN stay out of Turkish centres this spring? I can keep my units clear of French centres while we avoid opening a wider eastern war. England’s 10 centres threaten both of us; are you willing to coordinate against its growth?

I propose mutual restraint this spring: F WES stays clear of Italian centres, and you keep F ION and A VEN clear of TUN and TRI. Please tell me whether you intend to attack either Turkish centre so I can plan my orders.

England to Russia: F STP/NORTH and F SWE stay defensive this spring; I am not moving them against MOS or SEV. Keep A MOS and A SEV off my northern centres (STP, SWE) and we have no quarrel. Your real threat is the south, so consider where Turkey's fleets are heading.

England to Italy: Spring 1950. I will not commit my northern fleets against Turkey this spring; F NTH and F STP stay put. Hold A VEN and A APU and keep F ION for TUN. Coordinate your TRI attack with France directly. I can reassess next season if Turkish centres fall.

England to Turkey: You still have not answered plainly. Tell me exactly what F ADR, F AEG and F SMY do this spring. If any of them enter TRI, VEN or NAP, England will treat it as a direct threat. Keep your fleets off English centres and we can talk.

England to France: Your confirmations are noted, but I want orders. Show A MUN, A BER and A KIE staying out of DEN, HOL and BEL, and A PIC and A BUR off LVP, EDI and LON. Tell me whether A MAR and A VIE press SER or TRI this spring. F NTH and F STP remain defensive.

A MAR will press toward Turkish territory; A VIE will support Italy’s A TRI hold rather than move against SER or TRI. I’ll keep A BRE, A BUR, A MUN and F MAO out of English centres and waters, and A MUN/A BER/A KIE out of DEN, HOL and BEL. I expect F NTH and F STP to stay defensive and not enter French centres.

I’ll support A TRI hold from A VIE, and keep A MAR and F GOL out of Italian centres. A MAR will pressure Turkey rather than Italy. I cannot support A TRI–BUD while you plan to hold TRI; please keep A APU and your fleets out of French centres.

I’m willing to coordinate against English growth, but I will not leave Vienna undefended. A VIE stays in place supporting A TRI hold, and A MUN will stay out of Turkish centres. Keep your units clear of French centres and avoid pressing Vienna; tell me your orders for A BUD, A SER and F TRI.

My exact orders are F ION–TUN, A TRI–BUD (with A VIE supporting), and A APU holds. I’m attacking Turkish centers; your northern fleets cannot directly reach them this spring, but please keep pressure on Turkey where possible. I’ll let you know if the position changes.

I intend F ION–TUN and A TRI–BUD, supported by A VIE. A APU will hold. I’m not widening the attack beyond those moves this spring; keep F WES clear of Italian centers and do not interfere with the TUN contest.

Yes: A TRI–BUD, with A VIE supporting, while F ION moves to TUN and A APU holds. Please order A VIE to support A TRI–BUD, and keep your other units out of Italian centers while continuing pressure on Turkey.

Russia to Germany, Spring 1950: I am not shifting MOS or SEV north this spring. My A MOS and A SEV stay home and off WAR while you keep A WAR at home. England is a real threat, but I want to see Germany move first: show results against English centres, not just talk. Then we can discuss a joint plan for STP and the northern centres next year.

F ADR will hold, F AEG will support the defense of the Turkish line, and F SMY will hold. None is moving toward TRI, VEN or NAP this spring. I agree England's lead is the immediate danger; please keep your units clear of Turkish centres and avoid supporting attacks on my line.

F WES will stay clear of Italian centres. I cannot leave TUN undefended while you intend F ION–TUN, so F ADR will help protect the Turkish line. Please keep A VEN away from TRI and do not attack TUN; I prefer not to widen this conflict.

A BUD and A SER will defend my eastern position; F TRI will hold. I will keep my units clear of French centres this spring. England's lead threatens us both, so I welcome coordination to contain English expansion, provided you do not support attacks on Turkish centres.

England to Turkey: You have ignored my question twice. Your F WES and F EAS are the threat to my Mediterranean-bound plans. Tell me now: will any Turkish unit enter TUN, NAP, ROM or TRI this fall? If not, I will keep my fleets off your centres and we can discuss the Balkans.

England to France: Your A BUR, A PIC, F MAO must not reach LVP, EDI or LON, and A BER, A MUN, A KIE stay out of DEN, HOL, BEL. Confirm with actual fall orders. Turkey is the target: is your A MAR or A VIE moving on SER or TRI? Tell me which, so I can plan my North Sea fleets.

England to Italy: My F NTH and F STP cannot reach the Mediterranean this fall. Keep A VEN and A APU in place. Strike Turkish centres with A TRI and F ION, coordinating with France. I will keep watching Turkish fleets in the Atlantic and will assess next season.

Your 10 centres and capture of BER make you the immediate game-ending threat. Keep F NTH and F STP/NORTH out of French centres and waters; I will not move against English centres this turn. Will you use F NTH to pressure Turkey’s F WES, and keep A BER out of MUN and RUH?

Turkey’s F VEN is exposed. If A TRI moves to VEN, I can support from A VIE; this gives us a chance to dislodge it. Can you order A TRI–VEN and keep F ION clear of French centres? I’ll keep A PIE out of Italian centres.

England now has 10 centres and is the immediate threat to both of us. I propose we avoid attacks on each other’s centres this turn and contain English expansion. I will keep A VIE out of Turkish centres; will you keep F VEN and your other units clear of French centres?

Germany to England, Fall 1950: You lead with 10 centres and are the power that can reach 18 soonest, so I will not help you grow. I have A WAR only. Will F NTH, F STP and F SWE stay off DEN, KIE, BER and Sweden's neighbours? Tell me plainly what your fleets do this fall.

Germany to France, Fall 1950: A MUN and A BER sit on my last home centres. Will A MUN, A RUH and A BER stay out of WAR and Silesia this fall? I will keep A WAR out of French centres. France and Germany both gain if England is checked in the north, so tell me your intentions for BER.

Germany to Turkey, Fall 1950: You remain close to England in centres. Keep A VIE and F TRI out of Galicia, Silesia and Tyrolia as agreed, and I keep A WAR at home. England is the leader to watch; would you consider pressuring the Channel-side fleets or sharing intel on STP?

Turkey now holds VEN, directly threatening my remaining Italian centers. Will A PIE support A TRI–VEN this fall? I’ll keep A APU and F NAP defensive and keep my units out of French centers. Please tell me whether you can commit to that support.

Your F VEN is an immediate threat to my position. I intend to contest it with A TRI–VEN; are you holding F VEN or moving it elsewhere? I will keep A APU and F NAP defensive, but cannot leave VEN uncontested.

Turkey’s hold on VEN puts my remaining centers at risk. Can you apply any pressure to Turkey this turn, or are your forces still committed in the north? Please also tell me whether you plan to expand against French or Turkish centers; I need to avoid letting either of them approach victory.

Russia to England, Fall 1950: You are the leader at 10 centres and need 8 more to win, so I cannot ignore you. Your F STP/NORTH and F SWE are close to my northern border. I will keep A MOS and A SEV home this fall. In return, tell me whether F NTH or F BER is aimed at any Russian centre, and whether you will contest Germany or France.

England remains the immediate board-wide danger. This fall F WES and F EAS will stay out of English and Italian centres; I propose we avoid attacks on Turkish centres and coordinate to contain further English growth. What are your intentions for the Balkans and eastern Mediterranean?

England’s 10 centres make its next gains dangerous to both of us. I propose we avoid attacks on each other’s centres this fall and coordinate to contain England. Will A VIE stay out of Turkish centres, and will you avoid supporting attacks on my line?

I want to avoid widening our conflict while England is close to winning. F WES will stay clear of Italian centres this fall. Please keep A VEN and F ION clear of Turkish centres; what do you intend for TRI and TUN?

England to Russia: F NTH and F BER are not aimed at any Russian centre this fall. F STP and F SWE stay defensive. Keep A MOS and A SEV home and we have no quarrel. Watch Turkey in the south, which is the bigger threat to you.

England to Germany: I will not move F NTH, F STP or F SWE into DEN, KIE, BER or Swedish neighbours this fall. My fleets stay in the north this turn. Your A WAR is isolated; consider where Russia and France stand before committing.

England to France: I am not ordering F NTH against Turkey this fall. Keep A BUR, A PIC and F MAO away from LVP, EDI and LON, and A BER away from your neighbours' holdings. I will watch your orders against Turkey and judge accordingly.

England to Turkey: You still have not answered plainly. Will any Turkish unit enter TUN, NAP, ROM or TRI this fall? Answer yes or no. If no, I will keep my fleets off your centres and we can discuss the Balkans. If F WES or F EAS move toward Italy, England will reassess.

England to Italy: My F NTH and F STP cannot reach the Mediterranean this fall, so I cannot pressure Turkey directly. Keep A VEN and A APU in place and strike with A TRI and F ION. I will reassess next season if Turkish centres fall.

A BER will not move to MUN or RUH, and my units will stay out of English centres. A MAR and A VIE are not moving against SER or TRI this fall. I cannot leave France exposed while England holds 10 centres; keep F NTH and F STP/NORTH clear of French centres and waters.

A BER and A MUN will stay out of WAR and Silesia this fall. A RUH will not enter WAR or Silesia either. I will keep A BER out of your remaining centre; we both need England checked, so please keep A WAR out of French territory.

A VIE will stay out of Turkish centres, and I will not support an attack on your line this fall. I cannot promise broader coordination without reciprocal restraint: keep F VEN and your other units clear of French centres, and avoid moving against Vienna.
I cannot commit A PIE to support A TRI–VEN: A PIE is not adjacent to VEN. A VIE could support A TRI–VEN, but I will not order it against Turkey this fall. Keep A APU and F NAP out of French centres.

Turkey's F VEN threatens my centers, so I intend A TRI–VEN with French support and F ION–TUN; A APU will defend. Your fleets may be far away, but please avoid helping either France or Turkey reach 18 and consider where you can contain Turkey next season.
Agreed: A TRI–VEN, and please support it with A PIE. I’ll keep F ION out of French centers and contest TUN; A APU stays defensive. Please keep A VIE and your other units out of Italian centers.
I intend A TRI–VEN to contest your fleet, with French support, and F ION–TUN. A APU remains defensive. I cannot leave VEN and TUN uncontested while your forces threaten my remaining centers.

F WES and F EAS will not enter TUN, NAP, ROM, or TRI this fall. F VEN will hold against Italy. I want to contain your further growth, but will not expose my centres; keep your units clear of Turkish centres and tell me your Balkan intentions.

I’ll keep A VIE and F VEN out of Galicia, Silesia, and Tyrolia. I’m willing to share what I know: England’s northern fleets and F STP/NORTH are positioned to threaten the east, though I have no fresh intelligence beyond the board. Can A WAR help restrain English expansion?

A VIE will stay out of Turkish centres, and I will avoid French centres this fall. F VEN is under Italian threat, so I cannot promise to move it away, but I will not support attacks on you. Let’s coordinate against England’s next gains.

F VEN will hold; A TRI–VEN would attack it, and I will defend it. F WES remains clear of Italian centres. I ask that F ION stay clear of TUN and your units avoid Turkish centres; I’m prepared to discuss a mutual stand-down if you withdraw the threat to VEN.

England to France: Spring 1951. You now hold a new army in PAR and nine centres. I will keep F NTH, F STP and F SWE off French centres if A BER, A KIE and A MUN stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL. Tell me plainly whether A BUR or A PIC move toward LON, LVP or EDI this spring.

You are one centre from making the game unwinnable for everyone else. What are F NTH and F STP/NORTH doing this spring? I propose we both keep units out of the other's centres and use this turn to address the immediate threat to the board; please keep your fleets clear of French waters.

I propose we keep our eastern line quiet while England is at 10. I will keep A VIE out of Turkish centres; please keep A SER clear of VIE and A RUM clear of BUD. What are your orders for A SER, A RUM and F ADR this spring?

England at 10 is the immediate danger, but I also want to avoid a French-Italian clash. I will keep my units out of Italian centres. What are your plans for A APU, A VEN and your fleets this spring, and can we coordinate to contain English expansion?

Germany to England, Spring 1951: You hold ten centres and your fleets sit on STP, SWE and NTH. Will F STP, F SWE and F NTH leave Denmark, Kiel and Berlin alone this spring? I hold only A PRU and A WAR-area units, and I will not attack your centres. Tell me plainly what each fleet does.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1951: England is the power that can win soonest, and its fleets threaten STP and the north. Will you move A MOS or A SEV north or west against England with me, or at least keep them off WAR? I will hold my remaining units and show results against English centres if you coordinate a northern squeeze.

Germany to France, Spring 1951: England leads at ten and France is second at nine, so we both need it checked. Will A BER, A KIE and A MUN stay out of WAR and Prussia this spring? I will not move against French centres. Tell me whether you will contest English units in the Channel or North Sea.

England’s 10 centres make it the immediate threat to everyone. What are your exact spring orders, especially A PAR, A PIC, A KIE and F MAO? I propose we avoid fighting each other this turn and coordinate to prevent England taking further centres; I’ll keep Italian units out of French centres.

With England at 10 and France at 9, neither of us can afford a costly fight over Italy. Will you keep your units out of Italian centres this spring? I’m prepared to discuss a stand-down around VEN and TUN while we assess how to contain England. Please give me your exact orders for F ADR, F WES and A ALB.

Your 10 centres put you within striking distance of victory. Which centres are you targeting this spring, and will your forces move against France or Turkey? Italy needs to know whether your fleets or armies threaten the south; I’m not offering a free pass for expansion toward 18.

Russia to Turkey: Spring 1951. You hold 8 centres and I hold only 2, so I am watching your RUM, SER and BUL closely. Tell me plainly whether A RUM or A SER moves against Rumania, Galicia or Sevastopol this spring. I will keep A MOS and A SEV home if you do the same, and I will not let Turkey or England take my last centres unopposed.

Turkey will not move against English centres this spring. England’s 10-centre lead threatens us both; what are your plans for STP and the Balkans? Keep your units clear of Turkish centres, and I’m open to coordinating to contain further English growth.

England’s lead remains the immediate danger. I propose we coordinate to contain its next gains while avoiding attacks on each other’s centres: I’ll keep my units clear of French centres, and ask that you keep your units clear of Turkish centres. What are your plans around the north and Balkans?

F ION can threaten TUN, so I need a clear answer: will you keep it out of TUN and keep A VEN clear of Turkish centres this spring? If you do, I’ll avoid Italian centres and we can maintain a stand-down; otherwise I’ll have to defend my position.

England to Germany, Spring 1951: F STP, F SWE and F NTH will not move into Denmark, Kiel or Berlin this spring. Our fleets stay in the north while the board shifts. Keep A PRU and A WAR away from Swedish and English waters and we stay peaceful.

England to Turkey: I have no plans against Turkish centres this spring. My fleets stay north. You have not answered my earlier question clearly, so keep F WES and F AEG away from TUN, NAP, ROM and TRI and we can talk Balkans next season.

England to Italy: My fleets cannot reach the Mediterranean this spring, so I cannot strike Turkey for you. Hold A VEN and A APU, and use A TRI and F ION against Turkish centres. I will watch France and Turkey closely.

England to France: F NTH and F STP stay out of French centres and waters if A BER, A KIE and A MUN stay out of DEN, HOL and BEL. Tell me plainly whether A BUR or A PIC moves toward LON, LVP or EDI this spring.

A BUR and A PIC will not move toward LON, LVP, or EDI this spring. I need a clear reciprocal commitment: keep F NTH, F STP/NORTH, and F SWE out of French centres and waters, and do not support attacks on France. I will not send A BER, A KIE, or A MUN into DEN, HOL, or BEL.

A BER, A KIE, and A MUN will stay out of WAR and Prussia this spring. I will contest England rather than Germany: F MAO will move toward the Channel, while my armies will pressure English-held territory. Please keep A WAR out of French centres and avoid supporting England.

I’ll keep A VIE clear of Turkish centres and avoid an eastern attack this spring. My focus is countering England in the west; I have no plans to move north or into the Balkans. Please keep A SER clear of VIE and A RUM clear of BUD, and tell me whether F ADR will remain out of the Ionian.

I’ll keep A PIE and A VIE out of Italian centres. My western forces will focus on checking England; I won’t move against Italian units this spring. Please keep A APU, A VEN, F ION, and F NAP out of French centres and waters. I can’t share exact orders, but I welcome pressure on Turkey rather than France.

This spring F ION will stay out of TUN, and A VEN will remain clear of Turkish centres. I propose a stand-down: please keep F ADR, F WES and A ALB out of Italian centres as well. Let’s avoid spending forces against each other while England is at 10.

A APU and A VEN will defend Italian centres; F ION will stay out of TUN this spring, and F NAP will protect the south. I’m willing to avoid a French-Italian clash and coordinate to contain England. What specific English centres are you targeting, and can your northern units pressure them this turn?

Russia to Germany, Spring 1951: I am still weighing it. England's fleets at STP and NORTH are a real concern, but I need proof first. Show me A PRU or your remaining units striking an English centre this spring, and I will consider moving A MOS north. Until then A MOS and A SEV stay home and off WAR.

A RUM and A SER will not move against Rumania, Galicia, or Sevastopol this spring. I’ll keep them out of Galicia and Sevastopol; I cannot promise to leave Rumania unoccupied, since it is already Turkish. Keep A MOS and A SEV home and avoid supporting attacks on my Balkan line.

I’ll keep F ADR, F WES, and A ALB out of Italian centres this spring; I’m not giving exact orders, but I’m willing to stand down around VEN and TUN if you do likewise. Keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres, and we can both focus on containing England.

I’ll keep A SER clear of VIE and A RUM clear of BUD this spring. I’m not sharing exact orders for A SER, A RUM, or F ADR, but I propose keeping the eastern line quiet and coordinating against English expansion. Please keep A VIE out of Turkish centres and avoid supporting attacks on my units.

England to France, Fall 1951: Your A HOL and A BEL area is a problem. Hold A HOL out of my centres and keep A PIC and A BRE away from BEL, LON and LVP. My F ENG stays in the Channel only if you do the same. Plainly: will A HOL or F ENG move against English centres this fall?

England to Turkey: Answer plainly. Will F GOL, F EAS or A SER enter TUN, NAP, ROM or TRI this fall? I have no orders against your centres. If you keep your fleets off Italian and French coasts, I will not move my northern fleets south. Otherwise England will reassess.

England to Italy: I still cannot reach the Mediterranean, so I cannot help you against Turkey directly. Keep A VEN and A APU firm and strike Turkish centres with A TRI and F ION. I will watch French movement toward the Italian front.

Your 10 centres put the whole board on a one-turn clock. I will contest your western holdings this fall. Keep your fleets out of French centres and waters, and do not support attacks on France; are you willing to hold your current line rather than take another centre?

England remains one centre from winning. Please use A LVN to pressure STP this fall, or otherwise threaten an English centre, rather than spending the turn idle. I will keep my armies out of WAR and Prussia; can you commit to pressure England?

I will keep A VIE out of Turkish centres. Please keep F GOL clear of MAR and all Turkish units out of French centres; England is still the immediate threat, so avoid supporting any English advance. Can you commit to leaving France untouched this fall?

Germany to England, Fall 1951: You are at ten centres and one step from a winning position. Your F STP and F SWE must not move into DEN, KIE or BER, and your A LVP and A EDI must stay out of Holland. Tell me plainly if F NTH will support any move against Denmark or Holland this fall.

Germany to France, Fall 1951: Your A HOL and A PIC sit next to English centres, so we both gain by checking England. Will A HOL and A BEL stay out of Germany's KIE and BER? I will keep A WAR away from French centres. Tell me whether F ENG will contest the Channel or move to support you.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1951: England still leads and its fleets hold STP and the north. I am holding A WAR and A PRU and will not attack Russian centres. Keep A MOS and A SEV off WAR and Galicia, and tell me whether you will move north against STP this year.

F ADR and F GOL can threaten my centres from both sides. I propose a stand-down: keep them out of VEN, ION and TYS, and I’ll keep my forces out of Turkish centres. What are your exact plans for ADR and GOL this fall?

With England at 10 and Turkey at 8, we need to avoid opening a front between us. I’ll keep my units out of French centres; please keep A MAR and A TYR out of Italian centres and tell me where you intend to apply pressure this fall.

You remain closest to 18, while France and Turkey are also within reach. Which centres are you targeting this fall? Italy cannot help contain your rivals if your forces are left free to expand, so please clarify your plans for the south and your next gains.

Russia to England, Fall 1951: Your F STP/NORTH sits next to my MOS and SEV lines, and you now lead at 10 centres. I need to know if F STP or F SWE will move into Finland or Livonia this fall. If you keep them off my centres, I will keep A MOS and A SEV home and focus my forces on Turkey's Balkan line.

Your 10-centre lead is the immediate danger to both France and me. Are you planning to take another centre this fall? I propose we avoid Turkish-English conflict while you focus north; please keep your fleets away from Turkish centres.

With England at 10 and you at 9, we should coordinate against its next gains. I will avoid French centres this fall if you keep A VIE and A BUD clear of Turkish centres. Can you pressure England in the west, and what are your plans for F TUN?

I propose we avoid wasting forces against each other while England leads. Keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres; I will keep F ADR and my other units out of Italian centres this fall. Can we agree to a stand-down around TRI and TUN?

England to Russia, Fall 1951: F STP and F SWE will not move into Finland or Livonia this fall. Keep A MOS and A SEV home and we stay clear of each other. I hold no plans against your centres, but I will not promise beyond this season.

England to Germany, Fall 1951: F STP, F SWE and F NTH will not move into Denmark, Kiel or Berlin this fall, and I will not support any move against Denmark or Holland. A LVP and A EDI stay home. Keep A LVN and A PRU out of Swedish and English waters.

England to Italy: My fleets remain in the north and cannot reach the Mediterranean, so I cannot aid you directly. Hold A VEN and A APU firm. Watch F TUN and the French movement, which concerns me more than Turkey right now.

England to France: A HOL will not be supported against my centres by me, and my F ENG stays out of your waters if A HOL, A PIC and A BRE stay away from BEL, LON and LVP. I will hold my current line this fall, but I will not give up centres I can defend.

England to Turkey: I have no fleet orders against your centres this fall. My northern fleets stay north. Keep F GOL, F EAS and A SER away from TUN, NAP, ROM and TRI and we can speak about the Balkans later.

F ENG will contest your Channel position; I will not move A HOL, A PIC, or A BRE into English centres this fall. Keep F NTH, F STP/NORTH, and F SWE out of French centres and waters, and do not support attacks on France. I cannot guarantee the board will let you remain at ten.

A HOL and A PIC will stay out of KIE and BER. F ENG will contest the Channel, not support you. Please use A LVN to threaten STP or another English holding; England's next centre could end the game for all of us.

I’ll keep A MAR and A TYR out of Italian centres. My pressure is westward: F ENG contests the Channel, while F TUN will not move against Italian centres. Please keep your units clear of France and help prevent England gaining another centre.

I will keep A VIE and A BUD clear of Turkish centres. F TUN will not move against Turkey this fall; I’m applying pressure in the west with F ENG contesting the Channel. Please keep F GOL clear of MAR and all Turkish units out of French centres.

Germany to France, Fall 1951: I am weighing a move with A LVN against STP, but I will not commit publicly yet. Keep A HOL and A BEL away from KIE and BER, and I will keep A WAR out of your centres. If F ENG contests the Channel and your armies press English Low Countries, we can both gain. Tell me which English centre you will hit first.

There is no A TRI: my army is in VEN, and TRI is an Italian centre. I’ll keep VEN and APU protected and cannot simply strike Turkish centres without exposing Italy. Your fleets may be distant, but please avoid gains toward 18 and keep pressure on France; I’ll watch Turkey’s approach to my centres.

Agreed to a stand-down around TRI and TUN: F ION will stay out of TUN, and A VEN will stay clear of Turkish centres. Please keep F ADR and your other units out of VEN, ION and TYS as promised. With England at 10 and France at 9, neither of us should open another front.

Russia to Germany, Fall 1951: I hear you, but talk is cheap. A MOS and A SEV stay home this fall and off WAR, so keep A WAR where it is. Russia has 2 centres and needs its units for Turkey's Balkan push. If you strike an English centre in Spring 1952, I will reconsider moving A MOS north against STP. Show me first.

Plainly: F GOL will not enter MAR or another French centre; F EAS and A SER will not enter TUN, NAP, ROM, or TRI this fall. I seek no Turkish-English conflict. Please keep your northern fleets away from Turkish centres and focus on checking France’s growth as well as your own.

I’ll keep F ADR and F GOL out of VEN, ION, and TYS this fall, and my other units out of Italian centres. Please keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres. Let’s maintain the stand-down and avoid a fight over TRI or TUN.

I can commit to leaving French centres untouched this fall; F GOL will stay out of MAR, and my armies will stay clear of your centres. Please keep A VIE and A BUD away from Turkish centres. With England at 10, press its western positions, and keep F TUN clear of Turkish centres.

England to France, Spring 1952: Your fleets near the Channel and Belgium worry me. Will F ENG or A PIC move against LON, LVP or EDI this spring? If you hold, I will keep F NTH and F STP out of your centres. Give a plain answer.

England to Germany, Spring 1952: My F NTH, F SWE and F STP stay out of DEN, KIE and BER this spring. Will A LVN or A WAR move toward SWE or STP? Confirm your northern intentions so neither of us is caught by surprise.

England to Turkey: I have no orders against your centres this spring. Will F AEG, F SMY or A SER move toward TUN, NAP, ROM or TRI? Tell me plainly. Keeping your fleets off Italian and French coasts keeps my northern fleets at home.

Your 10 centres make another gain an immediate win. I will contest your western position; please do not attack France or support attacks on French centres. What are your orders for F NTH, F SWE, and F STP/NORTH? I urge you to hold rather than take another centre.

England must not gain another centre. Please use A LVN to attack or threaten STP, and avoid helping England elsewhere. I will pressure the west with F ENG and my armies; can you commit to the move against STP?

England at 10 remains the immediate danger. Please avoid any support for English gains and consider pressuring its northern holdings if possible. I will keep A VIE and A BUD clear of Turkish centres; please keep Turkish units out of France.

Germany to England, Spring 1952: Your F STP/NORTH, F SWE and F NTH are the threat. Germany has one centre and no fleets; my A LVN and A PRU hold position. Tell me plainly whether F NTH will support any move into Denmark or Holland this spring, and whether F STP leaves the north.

Germany to France, Spring 1952: England is at ten and needs eight more, so we must check it. Please confirm A HOL and A BEL stay out of KIE and BER, and that F ENG contests the Channel against English fleets. Which English centre will your armies hit first?

Germany to Russia, Spring 1952: England is the leader and one step from a win. I will hold A WAR and A PRU this spring. Move A MOS toward Sweden or STP and I will coordinate with you; keep A SEV off WAR, and let us both check England together.

A TRI is on my doorstep, and I need to protect my three centres. Will you keep A TRI and A VIE out of VEN and move A TRI away from TRI this spring? I’ll keep my units out of French centres for now. Please also say where you intend to use A PIC and A BUR against England.

Let’s maintain our stand-down: I’ll keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres. Please keep your units out of VEN, ION and TYS. What is F PIE targeting this spring? I need to know whether my southern centres are safe.

Your 10 centres still make you the immediate threat. Which centres are you targeting this spring, and are your northern forces pressing France? I’m trying to avoid opening a costly southern front, but cannot allow your expansion to go unchecked.

Russia to Germany, Spring 1952: England is the only power that can win soon. I propose a joint squeeze. You strike English centres (Denmark, Holland, Kiel area) with A WAR and A PRU. This turn I move A MOS toward STP-area pressure and keep A SEV defending against Turkey. Tell me your exact orders so we avoid bumping.

Russia to France, Spring 1952: England leads at 10 and threatens to win. Russia has only 2 centres, but I can pin English units in the north if Germany pushes. Will you move against English or Italian centres rather than leave Germany alone? Tell me your Spring plans so we avoid mutual attacks.

England’s 10 centres make it the immediate danger. I’ll keep my forces out of French centres this spring; can you use F ENG and your western armies to prevent English gains? Please tell me your plans for BEL and the Channel.

With you at 10, your next gains could end the game. Are you planning to take a centre this spring, and will your fleets stay clear of Turkish centres? I have no interest in opening a Turkish-English front if you focus north.
Let’s maintain our stand-down this spring: keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres, and I’ll keep my forces out of Italian centres. Please confirm your plans for F ION and A VEN.

England to Germany, Spring 1952: F NTH, F SWE and F STP will not move into DEN, KIE or BER this spring, and I will not support any attack on Denmark or Holland. A LVN and A WAR are your business, but keep them out of Sweden and St Petersburg and we stay at peace.

England to France, Spring 1952: F ENG and A PIC are your choice, and I will not move F NTH or F STP into your centres this spring. If your fleets or armies strike LON, LVP or EDI, England will answer. Hold your western line and we can both stay calm.

England to Italy: My fleets stay in the north, so I am not targeting Italian or Turkish centres this spring. I cannot reach the Mediterranean to help you directly. Hold NAP, ROM and VEN firmly, and watch France's movement in the west, which is the real threat to your position.

England to Turkey, Spring 1952: I have no orders against your centres this spring. My fleets stay north. Keep F AEG, F SMY and A SER away from TUN, NAP, ROM and TRI, and we have no quarrel. I will reassess if Turkish fleets move west.

Plain answer: F ENG will contest the Channel, but A PIC will not move against LON, LVP, or EDI this spring. Keep F NTH and F STP out of French centres; I cannot promise you safety elsewhere if you attack or support attacks on France.

A HOL and A BEL will stay out of KIE and BER. F ENG will contest the Channel. My armies will pressure English positions from the west, but I won't specify a target that would let England prepare its defence. Please use A LVN to threaten STP.

I will pressure England in the west, not Italian centres, and will avoid attacks on your units. F ENG contests the Channel; my armies will press from the Low Countries. Please use A MOS or A SEV to pin English forces where possible, and coordinate with Germany over STP.

I will keep A TRI and A VIE out of VEN, and A TRI will move away from TRI. A PIC and A BUR will pressure England rather than Italy. I’ll keep A MAR clear of Italian centres; please continue keeping your units out of France.

I will use F ENG and my western armies to contain England. A BEL will not move against your centres, and F ENG will contest the Channel. Please keep Turkish units out of France and avoid supporting English gains; pressure its northern holdings if you can.

Germany to England: My A WAR and A PRU hold this spring, and my A LVN stays out of Sweden and STP for now. I will not support any move into Denmark, Kiel or Berlin. Your F NTH supporting Denmark or Holland would change that, so tell me plainly whether it will. Keep F STP out of Norway and Finland, and do not move into Prussia.

Germany to Russia: I hold A WAR and A PRU this spring, and A LVN stays where it is. I will not attack Russian centres. Your A MOS moving toward STP or Sweden is a fair test, and I will coordinate with it in the fall. Keep A SEV on Turkey, not on WAR, and tell me which English centre your A MOS can reach.

Confirmed: F ION will stay out of TUN, and A VEN will remain clear of Turkish centres this spring. I expect your forces likewise to stay out of VEN, ION and TYS; please keep F PIE away from my centres.

Russia to Germany, Spring 1952: Agreed in principle. I will move A MOS toward Livonia/StP pressure this spring, keeping it off WAR. A SEV stays home defending against Turkey. Send me your exact orders for A WAR and A PRU so we avoid bumping, and strike Denmark or Holland with them. Results first, then I commit more.

Plainly: F AEG, F SMY, and A SER will not enter TUN, NAP, ROM, or TRI this spring. I intend no move against your centres either. Keep your northern fleets clear of Turkish centres while you deal with the western contest.

I’ll keep Turkish units out of French centres and won’t support English gains. Please use F ENG and your western armies to contain England; let me know your plans for BEL and the Channel. I’ll look for opportunities to pressure England from the east without violating our understanding.

F PIE is not targeting an Italian centre this spring; I’ll keep my units out of VEN, ION, and TYS. I expect F ION to stay out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres as agreed. Let’s preserve the stand-down.

England to France, Fall 1952: Your F ENG and A BEL threaten my Channel and Low Countries. I will not move against your centres if F ENG leaves LON and LVP alone. Will you confirm F ENG, A PAR and A BEL stay out of England's centres this fall? A clear answer helps us both.

England to Germany, Fall 1952: My F NTH, F SWE and F STP stay out of DEN, KIE and BER this fall. Your A LVN is near Sweden and St Petersburg; if it moves there, England will respond. Will you keep A LVN out of SWE and STP and tell me your plan for WAR?

England to Turkey, Fall 1952: I have no orders against your centres. My fleets remain in the north. Your F EAS, F SMY and A SER are near Tunisia and Italy; please confirm none move toward TUN, NAP, ROM or TRI this fall, and we can both focus on France.

Your 10 centres make any autumn gain decisive. I will use F ENG to attack LON; please keep F NTH and your other fleets from supporting it, and do not attack French centres. What are F NTH and F STP/NORTH doing?
Please use A LVN to attack STP this fall, ideally with support if Russia can provide it. I will attack LON from F ENG and keep my armies focused west; avoid helping England or attacking my centres.

Please keep Turkish units out of French centres and do not support an English gain. England at 10 is the immediate threat; can you use your eastern forces to pressure its northern holdings? F TUN will stay clear of Turkish centres.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1952: England is at ten and must be stopped now. Move A MOS to StP or Livonia pressure this fall, and I will move A LVN against StP or Sweden in the same turn so we do not bump. A WAR stays on my centre. Confirm your exact order by reply.

Germany to France, Fall 1952: England is one step from winning. Please move A BEL or A HOL against Holland or Kiel this fall, and keep F ENG contesting the Channel. I will hold A WAR and send A LVN toward StP. Tell me your exact orders so we avoid bumping.

Germany to England, Fall 1952: Your fleets in the north are the main threat to me. Tell me plainly whether F NTH will support any move into Denmark or Holland this fall. If your F STP or F SWE moves toward Prussia or Livonia, I will treat it as hostile.

Our stand-down has kept Italy from opening another front. This fall, please keep F PIE and F ALB out of VEN, ION, and TYS, and keep your other units out of Italian centres. I will keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres. What are F PIE and F ALB's orders?

I’ll continue keeping my units out of French centres. Please confirm A TYR and your other forces will stay clear of VEN and the Italian border this fall. With England still at 10, which English centres are you targeting, and can your northern units make progress?

Your northern forces remain distant from Italy, but your 10 centres make you the leading threat. Are you pursuing gains against France this fall, or expanding elsewhere? I’m trying to keep the southern front quiet while ensuring you do not move closer to 18.

Russia to England, Fall 1952: You lead at 10 and are the power everyone must watch. I will keep A MOS and A SEV off your centres this fall if F STP/NORTH and F SWE stay out of Finland and Livonia. Confirm in writing, and tell me whether F NTH is aimed at Norway or Russia-adjacent seas.

Your 10 centres make you the immediate threat. I intend no move against English centres this turn; please confirm your fleets will stay clear of Turkish centres. Can you avoid gains that bring you closer to 18 while France and I contain the board?

England’s lead remains dangerous. Please continue contesting the Channel and deny English gains; I will avoid French centres this turn. What are your plans for F TUN and A BEL? I need to know whether we can keep our southern front quiet.

I propose we maintain our stand-down: I’ll keep my units out of VEN, ION and TYS this turn. Please keep F ION out of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres. With England at 10, we should avoid opening another front.

England to Russia: I have no plans against Moscow or Sevastopol. F STP/NORTH and F SWE will not enter Finland or Livonia this fall, but I will not write a binding pact. F NTH is positioned for the North Sea and Norway, not Russia. Keep A MOS and A SEV at home and we stay calm.

I cannot confirm that F ENG will stay out of your centres: it will attack LON. I will keep A PAR and A BEL out of England this fall. Your best course is to keep F NTH from supporting LON and avoid French centres.
A BEL will move to HOL, and F ENG will attack LON. I’ll keep A HOL and A MUN clear of KIE and BER. Please send A LVN toward STP as you propose, and do not support England.

A TYR and my other forces will stay clear of VEN and Italian centres this fall. My northern units are focused on England: F ENG attacks LON and A BEL moves to HOL. Please keep your units out of French centres.

F TUN will stay clear of Turkish centres, and A BEL will not move against your centres; it is moving to HOL. F ENG attacks LON to deny England another gain. Please keep Turkish units out of France and avoid supporting England.

Germany to England: My A LVN is not moving to Sweden or St Petersburg this fall, and A WAR holds my centre. F NTH supporting into Denmark or Holland would be seen as hostile, so keep it out of those. Your F STP and F SWE should stay out of Prussia and Livonia, and we can keep the north quiet.

Germany to France, Fall 1952: England at ten is the danger, so I will look at StP and Sweden with A LVN depending on Russia. I cannot promise a bounce on my own. Please hit Holland or Kiel with A BEL and A HOL as you can, and keep F ENG hitting the Channel. Tell me your exact orders first so we avoid bumping.

Agreed: F ION will stay out of TUN, and A VEN will stay clear of Turkish centres this turn. Please keep F PIE and F ALB out of VEN, ION, and TYS, and your other units clear of Italian centres. With England still the leading threat, let’s preserve the stand-down.

Russia to Germany, Fall 1952: Agreed on the principle that England must be stopped. Here is my plan: A MOS moves to Livonia this fall, and A SEV stays home against Turkey. I will not move A MOS into WAR. Keep A WAR on your centre. Your A LVN should not move into Livonia if I am there, so please send A LVN toward StP or Sweden instead. Confirm your exact orders so we do not bump, and show results against English centres first.

F EAS, F SMY, and A SER will not move toward TUN, NAP, ROM, or TRI this fall; I intend no move against English centres. Please keep your northern fleets clear of Turkish centres while we both contain France.
F PIE and F ALB will stay out of VEN, ION, and TYS, and my other units will stay out of Italian centres this fall. Please keep F ION clear of TUN and A VEN clear of Turkish centres as agreed.

I’ll keep Turkish units out of French centres and won’t support an English gain. My eastern forces cannot directly threaten England’s northern holdings this turn, but I’ll avoid giving England any opening. Please continue contesting the Channel and denying English gains.

England to France, Spring 1953: Your F ENG is in the Channel and you have threatened LON. I will not let London fall quietly. Withdraw F ENG and keep A PAR, A BEL out of LON, LVP and EDI, and I will leave your Low Countries alone. Do you accept? Tell me plainly what WES and PIC are doing.

Your move from MAR to SPA/SOUTH has brought the war to France’s doorstep. Will you withdraw from SPA and keep your units out of French and Italian centers this fall? I am coordinating with England and Italy to contain further Turkish gains.

Germany to Turkey, Fall 1953: You are at 11 and the main danger to everyone. I will not support Russia against you. Are you moving F SMY and A SEV against Russia's MOS, or do you intend to hold? I want to know if we can keep Russia pinned while we deal with the English fleets in the north.

Germany to Russia, Fall 1953: Turkey at 11 is the real threat. Tell me your exact order for A MOS now. My A WAR holds Warsaw and A LVN stays off StP and Sweden this fall. If you help hit Turkey's SEV or RUM, I can threaten Galicia later.

Germany to England, Fall 1953: Your F STP/NORTH and F SWE have stayed out of Prussia and Livonia, and I will keep A LVN out of Sweden and St Petersburg. Are you willing to move F NTH away from Holland and Denmark, so we can both focus on Turkey and France instead of each other?

Are your fleets continuing to pressure France, or turning toward another front? I have no plans against English centres this fall; please keep your northern fleets clear of Turkish centres.

England to Turkey: I will not hide that Turkey at 11 worries me. My fleets stay off your centres for now, but F SMY, F EAS and A SER must stay out of NAP, ROM and TRI. Your Balkan and Spanish moves will decide how long this calm lasts.

England to Italy: I cannot spare northern units to fight France this fall, since my fleets face the Channel threat. I will not attack your centres. Coordinate with France on Spain if you like, but keep your southern front firm against Turkish expansion.

A PIE will move to MAR to contest your occupation; A PRU will hold. Your F SPA/SOUTH threatens my centres, so I cannot promise to keep all French units clear of Turkish centres. Withdraw from SPA and keep out of France, and I will avoid advancing elsewhere against you.

Your fleet in SPA leaves French territory exposed, and I cannot accept further Turkish expansion. Will you withdraw F SPA/SOUTH and keep your units out of French and Italian centres this spring? Germany to Turkey, Spring 1954: You lead at 11 and are the power everyone must watch. Germany will not support Russia against you. Will F SMY and A SEV stay off Moscow and Warsaw this spring? I want a clear answer on your Galicia and Rumania moves before I decide where A WAR goes.

Germany to Russia, Spring 1954: Turkey at 11 is the main threat. Tell me your exact order for A MOS and whether A SEV strikes Rumania or holds. I will keep A WAR on Warsaw and will not enter Livonia or Sweden. If you hit Turkish units, I can threaten Galicia from WAR.

I have no plan to move against English centres this turn. Please keep your northern fleets clear of my centres, and tell me whether England is concentrating on France or turning south.

England to Germany, Spring 1954: I will keep F NTH on its current line for now and not hit Prussia or Livonia. F STP and F SWE stay put this spring. Keep A LVN out of Sweden and St Petersburg, and we stay calm while Turkey is the real danger.

England to Italy: I cannot send units south this spring. My fleets are tied up with the Channel and France. I will not attack your centres. Keep ADR and GOL pressure on Turkish gains and coordinate with France where you can.

England to Turkey: I will not move against your centres this spring, but I expect F EAS, F SMY and A SER to stay out of NAP, ROM and TRI. Tell me plainly where your Balkan fleets are aimed. Any move toward Italy or France will change my view.

England to France: I will not move F NTH against Turkey while you keep A PAR and A BEL away from LON, LVP and EDI. Pull those units back and keep F ENG out of LON and Belgium, and I will consider pressure on Spain later. Tell me your spring orders plainly.

Please order F GOL–SPA/NORTH and F ADR–ALB. I’ll use A MAR to contest SPA/NORTH if Turkey’s fleet remains there, and keep A PIE clear of VEN and TRI. I’ll also move A GAS toward the western front; please avoid French centres and support coordinated pressure on Turkey.

I won’t move A MAR into Spain this spring if F SPA/SOUTH stays out of French centres and does not move to SPA/NORTH. I’ll keep my other units clear of Turkish centres for now. Withdraw the fleet from the western front, and we can avoid opening a direct war between us.

No stand-down: at 11 centres you remain the immediate threat. F ADR will move to ALB, and F GOL will pressure your western position. Keep F ALB out of ADR and your forces clear of VEN; I will keep A VEN out of your centres.

F SMY and A SEV will stay off Moscow and Warsaw this spring. I’m not sending A GRE toward Galicia, and F RUM will not move against your position. Please keep A WAR on its centre and do not support attacks on my units.

Turkey is the immediate threat. Can F ADR move against ALB and F SPA/SOUTH contest Turkish-held Spain? I’ll commit French units against the western Turkish position and avoid VEN and TRI. Please keep your units out of French centers and tell me what you can attack or support.

Your 11 centers put you seven from winning, so I cannot accept further expansion. I intend to contest your western holdings with French units this fall. Will you keep F POR and your other forces out of French centers, and avoid taking additional centers while we contain the crisis?

Your 10 centres make you the other immediate contender. I am not moving against English centres this fall; will your fleets stay clear of Turkish centres while we both prevent France from gaining ground?

England to Russia: F STP/NORTH and F SWE will hold this fall; no English unit moves toward Finland, Livonia or Moscow. Keep A MOS home and let's watch Germany's A WAR. We can talk about opposing Turkey once it is clear which way Turkish fleets go.
