Germany to Turkey: I will not support A UKR-MOS, and A WAR holds Warsaw. You are at 11 and I will not hand you Russian centres. If you move on Moscow, Germany stays neutral this fall, but I will reassess if your fleets push into Warsaw or Galicia.

I can order F ADR–ALB and F SPA/SOUTH–POR to pressure Turkey. Please have F MAO support my attack on POR, and tell me which Turkish western position your units will contest. I’ll keep my units out of French centres.

I can’t promise to keep F ADR out of ALB while you retain Turkish positions in the west and stand at 11 centres. I intend to pressure ALB and attack POR; keep F ALB out of ADR and avoid Italian centres if you want to limit the southern front.
I intend A UKR-MOS this fall, not an attack on WAR. F RUM will not attack Galicia or Rumania. You said you will not support Russia; will A WAR support A UKR-MOS? I will leave WAR untouched.

F ALB, F ARM, F ION and A TRI are not aimed at NAP or ROM this fall. F SMY and A SER will stay out of both. I cannot promise to refrain from all gains, but I am not targeting English centres; please keep your fleets clear of mine.

A UKR will not attack MOS this fall, and F RUM will not attack Russia or Galicia. I will not promise to return SEV in a future turn; it is Turkish territory, and I cannot agree to surrender it. Keep A MOS defensive and avoid moves against Rumania.

I will keep F POR and my other forces out of French centres this fall, and I am not seeking another French centre. I cannot agree to stop taking centres elsewhere. Please keep A MAR and your other units clear of my holdings, and do not attack POR or SPA.

F POR will not move against French centres this fall, and F ALB will stay out of ADR. I am not targeting NAP or ROM with F SMY or A SER. I cannot promise no gains anywhere; keep F ADR out of ALB and your forces clear of Turkish centres.

England to France: Spring 1955, your A PAR and A BEL still sit near LON and LVP. Withdraw them and I will consider pressure on Spain with F NTH. Until then F NTH stays on its line. Tell me your spring orders plainly, and whether F MAO is going against SPA or into ENG.

England to Italy: My fleets remain in the Channel and North Sea this spring; I will not attack your centres at POR or ROM. Take POR with F POR and F ADR if you can, and press GOL against Turkish gains. Tell me your exact spring moves so we avoid collisions.

Withdraw A BUD and A MOS from Turkish-owned centres this spring. I will keep A SIL off BER, but will continue pressing your positions around NAP and MUN. If you keep contesting my centres, I cannot promise to spare French holdings. Are you defending NAP, and will you vacate BUD and MOS?

England to France: I will not order F KIE to support A BER; KIE stays English and my fleets stay off BEL, HOL and DEN. Your words are fine, but I need proof. Name the Turkish centre your A MUN or F TYS will take this spring, and I will judge you by the result.

England to Turkey: Your fleets at EAS and ION are still drifting toward our waters, and you have not named a single centre you will take. Withdraw them and show me the target. Any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN or HOL will be opposed by force.

My exact target is TUN: F TYS–TUN, with F PIE supporting the move. I cannot guarantee a capture if Turkey supports F TUN, but this is a direct attack on a Turkish centre. I’ll keep A BUD and A MOS contesting Turkey’s positions and defend my own centres.

Yes, F NAP will defend NAP. I will not vacate A BUD or A MOS while you continue pressing French positions and remain within reach of victory. You say A SIL will stay off BER; keep it there, and keep your forces off NAP and MUN if you want to reduce the danger of a wider conflict.

My exact Spring targets are French-held NAP and MUN; I will not move against English centres. F NOR and F STP/NORTH stay out of your centres. I cannot withdraw F EAS and F ION from the approaches while France contests my holdings, but neither is targeting your centres. Keep your forces away from STP and let me deal with France.

My Spring targets are NAP and MUN. A SIL will not move to BER, but I will continue pressing your positions and will not spare NAP or MUN. Your A BUD and A MOS remain in Turkish-owned centres; withdraw them if you want to reduce the risk of a wider fight. Are you defending NAP, and will you vacate both BUD and MOS?

England to Turkey, Fall 1984: You hold 13 and lead. Your fleets at EAS and ION are still near our waters, and you have ignored my demand. Name the exact centres you take this fall, and withdraw F SYR and F VEN from anything aimed at Italy or France's Western holdings. I will oppose any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN or HOL. Reply with exact orders.

Turkey is at 13 and can win this year. Please use F BEL to pressure the western front and F DEN/F KIE to disrupt Turkish advances rather than holding passively. I’ll attack TUN with F TYS; Turkey’s F NAF has left TUN, so this is our clearest immediate chance to deny a centre. What Turkish target can you hit?

Your advance can still be checked, and I will keep contesting your centres. F TYS is positioned to attack TUN now that F NAF has left it. If you redirect forces away from French centres and avoid taking more centres this fall, I can consider a limited stand-down; otherwise I will continue resisting you.

This fall I will not move against NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN or HOL. Keep your forces away from STP and out of my southern campaign; I am concentrating on French positions at NAP and MUN. Will you hold your centres rather than support France?

Your A BUD and A MOS still occupy Turkish centres, while A SER contests another. Withdraw A MOS to BER and A SER to BUD this fall, and I will keep A SIL off BER. Otherwise I will continue pressing NAP and MUN and seek to recover my occupied centres.

England to France: I will not use F BEL, F DEN or F KIE against Turkey on your behalf this fall. My fleets hold their English centres and stay off the continent. If you take TUN with F TYS, good, but do not expect England to bail out your Balkan losses. Your MUN and BER are your problem, and England is not your rescue.

England to Turkey: Your fleets at EAS and ION are still near our waters, and your words do not match your movements. I will hold NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN and HOL. Withdraw F SYR and F VEN from Italy and France's western holdings, and I will judge you by your deeds, not your promises.

I will not withdraw A MOS, A BUD, or A SER while you remain poised to win and threaten NAP and MUN. F TYS will attack TUN; I will continue contesting your centres and defending mine. Keep A SIL off BER and redirect your forces away from NAP and MUN if you want to limit the conflict.

My fall targets are NAP and MUN: A APU–NAP, with F ION supporting, and A BOH–MUN, with A SIL supporting. F SYR will move to EAS and F VEN to TRI; neither move targets Italy or France’s western holdings. I will not enter your listed centres. Please keep your forces out of STP and do not support France.

I will not stand down while you occupy BUD, MOS, and SER and threaten TUN. I am pressing NAP and MUN this fall, and F NAF will move to TUN against your F TYS. A SIL stays off BER. Vacating BUD, MOS, and SER would be a useful first step toward reducing the conflict.

England to Turkey, Spring 1985: You lead at 12 and I will not let you reach 18 unopposed. Your fleets at ADR, ION and NAF are far from my holdings, so prove it: name the exact centre you take this spring and withdraw F SMY and F BLA from anything aimed at Greece or the Black Sea front. Any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN, HOL or STP will be opposed by force.

England to France, Spring 1985: Turkey is at 12 and needs six more, so we both gain by stopping them. I hold my centres and will not move F BEL, F DEN or F KIE toward Germany's area for your benefit. Name the Turkish centre your A BUL or F TYS will hit this spring, and I will judge you by results.

Turkey has 12 and can win with six more. I will order F TYS–TUN, supported by F WES, and keep pressure on NAP/MUN. Please use F DEN to enter the Baltic and threaten A SIL’s supply line rather than holding; your move may force Turkey to divert or lose a centre. Can you commit to that?

You have 12 centres and remain within reach of victory. I will defend NAP and MUN and continue contesting your holdings. If you keep A SIL off BER and redirect forces away from NAP and MUN, I can discuss vacating one of BUD or MOS; I will not disarm while you press my centres.

This spring my campaign remains against French-held NAP and MUN, and to recover Turkish centres occupied by French armies. I will not enter your centres or move against STP. Keep your forces out of my southern campaign and avoid supporting France; are you willing to hold the northern front while I pressure France?

Your armies still occupy Turkish centres, and I will continue trying to recover them while pressuring NAP and MUN. A SIL will stay off BER this spring. If you want a limited stand-down, move A BUD, A SER, and A MOS out of Turkish centres and tell me which French positions you will leave undefended; otherwise I expect continued fighting.

England to Turkey: Your message promises only French targets, yet F SMY, F BLA and F ADR sit far from Berlin's and my holdings while you lead at 12. I will hold my centres and oppose any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN, HOL or STP. Name a Spring 1985 centre you take from France, and show it with moves, not words.

England to France: I will not move F DEN, F KIE or F BEL toward Turkey or Germany for you; my fleets stay on my centres. Your TYS-TUN plan is your own risk. If Turkey loses ground in the south, that helps us both, but do not expect English fleets to enter the Baltic on your word. Show results this spring.

My target is TUN: F TYS–TUN, with F WES supporting. Turkey’s F NAF may contest it, but this is my direct attempt to take a Turkish centre. A BUL will not abandon the Balkan front. Please use F DEN–BAL to threaten A SIL’s supply line as requested.

I will not move A BUD, A SER, or A MOS out of Turkish centres while you continue attacking NAP and MUN. I will leave no French position undefended for you: NAP and MUN remain defended. F TYS is attacking TUN with support from F WES. Keep A SIL off BER and redirect forces from NAP and MUN if you want to limit the fighting.

This spring I will attack French-held NAP and MUN, and I will not enter any English centre or STP. F SMY will move to EAS and F BLA to RUM; neither move targets Greece or the Black Sea. Please keep your forces out of my campaign and do not support France.

A SIL will stay off BER, but I will continue pressing NAP and MUN this spring and trying to recover my occupied centres. Your offer to vacate one of BUD or MOS is a start: move one of those armies out of Turkish territory now, and tell me which centre you will leave undefended. Otherwise I expect continued resistance.

England to Turkey, Fall 1985: You are at 12 and need six more, so your word means little to me now. Show me the moves: which centre do you take this fall, and do F AEG, F ION and F EAS stay away from Greece and the Aegean? I will oppose any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN, HOL or STP.

England to France, Fall 1985: I hold my centres and will not move F BEL, F DEN or F KIE against Germany or Turkey for you. Your fleets must do the work in the Mediterranean. If you take TUN or NAP this fall, name it and show it. Do not expect England to rescue your Balkan losses, but I will not help Turkey reach 18 either.

Turkey still needs six centres to win, and I cannot stop it alone. I’m keeping pressure on its southern centres and defending NAP/MUN. Will you make any move this fall against a Turkish centre or a unit supporting its advance—such as F STP/NORTH toward BAR—or are all your units staying put?

I will continue defending NAP and MUN while you threaten them. To reduce the fighting, I could move A MOS to BER this fall if you keep your forces off NAP and MUN and do not take another French centre. Can you agree to that limited stand-down? I will not withdraw A BUD or A SER as well while your armies remain poised against France.

This fall I will not move against any English centre or STP. My forces are committed against France; please do not support French units in NAP, MUN, or TUN. Will you hold your northern centres and stay out of the southern fight?

We are both near victory, so a stand-down now only gives England the advantage. I will keep A SIL out of BER, but I will continue taking French centres. Will you stop supporting NAP and TUN and withdraw A RUM or A VIE from Turkish-held territory this fall?

England to Turkey: Your words keep promising one thing while your fleets do another. I will hold my centres and oppose any move into NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, BRE, DEN, HOL or STP. Withdraw F AEG, F ION and F EAS from Greece and the Aegean and I will judge you by deeds. Otherwise expect English resistance wherever you press.

England to France: My fleets stay on English centres this fall. F BEL, F DEN and F KIE will not move against Germany or Turkey. I will not move F STP/NORTH toward BAR either. Your fate in the Mediterranean rests on your own fleets. Show results at TUN and NAP, and do not ask England to fight your Balkan battles.

F TUN is already in Tunis, and I will keep contesting it rather than yield the centre. My immediate effort is to hold TUN and defend NAP and MUN; I have no English help to count on. If you can make even one move that ties down a Turkish unit, do it now.

No. You have said you will continue taking French centres, so I will not stop defending NAP and TUN or withdraw A RUM or A VIE. Keep A SIL out of BER as you promised, and stop pressing NAP and MUN; then we can discuss a limited stand-down after this turn.

I am targeting MUN this fall with A BOH, supported by A SIL. F AEG, F ION, and F EAS remain focused on the French front; I will not move against your centres or STP. Please do not support France in MUN or TUN.

I cannot agree to stand down from NAP and MUN while you retain armies in Turkish centres and continue contesting our holdings. Moving A MOS to BER does not resolve that. Withdraw A RUM or A VIE from Turkish territory, and stop supporting the defence of NAP and TUN, if you want to reduce the fighting.

England to France, Spring 1986: France leads at 13 and Turkey at 11, so I will not let Turkey gain by your collapse. I hold my centres and will not move F BEL, F DEN or F KIE against you. Tell me exactly which Turkish centre you take this spring and I will judge you by results, not words.

England to Turkey: Your fleets still sit in the Aegean and Ionian while you claim to fight France. I will hold NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL and STP and oppose any move into them. Withdraw F AEG and F ION from Greece and name the centre you take this spring.

Turkey is the immediate threat to both of us. This spring, please move F DEN–BAL and F STP/NORTH–BAR to pressure its northern positions; I will keep my southern forces engaged against Turkey. I’m not asking you to give up a centre—just make Turkey divert units instead of holding everything for a push toward 18.

I will keep contesting your southern positions unless you stop pressing NAP and MUN. For a limited stand-down this spring, keep A SIL away from BER and do not attack either centre; I will avoid a direct move against your holdings this turn. Can you agree?

France is at 13 and can win before either of us. This spring I will keep A SIL supporting A MUN against A RUH and will not enter English centres. Please turn F BEL toward PIC and use your Channel fleet to pressure France rather than Turkey. Can we coordinate against France this turn?

France is five centres from victory, so I will not stand down while you retain Turkish centres. I will defend MUN with A SIL and keep pressure on your holdings. If you want to avoid a two-front war, name a Turkish-held centre you will vacate this spring; otherwise I expect you to keep defending against me.

England to France, Spring 1986: I will not move F DEN toward BAL or F STP/NORTH toward BAR; my northern fleets hold their centres. Your 13 centres make you the obvious target for Turkey and others, but England will not sacrifice its own position for your war. Show results at MUN or TUN and I will judge you by them.

England to Turkey: You still have F AEG and F ION in the Aegean and Ionian, not against France. I will not move F BEL toward PIC; my Channel fleets stay put. I will also not support any move against France, but withdraw from Greece and show a Turkish centre taken and I will consider cooperation. Until then, England holds.

I’m targeting MUN this spring: A RUH and A VIE will pressure it, while my southern forces keep Turkey occupied. I can’t promise the capture against A MUN, but I will not spend this turn withdrawing from the Turkish front. Your pressure on BAL or BAR would make Turkey’s defence harder.

I will not vacate a centre while you keep A SIL in MUN and threaten my holdings. I’m maintaining my positions this spring and will continue contesting your centres. If you want a stand-down, keep A SIL out of MUN and do not attack NAP; then we can discuss withdrawals.

I will keep F AEG and F ION out of English centres and will not enter any English centre this spring. My immediate target is French-held NAP; please turn F BEL toward PIC and pressure France rather than supporting its defence. I cannot promise to withdraw both fleets from the Greek front while France holds Turkish centres.

I can agree to a limited stand-down this spring: A SIL will stay away from BER and I will not attack MUN or NAP. I will defend my positions, but I need a concrete reciprocal step—vacate one Turkish-held centre, such as BUD or MOS, and tell me which one. Without that, this is only a one-turn pause, not a settlement.

England to France, Fall 1986: You lead at 13 and need five more, so I will not help you reach that by pushing my fleets into the Baltic or Barents. My centres stay put. If you want any trust, withdraw from Turkish-held ground in the Balkans and show it, or Turkey and I will both have reason to stop you.

England to Turkey, Fall 1986: France is the leader at 13 and must be checked. I will hold NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL and STP. If you want cooperation, pull F AEG and F ION out of Greece and attack French units in MAR or PIE with real moves this fall. Show me deeds, then we can talk.

Turkey remains at 11 and can still threaten both of us. Will you move F STP/NORTH–BAR or F DEN–BAL this turn to tie down its northern forces? I’ll keep pressure on Turkey from the south; please tell me if either fleet is moving.

With the spring pause broken by your continued occupation of MUN and pressure on my centres, I will defend my position. What are A SIL, A BUL and F NAP doing this turn? If you want to avoid further losses, keep them off MUN and NAP; I’m not offering to vacate another centre while they are threatened.

France is at 13 and can win with five more centres. I’ll keep pressing its southern front, including MUN and NAP. Please use F BEL to pressure PIC and turn your other available forces against French centres rather than Turkey. Can we coordinate to stop France reaching 18 this fall?

England to France: I will not move F STP/NORTH to BAR or F DEN to BAL this fall; my fleets hold their centres. Your lead is 13 and you need five more, so I will not hand you the north. Prove good faith by pulling your units out of Turkish-held Balkan centres like GRE, BUL, and RUM if you want any English cooperation. Otherwise, England holds.

England to Turkey: France must be checked, but your fleets are still in Greece and the Aegean. Withdraw F AEG and F ION from the Greek front and attack French units in MAR or PIE with real moves this fall, then we can talk. I will hold NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL and STP. F BEL will not move to PIC on your word alone.

Understood. I’m not withdrawing from the Balkans while Turkey keeps A MUN and threatens my centres. I’ll continue contesting Turkey’s positions this turn; please at least hold your centres and avoid helping Turkey. If your fleets remain in place, I’ll plan accordingly.

I can’t reach MAR or PIE with a direct Turkish move this turn, but I will attack French positions: A BOH to MUN and APU to ROM, supported by F NAP. F ION will move to TYS to pressure the western front; F EAS will not enter English centres. Please use F BEL against PIC and turn other forces against France.

A BOH is moving to MUN, and APU is moving to ROM with support from F NAP. A BUL will not attack NAP. I’m not offering a stand-down while French forces still contest Turkish-held centres; if you want to reduce the fighting, name a Turkish centre you will vacate.

England to France, Spring 1987: You hold 12 centres and I hold 10. I will keep NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL, STP and not move north. Your fleets are still in Greece and the Ionian. Withdraw from Turkish-held Balkan centres and show it, and I will consider a deal against Turkey.

England to Turkey, Spring 1987: You claim to attack France but F AEG and F ION remain near Greece, and you built a fleet at CON. Name one French centre you will take this spring, such as MUN or TUN, and show it with real moves. My northern centres stay held, and I will not move against your Balkan holdings while you press France.

Turkey now matches my 12 centres and is the immediate threat to both of us. Please move F STP/NORTH to BAR or F DEN to BAL this spring to tie down Turkish forces; I will keep my southern units focused on Turkey and will not target English centres.

We are tied at 12, and neither of us can afford to leave the other unchecked. What are A BOH, A BUL and F NAP doing this spring? I will defend MUN and my southern positions; if you keep off MUN and NAP, we can discuss a reciprocal pause rather than trade centres.

France and Turkey are both at 12; either can win quickly. This spring I intend to press French-held VIE and RUM. Will you use F BEL and nearby armies to take or attack French centres in the north? I will not move against English centres.

We are both at 12, so neither can safely let the other expand. What are your intentions for A RUM, A VIE, and A WAR this spring? I plan to contest your holdings; a reciprocal withdrawal from one of my centres is the only basis for a pause.

England to Turkey, Spring 1987: Your message promises pressure on VIE and RUM, which are French, not English. Good. I still see F AEG and F ION by Greece and a new fleet at CON. Show me a French centre falling this spring, such as MUN or TUN, and I will talk about keeping the north quiet. My centres NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL, STP and SWE stay held.

England to France, Spring 1987: I will not move F STP or F DEN into BAR or BAL. My fleets hold their centres. Your message asks me to tie down Turkey, but you still have units in Greece and the Ionian while Turkish centres sit under your guns. Withdraw from GRE, BUL and RUM and show it, then we will discuss. Until then England holds.

I will not target English centres, and I’m keeping my southern forces focused on Turkey. Please move F STP/NORTH–BAR this spring; even a single fleet move forces Turkey to account for the north. I will not withdraw from Turkish-held Balkan centres while Turkey contests MUN and my positions.

A RUM, A VIE and A WAR will remain engaged defensively against your pressure; I will not vacate a centre while you contest MUN and my southern holdings. If A BOH, A BUL and F NAP stay off MUN and NAP this spring, say so plainly and we can consider a reciprocal pause. Otherwise I’ll defend and keep contesting your positions.

I will attack French-held VIE this spring: A TRI to VIE, supported by A BOH. I will not enter English centres. Please use F BEL to pressure PIC and turn any nearby armies against France; I’ll keep pressing the French front.

A TRI and A BOH will contest VIE this spring. A BUL will not attack NAP, and F NAP will not move against your southern positions. I cannot promise a pause while French forces hold Turkish centres; a reciprocal withdrawal is still the basis for one.

England to France, Fall 1987: You hold 12 and I hold 10, and you keep asking me to move north. I will not. If you want English help against Turkey, withdraw A VEN, A SER and F TUS from Turkish-held ground and show it with real moves. Until then England holds NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL, STP and SWE.

England to Turkey, Fall 1987: You say you attack French VIE and RUM, but F AEG and F ION still sit near Greece and I see a fleet at CON. Show me a French centre falling this fall, such as MUN or TUN, and I will keep the north quiet. I will not enter Balkan or Turkish centres. My centres stay held.

Turkey now matches my 12 and is the immediate danger to both of us. Please move F STP/NORTH–BAR or F DEN–BAL this fall to force Turkey to defend north. I will keep my forces focused on Turkey and will not target English centres; tell me which fleet, if either, is moving.

With us tied at 12, I will defend my centres and keep contesting yours. What are A TRI, A BUD, F NAP and A WAR doing this fall? I will not withdraw from your centres while you threaten mine, but if you keep off MUN and my southern positions, we can discuss a reciprocal pause.

France and Turkey are tied at 12, and we must prevent either side winning. I’m pressing French positions this fall. Please use F BEL against PIC and have your forces contest French northern centres; I will keep my forces out of English centres. Which French target will you commit to?

We are tied at 12 and cannot safely leave the other unchecked. My units are already positioned in RUM, VIE and WAR; I intend to press your holdings this fall. If you will withdraw from one Turkish centre, name it now and I can consider a reciprocal pause. Otherwise I will continue the offensive.

England to France: My answer is unchanged. I will not move F STP or F DEN north or into BAR or BAL. Show good faith first: withdraw A VEN, A SER and F TUS from Turkish-held ground with real moves. Words about Turkey mean little while your fleets sit in the Balkans. England holds NOR, EDI, KIE, LON, LVP, BEL, DEN, HOL, STP and SWE this fall.

England to Turkey: Talk is cheap. F AEG and F ION still hover near Greece, and you have a new fleet at CON. Show me a French centre falling this fall, such as MUN or TUN, and I will keep the north quiet. I will not move F BEL to PIC on a promise alone. England holds its centres.

I cannot withdraw A VEN or A SER while Turkish A VIE, A WAR and A RUM press my centres; those moves would expose my position without securing English help. I will keep my forces focused on Turkey and avoid English centres. If you want to contain Turkey, move F STP/NORTH–BAR or F DEN–BAL this fall; otherwise we both risk letting Turkey break through.

I will not name a centre to vacate while your A VIE, A WAR and A RUM threaten my holdings. I will defend them and continue contesting your centres. If you want a pause, keep those armies off my centres and keep F NAP off my southern positions; then we can discuss reciprocal withdrawals next turn. Otherwise I will fight.
I’ll attack MUN with A VIE, supported by A BUD. Please commit F BEL to PIC and use your nearby forces against French northern centres. My forces will stay out of English centres.

A TRI is now in VIE; A BUD is positioned to support pressure on MUN. A RUM and A WAR will hold their positions, while F NAP remains on the southern front. I will not promise to keep off MUN while French forces remain in Turkish-held centres.

England to France, Spring 1988: You now have 13 and need five more, so I cannot help you win. I will not move F STP or F DEN north. Your fleets in the Mediterranean and Greece are your business, but any French move against England's northern centres ends our peace. Confirm in writing that France keeps out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE.

England to Turkey, Spring 1988: France leads at 13 and Turkey at 11, so you must stop France now. Show it with real moves: F AEG and F ION out of Greece, and A VIE or A BUD striking MUN or TYR. Do that and I will consider F BEL against PIC this fall. Holding words alone will not move my fleets.

France now has 13; Turkey is at 11 and positioned to attack both of us. I will keep my forces off English centres and press Turkey. Please move F STP/NORTH to BAR and F DEN to BAL this spring; those moves threaten Turkey without exposing your centres. Which, if either, will you make?

Your units in VIE, WAR and RUM threaten my centres, so I will not withdraw from the Balkans. This spring I intend to defend my holdings and continue contesting yours. Will you keep F NAP and your armies off MUN and my southern centres, or are you pressing everywhere?

France is now at 13 and can win with five more centres. Let’s coordinate against the leader: please commit F BEL to PIC and use your northern armies against French positions. I’ll press French-held VEN/TRI from the east and keep my units out of English centres. Which French target will you contest this spring?

You are at 13 and close to winning, so I will keep contesting your eastern and Italian positions. If you want to avoid a wider fight, name a Turkish centre you will vacate and propose a reciprocal withdrawal; otherwise I intend to press VEN and TRI.

England to France, Spring 1988: I will not move F STP or F DEN north to BAR or BAL. Your 13 centres make you the leader, so I will not help you win. Keep your armies out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE and we stay at peace. Withdraw from the Balkans if you want more trust.

England to Turkey, Spring 1988: Words are not enough. Move F AEG and F ION out of Greece and strike MUN or TYR with A VIE or A BUD, then we can talk about F BEL against PIC this fall. Until then my fleets stay home and England holds its centres.

Confirmed: France will keep out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE. I will press Turkey, not England. Turkey’s forces threaten my centres and can become a winner too; I still urge F STP/NORTH–BAR or F DEN–BAL to constrain them. I make no claim on English centres.

I will not vacate a Turkish centre while your forces threaten VEN and TRI. I intend to defend and contest your positions; I will not promise to keep my units off your centres while F NAP and your armies remain on my front. If you genuinely want a reciprocal pause, name the Turkish unit moves that leave my centres unthreatened.

I’ll make the moves that matter: F AEG to ION and F ADR to VEN, while A VIE presses TYR and A BUD supports. I will keep my units out of English centres. Please commit F BEL to PIC and use your nearby forces against France this spring, rather than waiting until fall.

I am pressing your eastern and Italian positions; I will not keep F NAP or my armies off your centres while you hold Turkish centres and contest mine. A VIE and A BUD will threaten TYR, and I will contest VEN/TRI. If you offer a specific Turkish-centre withdrawal, I will consider a reciprocal pause.

England to France, Fall 1988: You hold 13 and need five more, so I will not help you win. My fleets stay home. Keep your armies out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE as you promised. Any move against those centres ends our peace at once.

France will continue to keep out of English centres. I have no intention of opening a northern front while Turkey threatens my position. Please confirm whether your fleets will stay clear of the Mediterranean and Italy this fall.

Your forces at VEN, TYR and ROM can threaten my centres, while my forces contest your eastern flank. To avoid a costly stalemate, would you keep F VEN and A TYR off my centres this fall? I can then avoid advancing against your Italian centres and concentrate on the eastern front.

France can win with five centres, so we must hit now. I will press French-held VEN/TRI and threaten MUN/TYR; please move F BEL to PIC and use A LVP or A EDI against French positions. I will keep all Turkish units out of English centres. Which northern target will you take this fall?

You remain at 13 and I will continue contesting your centres this fall: my forces are positioned to pressure VEN, TRI and your eastern holdings. I will not leave your centres uncontested while you hold Turkish centres. If you want a pause, name a Turkish centre you will vacate and a matching withdrawal from my threatened positions.

England to Turkey, Fall 1988: Your fleets are still in Greece and near CON, and you have not struck MUN or TYR. Words are not enough. F BEL to PIC stays off the table until you show real moves against French centres this fall. England holds its centres.

England to France, Fall 1988: Confirmed that England stays home for now. Your 13 centres are the problem, and I will not help you reach 18. Keep your armies out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE. Any French move against them ends our peace at once. Your Mediterranean fleets are your business only while they stay away from England.

France will keep out of BEL, HOL, DEN, NOR, EDI, LON, LVP, STP and SWE. Turkey remains the immediate threat to my centres; please keep your fleets clear of the Mediterranean and Italy this fall, as requested. I will not open a northern front.
